words.en: To penetrate means to enter or pass through something, especially when this is difficult or when it is not obvious how to do it.

words.ex: He affirm that the plan will work.
words.ex_cn: 他断言这个计划会成功。
words.en: If you affirm that something is true or that something exists, you state firmly and publicly that it is true or that it exists.

words.ex: He reaffirmed his commitment to the team.
words.ex_cn: 他重申了对团队的承诺。
words.en: If you reaffirm something, you state it again clearly and firmly.

words.ex: He kept his dignity even when he was poor.
words.ex_cn: 即使他很穷，他依然保持尊严。
words.en: Dignity is the quality of being worthy of honor or respect.

words.ex: The dignitary gave a speech at the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 这位显要人物在仪式上发表了演讲。
words.en: A dignitary is a person who has an important position in a society or an organization.

words.ex: The charity helps poor children get food and education.
words.ex_cn: 这个慈善团体帮助贫困儿童获得食物和教育。
words.en: An organization that helps people in need, or the act of giving money, food, or help to those who need it.

words.ex: The old painting was sold at an auction.
words.ex_cn: 那幅旧画在拍卖会上被卖出了。
words.en: An auction is a public sale where goods or property are sold to the highest bidder.

words.tr:
n. 保护区；储备；保留；
v. 预订；
words.ex: The wildlife reserve is home to many endangered animals.
words.ex_cn: 这个自然保护区是许多濒危动物的家园。
words.en: If you reserve something such as a table, ticket, or magazine, you arrange for it to be kept for you and not given to anyone else.

words.ex: The difference between the two colors is subtle.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色之间的区别很微妙。
words.en: Something that is subtle is not immediately obvious or noticeable, but is rather indirect or understated.

words.ex: The subtlety of her smile made everyone curious.
words.ex_cn: 她微笑的微妙之处让所有人都感到好奇。
words.en: The quality of being subtle, especially in a way that is difficult to notice or understand.

words.ex: The long meeting was tedious.
words.ex_cn: 这场漫长的会议很沉闷。
words.en: If you describe something such as a job, task, or situation as tedious, you mean it is boring and rather frustrating.

words.tr:
n. 媒介；方法；
adj. 中等的；适中的；
words.ex: TV is a popular medium for advertising.
words.ex_cn: 电视是一种流行的广告媒介。
words.en: A medium is a method or way of expressing something.

words.tr:
v. 耗尽；用完；使筋疲力尽
n. 排气管；废气
words.ex: The long hike exhausted him.
words.ex_cn: 这次漫长的徒步旅行让他筋疲力尽。
words.en: If something exhausts you, it makes you so tired, either physically or mentally, that you have no energy left.

words.tr: adj. 用不完的；无穷无尽的；
words.ex: The sun provides an inexhaustible source of energy.
words.ex_cn: 太阳提供一种用不完的能量来源。
words.en: If you describe something as inexhaustible, you are emphasizing that there is a very large quantity of it and that it is not likely to be used up or to run out.

words.tr:
n. 流体；流质；
adj. 流动的；
words.ex: Water is a common fluid.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种常见的流体。
words.en: A fluid is a substance that can flow and change its shape easily, such as a liquid or a gas.

words.ex: The extra words are superfluous.
words.ex_cn: 这些额外的词是多余的。
words.en: Something that is superfluous is unnecessary or no longer needed.

words.ex: Birds migrate south in winter.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类在冬天迁徙到南方。
words.en: If people migrate, they move from one place to another, especially in order to find work or to live somewhere for a short time.

words.ex: The migrant found a new job in the city.
words.ex_cn: 这位移居者在城市里找到了一份新工作。
words.en: A migrant is a person who moves from one place to another, especially in order to find work.

words.ex: He speaks English with a French accent.
words.ex_cn: 他说英语时带有法国口音。
words.en: An accent is a distinctive way of pronouncing a language, especially one associated with a particular country, area, or social class.

words.ex: She accentuates the first syllable when she says the word.
words.ex_cn: 她说这个词时重读第一个音节。
words.en: To accentuate something means to emphasize it or make it more noticeable.

chapters.name: Part II 专八最常考词汇 Lesson 6

words.ex: He sat with good posture at the desk.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在书桌前，姿势端正。
words.en: Your posture is the way in which you hold your body when you are standing or sitting.

words.ex: He changed his stance on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他改变了对气候变化的立场。
words.en: A stance is a particular way of standing, especially in sports such as golf or baseball, or a person's attitude or opinion about something, especially when it is stated publicly.

words.ex: He embeds the photo in the document.
words.ex_cn: 他把照片插入到文档中。
words.en: To fix something firmly and deeply in a surrounding mass.

words.tr:
v. 盖印；印刻；使铭记
n. 盖印；痕迹
words.ex: He used a stamp to imprint his name on the box.
words.ex_cn: 他用印章在盒子上盖印了他的名字。
words.en: To imprint something means to mark or stamp it with a design or a symbol. It can also mean to fix something firmly in someone's mind.

words.ex: The teacher tried to infuse confidence into the students.
words.ex_cn: 老师试图向学生注入信心。
words.en: If you infuse a quality into someone or something, you fill them with it. If a quality infuses something, it is present throughout it.

words.tr:
v. 投入；跳入
n. 跳进；骤降
words.ex: He plunged into the cold water.
words.ex_cn: 他跳进了冰冷的水里。
words.en: If something or someone plunges in a particular direction, especially into water, they fall, rush, or throw themselves in that direction.

words.tr: adj. 完全的；荒凉的；光秃秃的；僵硬的；严厉的
words.ex: There was a stark difference between the two results.
words.ex_cn: 这两个结果之间有完全的差异。
words.en: Stark means complete, severe, or obvious in a way that is impossible to avoid noticing.

words.tr: adj. 可理解的；明白易懂的；清楚的
words.ex: His explanation was intelligible to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的解释人人都能听懂。
words.en: Capable of being understood; comprehensible.

words.ex: His speech was coherent and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲连贯且易于理解。
words.en: If something is coherent, it is well planned, so that it is clear and sensible and all its parts go well with each other.

words.tr: v. 扫；“sweep”的现在分词； adj. 全面的；
words.ex: He sweeping the floor every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上扫地。
words.en: If you describe something as sweeping, you mean it is very extensive or has a very wide effect.

words.ex: The police told everyone to evacuate the building.
words.ex_cn: 警察让所有人撤离大楼。
words.en: To evacuate means to remove people from a place of danger to a safer place.

words.ex: He turned his head to avert the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他转过头去避免了事故。
words.en: If you avert something unpleasant, you prevent it from happening.

words.ex: He shuns loud parties because he is shy.
words.ex_cn: 他因为害羞而避开热闹的派对。
words.en: If you shun someone or something, you deliberately avoid them or keep away from them.

words.tr:
n. 旁路；
v. 绕过；
words.ex: The city built a bypass around the old town.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市建了一条绕过老城区的旁路。
words.en: If you bypass a place or a system, you avoid it or go around it instead of going through it.

words.tr: v. 绕行；设法避开；智胜；围住
words.ex: He circumvented the traffic by taking a small road.
words.ex_cn: 他通过走一条小路绕过了交通拥堵。
words.en: If someone circumvents a rule or restriction, they avoid having to obey it, usually in a clever and dishonest way.

words.tr:
n. 蜂拥；狂奔；大西部赛马会（美国西部或加拿大）
v. 惊跑；蜂拥
words.ex: The cows ran in a stampede when they heard the loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 当牛群听到巨大的噪音时，它们惊慌狂奔。
words.en: A stampede is a situation in which a group of people or animals suddenly start running in a wild and uncontrolled way, often because they are frightened.

words.ex: The heat was inescapable in the small room.
words.ex_cn: 小房间里热得无法逃避。
words.en: If you describe a fact, situation, or activity as inescapable, you mean that it is difficult not to notice it or be affected by it.

words.ex: The city needs better infrastructure for roads and water.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市需要更好的道路和供水设施。
words.en: The basic physical and organizational structures and facilities (e.g., buildings, roads, power supplies) needed for the operation of a society or enterprise.

words.tr: v. 构成…的基础（或起因）
words.ex: Poor diet underlies many health problems.
words.ex_cn: 不良饮食是许多健康问题的根源。
words.en: If something underlies a situation or activity, it is the cause or basis of it.

words.ex: Smartphones supplanted landline phones.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机取代了固定电话。
words.en: To supplant someone or something means to take the place of them, often by being more powerful or effective.

words.ex: He tries not to demean his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他尽量不贬低他的同学。
words.en: To demean someone or something means to cause them to lose their dignity or respect.

words.ex: Many people decry the use of plastic bags.
words.ex_cn: 许多人公开反对使用塑料袋。
words.en: If you decry something, you criticize it as being wrong or harmful.

words.ex: They exalt their hero with cheers.
words.ex_cn: 他们用欢呼赞美他们的英雄。
words.en: To exalt someone or something means to praise them very highly.

words.ex: He is adept at solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长解决数学问题。
words.en: Someone who is adept at something is very skilled at it.

words.ex: The cat is agile and jumps high.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫很敏捷，跳得很高。
words.en: Someone who is agile can move quickly and easily.

words.ex: He gave an artful answer to the tricky question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个棘手的问题给出了一个巧妙的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as artful, you mean that they are clever and skillful at achieving what they want, especially by deceiving people.

words.ex: The surgeon's dexterity saved the patient's life.
words.ex_cn: 外科医生的灵巧救了病人的命。
words.en: Skill and grace in physical movement, especially in the use of the hands; adroitness.

words.ex: The artisan makes handmade pottery.
words.ex_cn: 这位工匠制作手工陶器。
words.en: An artisan is someone who makes things by hand, especially using traditional methods.

words.tr: n. 实际知识；技术；窍门
words.ex: He has the know-how to fix the machine.
words.ex_cn: 他有修理这台机器的诀窍。
words.en: Practical knowledge or expertise in a particular field or area.

words.ex: He is a novice at playing the guitar.
words.ex_cn: 他是个吉他新手。
words.en: A novice is someone who has just started learning or doing something and does not have much experience.

words.tr: adj. 不适当的；无能的；笨拙的
words.ex: His inept reply made the situation worse.
words.ex_cn: 他不适当的回答让情况变得更糟。
words.en: If you say that someone is inept, you are criticizing them because they do something with a complete lack of skill.

words.ex: This temperature is the optimum for growing plants.
words.ex_cn: 这个温度是最适宜植物生长的。
words.en: The optimum is the best or most favorable condition, degree, amount, etc., for achieving a particular result.

words.tr: adj. 有资格的；合格的；合意的；
words.ex: He is eligible to vote because he is 18 years old.
words.ex_cn: 他年满18岁，有资格投票。
words.en: Someone who is eligible for something is qualified or allowed to do it.

words.tr:
n. 提倡者；
v. 提倡；
words.ex: He is an advocate for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁用水的提倡者。
words.en: If you advocate a particular action or plan, you recommend it publicly.

words.tr: n. 支持者；拥护者；辩护者
words.ex: He is a proponent of clean energy.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁能源的支持者。
words.en: A proponent of an idea or course of action is someone who supports it and tries to persuade other people to support it.

words.tr: n. 阐述者；拥护者；代表者；指数
words.ex: He is the exponent of modern education reform.
words.ex_cn: 他是现代教育改革的阐述者。
words.en: An exponent is someone who supports and explains a particular idea, theory, or system, or a symbol that shows how many times a number is to be multiplied by itself.

words.ex: His countenance showed surprise.
words.ex_cn: 他的面容流露出惊讶。
words.en: A person's face or facial expression; support or approval.

words.tr:
adj. 偏袒的；党派性的
n. 强烈支持者；党羽；游击队员
words.ex: He gave a partisan answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了偏袒的回答。
words.en: A partisan is a strong supporter of a party, cause, or person. It can also refer to a member of an armed group formed to fight secretly against an occupying force.

words.ex: He believes in an egalitarian society where everyone is equal.
words.ex_cn: 他相信一个人人平等的平等主义社会。
words.en: Egalitarian is used to describe something that is based on the principle that all people are equal and deserve equal rights and opportunities.

words.ex: The elite of the city often meet at private clubs.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的精英经常在私人俱乐部会面。
words.en: You can refer to the most powerful, rich, or talented people within a particular group, place, or society as the elite.

words.ex: He is the protagonist in the story.
words.ex_cn: 他是故事中的主角。
words.en: The main character in a story, play, film, etc., especially the one who is good or who the audience is expected to support.

words.ex: The king sent an emissary to talk to the neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 国王派了一名使者去与邻国交谈。
words.en: An emissary is a person who is sent on a special mission, usually as a diplomatic representative.

words.ex: He met a compatriot at the airport.
words.ex_cn: 他在机场遇到了一位同胞。
words.en: A compatriot is a person from your own country.

words.ex: He is the recipient of the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个奖项的接受者。
words.en: A recipient is a person who receives something.

words.ex: He is the namesake of his grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他是他祖父的同名者。
words.en: A namesake is a person or thing that has the same name as another person or thing.

words.ex: The temple is a divine place.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙是神的圣地。
words.en: Something that is divine relates to a god or goddess.

words.tr: v. 置入神龛中；入庙祀奉；奉为神圣；珍藏
words.ex: They enshrined the ancient statue in a golden shrine.
words.ex_cn: 他们把这尊古代雕像置入了一个金色神龛中。
words.en: If something such as a tradition or a right is enshrined in something such as a constitution or law, it is protected by it.

words.ex: He shows piety by praying every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天祈祷，表现出虔诚。
words.en: Piety is strong religious belief, or behaviour that is religious or morally correct.

words.ex: He can describe the picture in one sentence.
words.ex_cn: 他能用一句话描述这幅画。
words.en: If you describe a person, object, event, or situation, you say what they are like or what happened.

words.tr: v. 奉为神圣；贡献；奉献
words.ex: They consecrate the church with prayer and song.
words.ex_cn: 他们用祈祷和歌声将教堂奉为神圣。
words.en: To consecrate something means to officially declare it to be holy and to be used for religious purposes.

words.ex: He is a charismatic leader who inspires everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有魅力的领导者，能激励每个人。
words.en: A charismatic person attracts, influences, and inspires people by their personal qualities.

words.tr: adj. 最高的；至上的；最重要的；
words.ex: His safety is paramount.
words.ex_cn: 他的安全是最重要的。
words.en: Something that is paramount or of paramount importance is more important than anything else.

words.ex: The view from the mountain was stupendous.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色令人惊叹。
words.en: Something that is stupendous is extremely impressive or large.

words.ex: Her performance was phenomenal.
words.ex_cn: 她的表现非常非凡。
words.en: If you describe something as phenomenal, you think it is extremely good or impressive.

words.ex: He made a hypothesis that plants grow faster in light.
words.ex_cn: 他提出一个假设，认为植物在光照下长得更快。
words.en: A hypothesis is an idea which is suggested as a possible explanation for a particular situation or condition, but which has not yet been proved to be correct.

words.ex: You need basic math as a prerequisite for this course.
words.ex_cn: 你学习这门课程的前提是掌握基础数学。
words.en: A prerequisite is something that must exist or happen before something else can exist or happen.

words.ex: The mountain has great prominence in the landscape.
words.ex_cn: 这座山在景观中十分突出。
words.en: If someone or something is in a position of prominence, they are important or well-known.

words.tr: n. 高超的技艺；造诣；英勇；
words.ex: His prowess in basketball amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在篮球方面的高超技艺让所有人都惊叹。
words.en: Exceptional skill or ability in a particular field or activity.

words.ex: The movie was mediocre and not worth watching.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影很平庸，不值得看。
words.en: If you describe something as mediocre, you mean that it is of average quality but you think it should be better.

words.tr: adj. 外来的；外国来的；奇异的；
words.ex: The market sells exotic fruits from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个市场出售来自其他国家的外来水果。
words.en: Something that is exotic is unusual and interesting because it comes from or is related to a distant country.

words.ex: The indigenous people live in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 本土居民住在森林里。
words.en: Indigenous people or things belong to the country in which they are found, rather than coming there or being brought there from another country.

words.tr: adj. 奇怪的；奇数的；余的；
words.ex: He wore an odd hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶奇怪的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as odd, you mean that they are strange or unusual.

words.tr: adj. 离奇的；奇特的；奇怪的；
words.ex: The clown wore a bizarre hat with three eyes.
words.ex_cn: 小丑戴着一顶有三只眼睛的离奇帽子。
words.en: Something that is bizarre is very odd and strange.

words.ex: He wore a weird hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶怪异的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as weird, you mean that they are strange, unusual, or mysterious.

words.ex: He wore an outlandish hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶奇异的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as outlandish, you mean that it is very unusual, strange, or exaggerated.

words.tr: n. 奇事；巧合；怪癖；奇行
words.ex: His habit of talking to his plants is a strange quirk.
words.ex_cn: 他跟植物说话的习惯是一个奇怪的奇事。
words.en: A quirk is a peculiar habit or aspect of a person's character, or an unexpected twist in a situation or story.

words.ex: The two cultures are disparate in their traditions.
words.ex_cn: 这两种文化在传统上完全不同。
words.en: Things that are disparate are clearly different from each other in quality or type.

words.ex: There is a disparity in pay between men and women.
words.ex_cn: 男女之间的工资存在差异。
words.en: A disparity between two or more things is a noticeable difference between them.

words.ex: He flipped the pancake with a spatula.
words.ex_cn: 他用铲子快速翻转了煎饼。
words.en: To flip something means to turn it over quickly one or more times, or to make something do this.

words.tr: adj. 谨慎的；慎重的；精明的
words.ex: He is prudent with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他在花钱时很谨慎。
words.en: If you are prudent, you are careful and avoid taking unnecessary risks.

words.ex: He was wary of strangers who offered free gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些提供免费礼物的陌生人保持谨慎。
words.en: If you are wary of something or someone, you are cautious because you do not know much about them and you believe they may be dangerous or cause problems.

words.tr: v. 详细检查；仔细察看
words.ex: The teacher scrutinizes every student's homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师仔细检查每位学生的作业。
words.en: If you scrutinize something, you examine it very carefully, often to find out some information from it or about it.

words.tr: n. 清醒；镇定；严肃；节制
words.ex: He values sobriety after his accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后重视清醒。
words.en: The state of being sober, especially in terms of not being under the influence of alcohol.

words.ex: He gave a perfunctory nod and left.
words.ex_cn: 他敷衍地点了点头，然后离开了。
words.en: If you describe something that is done as perfunctory, you mean that it is done as a duty or a formality, without much care or interest.

words.ex: He made an impetuous decision to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他冲动地决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you describe someone as impetuous, you mean that they are likely to act quickly and suddenly without thinking or being careful.

words.tr: adj. 自负的；自命不凡的；浮华的
words.ex: He gave a pompous speech with big words.
words.ex_cn: 他用华丽的词藻做了一番自大的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as pompous, you mean that they behave or speak in a very serious way because they think they are more important than they really are.

words.tr: adj. 混杂的；什锦的；各样的
words.ex: He bought assorted candies at the store.
words.ex_cn: 他在商店买了各种各样的糖果。
words.en: Assorted means consisting of various kinds mixed together.

words.ex: The store offers an assortment of snacks.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店提供各种各样的零食。
words.en: An assortment is a group of similar things that are of different types or sizes.

words.ex: The colors intermingle in the painting.
words.ex_cn: 画中的颜色混合在一起。
words.en: If things intermingle, they mix together or are mixed together.

words.tr: n. 收容所；避难所；精神病院；（政治）庇护
words.ex: The old building now serves as an asylum for the homeless.
words.ex_cn: 这栋旧建筑现在是无家可归者的收容所。
words.en: An asylum is a place where people who are in danger or who have no homes can go for safety and protection.

chapters.name: Part II 专八最常考词汇 Lesson 7

words.ex: We bought spices at the local bazaar.
words.ex_cn: 我们在当地的集市上买了香料。
words.en: A bazaar is a market consisting of rows of shops or stalls, especially in the Middle East, or a sale of miscellaneous contributed articles to benefit some charity.

words.ex: He spends hours in cyberspace every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天在虚拟空间里花几个小时。
words.en: Cyberspace is the notional environment in which communication over computer networks occurs.

words.ex: The car has a futuristic design.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车具有未来派的设计。
words.en: If you describe something as futuristic, you mean that it is very modern and unusual in appearance, and often looks as if it comes from a time in the future.

words.tr: v. 追溯到；“date”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 过时的；陈旧的；
words.ex: This coin is dated to the year 1500.
words.ex_cn: 这枚硬币追溯到1500年。
words.en: Something that is dated is old-fashioned and no longer relevant or useful.

words.tr: adj. 卷角的（书等）；（书页）折角的
words.ex: He has a dog-eared book on his desk.
words.ex_cn: 他的书桌上有一本翻旧了的书。
words.en: Having pages that are worn or turned down from use, especially a book.

words.ex: Blue jeans are in vogue this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年牛仔裤很时髦。
words.en: If something is in vogue, it is very popular and fashionable.

words.tr: adj. 普遍的；流行的；盛行的；
words.ex: Smoking is prevalent in that country.
words.ex_cn: 在那个国家，吸烟很普遍。
words.en: If a condition, practice, or belief is prevalent, it is common or widespread.

words.tr:
n. 刻板印象；陈规老套
v. 对…存有成见；把…模式化
words.ex: He broke the stereotype that boys cannot cry.
words.ex_cn: 他打破了男孩不能哭的刻板印象。
words.en: A stereotype is a fixed general image or set of characteristics that a lot of people believe represent a particular type of person or thing.

words.tr: v. 制定法律；用立法规定
words.ex: The government will legislate new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将制定新规则。
words.en: To legislate means to make or enact laws.

words.tr: adj. 立法的；制定法律的；
words.ex: The legislative branch makes laws.
words.ex_cn: 立法部门制定法律。
words.en: Relating to the making of laws.

words.ex: He filed a lawsuit against the company.
words.ex_cn: 他向这家公司提起了诉讼。
words.en: A lawsuit is a case in a court of law which concerns a dispute between two people or organizations.

words.tr: v. 进行；继续；继续进行；“proceed”的现在分词；
words.ex: The meeting is proceeding as planned.
words.ex_cn: 会议按计划进行。
words.en: A proceeding is an event or a series of actions, especially one that is formal or official.

words.tr: n. 诉讼；（会议）记录；“proceeding”的复数；
words.ex: The proceedings took longer than expected.
words.ex_cn: 这场诉讼比预期的时间更长。
words.en: The proceedings are the series of events or actions that happen in a particular situation, especially in a legal case or a meeting.

words.ex: The plaintiff sued the company for damages.
words.ex_cn: 原告起诉该公司要求赔偿。
words.en: A plaintiff is a person who brings a case against another in a court of law.

words.ex: He made a plea for help.
words.ex_cn: 他恳求帮助。
words.en: A plea is a request or an appeal made in an urgent or emotional manner, or a statement made by someone in a court of law in which they say whether they are guilty of a crime or not.

words.ex: The judge will arbitrate the dispute between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 法官将调解这两个邻居之间的纠纷。
words.en: To arbitrate means to officially settle a dispute by making a decision that both sides accept.

words.tr: adj. 统治的；支配的； v. “rule”的现在分词；
words.ex: The ruling class controls the government.
words.ex_cn: 统治阶级控制着政府。
words.en: A ruling is an official decision made by a judge or court, or a decision made by someone in authority.

words.ex: The teacher will revoke his privilege to use the computer.
words.ex_cn: 老师将撤销他使用电脑的权限。
words.en: If someone in authority revokes something such as a law, license, or agreement, they cancel it.

words.ex: He was released on parole after serving half his sentence.
words.ex_cn: 他在服刑一半后获得假释。
words.en: Parole is the release of a prisoner temporarily (for a special purpose) or permanently before the completion of a sentence, on the promise of good behavior.

words.ex: The cumulative score is the total of all previous points.
words.ex_cn: 累积得分是所有之前分数的总和。
words.en: If a series of events have a cumulative effect, each event makes the effect greater.

words.tr: adj. 刺鼻的；一语道破的
words.ex: The cheese has a pungent smell.
words.ex_cn: 这种奶酪有刺鼻的气味。
words.en: Having a sharply strong taste or smell.

words.ex: The forest remained pristine and untouched.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林保持原始且未被破坏。
words.en: Something that is pristine is in its original condition and has not been spoiled or damaged.

words.ex: The engineer built a prototype of the new car.
words.ex_cn: 工程师制作了这辆新车的原型。
words.en: A prototype is the first or original example of something that has been or will be copied or developed; it is a model or preliminary version.

words.ex: This apple is a variant of the red delicious.
words.ex_cn: 这种苹果是红富士的一个变体。
words.en: A variant is something that is slightly different from other similar things.

words.ex: The baby was born with a malformed hand.
words.ex_cn: 这个婴儿出生时手部畸形。
words.en: A malformed object or part of the body is not the correct shape or size because it has developed wrongly.

words.ex: The bulk of the students passed the exam.
words.ex_cn: 大部分学生通过了考试。
words.en: The bulk of something is most of it. The bulk of something is its size, especially when it is very large.

words.ex: The milk turned into curd after sitting overnight.
words.ex_cn: 牛奶放了一夜后变成了凝乳。
words.en: A soft, white substance formed when milk coagulates, used as the basis for cheese.

words.ex: The statue was colossal, taller than the building.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像巨大，比大楼还高。
words.en: If you describe something as colossal, you are emphasizing that it is very large.

words.ex: This is an evolutionary change in the species.
words.ex_cn: 这是该物种的一种进化的改变。
words.en: Relating to or denoting processes of development or growth, especially in a biological context.

words.tr: adj. 未充分发展的；初步的；基本的；
words.ex: His knowledge of math is rudimentary.
words.ex_cn: 他对数学的了解是初步的。
words.en: Rudimentary means relating to the basic or simplest aspects of a subject, or being in the earliest stages of development.

words.tr: adj. 暂定的；不确定的；试验性的；
words.ex: We made a tentative plan to meet next week.
words.ex_cn: 我们制定了一个下周见面的暂定计划。
words.en: If you make a tentative suggestion or plan, you make it without being sure that it is right or acceptable.

words.tr: adj. 毫不怀疑的；无危险意识的；无戒备心的
words.ex: The unsuspecting man gave his wallet to the stranger.
words.ex_cn: 那个毫无戒心的人把钱包给了陌生人。
words.en: If you describe someone as unsuspecting, you mean that they are not aware of something that is happening or going to happen, especially something that will cause them harm.

words.tr: adj. 无穷尽的；经久不衰的；永远可靠的
words.ex: Her unfailing smile made everyone feel welcome.
words.ex_cn: 她永不消失的微笑让每个人都感到受欢迎。
words.en: If you describe someone's good qualities or behaviour as unfailing, you mean that they never change.

words.ex: The new policy is problematic for small businesses.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策对小企业来说成问题。
words.en: If something is problematic, it involves problems and is difficult to deal with or solve.

words.tr:
n. 疑虑；怀疑
v. 使疑虑；使担忧；“misgive”的现在分词
words.ex: He had a misgiving about the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个计划感到不安。
words.en: A misgiving is a feeling of doubt or anxiety about something that might happen or might have happened.

words.ex: The witness lost credibility after lying.
words.ex_cn: 证人因撒谎而失去了可信性。
words.en: The quality of being trusted and believed in.

words.tr: adj. 性欲的；性爱的；色情的
words.ex: The movie contains erotic scenes that are not suitable for children.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影包含不适合儿童的色情场景。
words.en: Relating to or tending to arouse sexual desire or excitement.

words.tr: adj. 感觉上的；感官的；（引起）美感的
words.ex: She wore a sensuous silk dress.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件性感的丝绸裙子。
words.en: Relating to or affecting the senses rather than the intellect; characterized by a pleasing or luxurious quality that appeals to the senses.

words.tr:
n. 强烈的性欲；强烈的欲望
v. 对…有极强的性欲（或欲望）
words.ex: His lust for power ruined his relationships.
words.ex_cn: 他对权力的强烈欲望毁掉了他的关系。
words.en: Lust is a strong feeling of wanting to have or to do something, especially sexual desire.

words.tr:
v. 调情；轻率地对待
n. 与多人调情的人
words.ex: He flirts with her at the coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他在咖啡店向她调情。
words.en: If you flirt with someone, you behave as if you are sexually attracted to them, in a playful or not very serious way.

words.tr: v. 使气馁；使胆怯；吓倒
words.ex: The loud noise did not daunt her.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音并没有吓倒她。
words.en: If something daunts you, it makes you feel slightly afraid or worried about dealing with it.

words.tr: adj. 使人畏缩的；吓人的； v. “daunt”的现在分词；
words.ex: The math test seemed daunting to him.
words.ex_cn: 这次数学考试让他感到畏缩。
words.en: Something that is daunting makes you feel slightly afraid or worried about dealing with it.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.tr: v. 向往；渴望；追求；立志
words.ex: He aspires to be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他向往成为一名医生。
words.en: If you aspire to something, you have a strong desire to achieve it or attain it.

words.ex: They ascribe his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他们把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you ascribe an event or condition to a particular cause, you say or consider that it was caused by that thing.

words.ex: The study found a causal link between smoking and lung cancer.
words.ex_cn: 这项研究发现了吸烟与肺癌之间的因果关系。
words.en: A causal factor or event is one that causes or leads to something else.

words.tr:
adj. 作为结果的；合成的
n. 结果；产物
words.ex: The resultant force moved the box forward.
words.ex_cn: 合力把箱子向前推了。
words.en: A resultant thing or situation is the one that follows or is caused by a particular event or action.

words.tr: adj. 宏伟的；壮丽的；威严的；
words.ex: The majestic mountain stood above the clouds.
words.ex_cn: 那座宏伟的山峰耸立在云层之上。
words.en: If you describe something as majestic, you mean that it has a quality of greatness and impressiveness that often inspires admiration or awe.

words.ex: The grandeur of the palace amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿的宏伟让每个人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The quality of being grand or splendid in appearance or style.

words.tr:
v. （使）连锁；（使）相互扣住
n. 互锁设备
words.ex: The puzzle pieces interlock tightly.
words.ex_cn: 拼图块紧密地互锁在一起。
words.en: To interlock means to fit together firmly or closely, or to cause things to fit together in this way.

words.ex: The local company is an affiliate of the big global brand.
words.ex_cn: 这家本地公司是这个全球大品牌的分公司。
words.en: If an organization is affiliated with another larger organization, it is officially connected with the larger organization or is a member of it.

words.ex: The data points correlate with each other.
words.ex_cn: 这些数据点相互关联。
words.en: If one thing correlates with another, there is a close similarity or connection between them, often because one thing causes the other.

words.ex: The two rooms adjoin each other.
words.ex_cn: 这两个房间彼此相邻。
words.en: If one room, place, or object adjoins another, they are next to each other.

words.ex: At this juncture, we need to make a decision.
words.ex_cn: 在这一关键时刻，我们需要做出决定。
words.en: A particular point in events or time, especially one that is critical or decisive.

words.ex: The proximity of the school to the park makes it nice for kids.
words.ex_cn: 学校靠近公园，对孩子们来说很好。
words.en: Proximity refers to the state of being near in space or time.

words.ex: He tries to assimilate new words every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天努力吸收新单词。
words.en: To assimilate means to take in and understand fully ideas, information, or culture, or to make something become part of a group or system.

words.ex: The school used to segregate students by race.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校过去按种族隔离学生。
words.en: To segregate means to separate one group of people, animals, or things from another, especially because they are of different types or belong to different categories.

words.ex: Can you differentiate between the two colors?
words.ex_cn: 你能区分这两种颜色吗？
words.en: To differentiate means to recognize or express the difference between things or people.

words.tr: v. 使分离；脱离；与…无关
words.ex: He tried to disassociate himself from the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他试图把自己和那个错误分开。
words.en: To disassociate means to separate or disconnect something from something else, often in a way that is not physical.

words.ex: The two groups are discrete and do not overlap.
words.ex_cn: 这两个群体是分离的，没有重叠。
words.en: Something that is discrete is separate and distinct in form or concept.

words.ex: The project is ongoing.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目正在进行中。
words.en: An ongoing situation has been happening for quite a long time and seems likely to continue for some time in the future.

words.ex: He tries to mediate between the two friends.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在两个朋友之间调解。
words.en: To intervene between people or parties in order to bring about an agreement or reconciliation.

words.tr: v. 沉思；冥想；考虑；仔细计划
words.ex: He meditates every morning to feel calm.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上冥想以保持平静。
words.en: To meditate means to spend time in quiet thought for religious purposes or relaxation.

words.tr: v. 考虑；深思；凝视；思考…的可能性
words.ex: He contemplates quitting his job.
words.ex_cn: 他正在考虑辞去工作。
words.en: If you contemplate an action, you think about whether to do it or not.

words.tr: n. 测量仪器；规格；评估；
words.ex: The mechanic used a gauge to check the tire pressure.
words.ex_cn: 机械师用一个测量仪器来检查轮胎气压。
words.en: A gauge is a device that measures the amount or quantity of something and shows the measurement in a form that is easy to read, such as a dial or a digital display.

words.tr: v. 使可见；使形象化；设想；
words.ex: He uses maps to visualize the data.
words.ex_cn: 他使用地图来使数据可见。
words.en: If you visualize something, you imagine what it is like by forming a mental picture of it.

words.ex: The teacher will formulate a new rule for class.
words.ex_cn: 老师将制定一条新的课堂规则。
words.en: If you formulate something such as a plan or proposal, you invent it, thinking about the details carefully.

words.ex: He contrived to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他设法按时完成了项目。
words.en: If you contrive an event or situation, you succeed in making it happen, often by tricking someone.

words.tr: n. 头脑风暴；集思广益； v. “brainstorm”的现在分词；
words.ex: We had a brainstorming session to find new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 我们进行了一次头脑风暴来寻找新点子。
words.en: Brainstorming is a group creativity technique by which efforts are made to find a conclusion for a specific problem by gathering a list of ideas spontaneously contributed by its members.

words.tr: v.  合理化； 使合理
words.ex: He tries to rationalize his bad choices.
words.ex_cn: 他试图为自己的错误选择找借口。
words.en: To rationalize something means to try to find reasons to explain or justify it, often when these reasons are not really good ones.

words.tr: n. 基本原理；基础理论；
words.ex: The rationale for the new rule is to save time.
words.ex_cn: 这个新规则的基本原理是节省时间。
words.en: The fundamental reasons or logical basis for a course of action or belief.

words.tr: adj. 公开的；明显的；公然的
words.ex: His anger was overt and hard to miss.
words.ex_cn: 他的愤怒是明显的，很难忽视。
words.en: An overt action or attitude is done or shown in an open and obvious way.

words.ex: He is overly careful with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他花钱过于谨慎。
words.en: To an excessive degree.

words.ex: He was unduly harsh on his son.
words.ex_cn: 他对儿子过于严厉。
words.en: If you say that something does not happen or is not done unduly, you mean that it does not happen or is not done to an excessive or unnecessary extent.

words.ex: He crammed the suitcase with clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他把衣服塞满了行李箱。
words.en: If you cram things or people into a place, you put them into it even though there is hardly enough room for them.

words.ex: He is encumbered by too many debts.
words.ex_cn: 他被太多的债务拖累。
words.en: To encumber someone or something means to weigh them down or to block or hinder them.

words.tr:
n. 一小口；
v. 呷；啜；小口喝；
words.ex: He took a sip of water.
words.ex_cn: 他喝了一小口水。
words.en: To drink something slowly by taking small amounts into your mouth.

words.tr: phrase. 覆盖范围的文字说明；用于描述某项服务或产品覆盖区域的标注文字
words.ex: The map includes a coverage lettering that explains the service areas.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图包含了一段文字说明，解释了服务范围。
words.en: Text or lettering used to describe or provide information about an insurance policy's coverage.

words.tr: n. 天花乱坠的广告宣传；炒作；
words.ex: The new phone got a lot of hype before its release.
words.ex_cn: 这款新手机在发布前受到了大量天花乱坠的广告宣传。
words.en: If someone or something is hyped, they are praised or advertised a lot in newspapers, on television, etc., especially in a way that is intended to make them seem very exciting or important.

words.ex: The virus can propagate quickly among people.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒可以在人群中迅速传播。
words.en: To propagate something means to spread it and encourage more people to believe in it or support it.

words.tr:
v. 促进；使增长；
n. 提高；增强；
words.ex: Exercise can boost your energy.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进你的精力。
words.en: If one thing boosts another, it causes it to increase, improve, or be more successful.

chapters.name: Part II 专八最常考词汇 Lesson 8

words.ex: Exercise can enhance your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提高你的健康。
words.en: To enhance something means to improve its value, quality, or attractiveness.

words.ex: The wind propels the sailboat forward.
words.ex_cn: 风推动帆船前进。
words.en: To propel something in a particular direction means to cause it to move in that direction.

words.tr: v. 赋予能量；使精力充沛；激励
words.ex: Coffee helps me energize in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 咖啡帮助我在早上恢复活力。
words.en: To energize someone means to give them the enthusiasm, determination, and energy to do something.

words.ex: The new law gave impetus to environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 新法律为环境保护提供了推动力。
words.en: Something that gives a process impetus or an impetus makes it happen or progress more quickly.

words.ex: She painted with great verve.
words.ex_cn: 她作画时充满热情。
words.en: If you say that someone has verve, you mean that they seem to have a lot of energy and enthusiasm.

words.tr: v. 体现；使具体化；包含
words.ex: He embodies kindness and patience.
words.ex_cn: 他体现了善良和耐心。
words.en: To embody means to represent a quality or an idea exactly; to include or contain something.

words.ex: The book encompasses all basic math skills.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了所有基础数学技能。
words.en: If something encompasses particular things, it includes them.

words.tr: v. 举例说明；例证；例示
words.ex: This example exemplifies the rule clearly.
words.ex_cn: 这个例子清楚地说明了这条规则。
words.en: To exemplify means to be a typical example of something or to give an example of something.

words.tr: adj. 典范的；可做模范的；惩戒性的
words.ex: He is an exemplary student who always finishes his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名模范学生，总是完成作业。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as exemplary, you think they are extremely good and suitable to be copied by other people.

words.tr: v. 作…的摘要；成为…的缩影；概括；集中体现
words.ex: This painting epitomizes the beauty of nature.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画概括了自然的美。
words.en: If you say that something or someone epitomizes a particular thing, you mean that they are a perfect example of it.

words.ex: This experiment is a paradigm of scientific method.
words.ex_cn: 这个实验是科学方法的范例。
words.en: A paradigm is a model or pattern that is considered to be a typical example of something.

words.ex: Love is an intangible thing.
words.ex_cn: 爱是一种无形的东西。
words.en: Something that is intangible is not able to be touched or seen, but is still important or valuable.

words.tr:
adj. 不可接触的；达不到的
n. 不可接触者；贱民（旧时印度）
words.ex: The caste system made some people untouchable.
words.ex_cn: 种姓制度使一些人成为不可接触的人。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as untouchable, you mean that they cannot be affected or harmed by anything.

words.ex: His poem explores existential questions about life.
words.ex_cn: 他的诗歌探讨了有关存在的生命问题。
words.en: Relating to existence, especially human existence as viewed in the theories of existentialism.

words.ex: The terrestrial animals live on land.
words.ex_cn: 陆地动物生活在陆地上。
words.en: Of, on, or relating to the earth.

words.ex: The company is a legal entity.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司是一个法律实体。
words.en: An entity is something that exists separately from other things and has a clear identity of its own.

words.ex: He tried to repress his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抑制自己的愤怒。
words.en: If you repress a feeling, you deliberately do not express it, often because it is considered unacceptable or inappropriate.

words.ex: Her irrepressible laugh filled the room.
words.ex_cn: 她抑制不住的笑声充满了房间。
words.en: If someone is irrepressible, they are full of energy and enthusiasm and cannot be controlled or stopped.

words.ex: He felt the repression of his true feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他感受到了压抑自己真实情感的痛苦。
words.en: Repression is the act of subduing someone or something by force, or the state of being subdued in such a way.

words.ex: The law constrains companies from polluting rivers.
words.ex_cn: 法律约束公司不得污染河流。
words.en: To constrain someone or something means to limit their development or force them to behave in a particular way.

words.tr:
n. 路障；栅栏；阻碍
v. 设路障；阻挡
words.ex: The police put up a barricade to stop the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 警察设了一个路障来阻止人群。
words.en: A barricade is a temporary structure that is built across a road, entrance, or other route to prevent people from passing. It can also refer to the act of creating such a structure.

words.ex: The rain precludes a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 下雨阻止了野餐。
words.en: If something precludes an event or action, it prevents it from happening.

words.ex: Wear a helmet to counteract the risk of head injury.
words.ex_cn: 戴头盔以对抗头部受伤的风险。
words.en: If you counteract something, you reduce its effect by doing something that produces an opposite effect.

words.ex: The heavy fine is a deterrent to cheating.
words.ex_cn: 高额罚款是一种威慑作弊的力量。
words.en: Something that discourages or is intended to discourage someone from doing something.

words.ex: The storm unleashed heavy rain.
words.ex_cn: 风暴释放出大雨。
words.en: If you say that someone or something unleashes a powerful force, feeling, activity, or group, you mean that they suddenly start it or send it to move somewhere.

words.ex: The king banish the traitor from the kingdom.
words.ex_cn: 国王将叛徒驱逐出王国。
words.en: To banish someone means to send them away from a country or place and not allow them to return.

words.ex: The venerable teacher has taught for over 40 years.
words.ex_cn: 这位值得尊敬的老师已经教书40多年了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as venerable, you mean that they are old and respected.

words.ex: People venerate the ancient sage for his wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 人们因他的智慧而崇敬这位古代圣人。
words.en: To regard with respect or reverence.

words.ex: It is paradoxical that he sleeps all day but stays awake at night.
words.ex_cn: 他白天睡觉却晚上醒着，这很矛盾。
words.en: If something is paradoxical, it involves two facts or qualities which seem to contradict each other.

words.tr: adj. 不安全的；危险的；不稳当的；
words.ex: The ladder was precarious and might fall.
words.ex_cn: 梯子不安全，可能会倒。
words.en: If a situation is precarious, it is uncertain or dangerous, and could get worse or fail.

words.tr: adj. 欠缺的；过小的；少量的
words.ex: He had scanty food for the whole day.
words.ex_cn: 他一整天的食物很少。
words.en: If something is scanty, there is not enough of it or it is too small in amount.

words.ex: The storm personifies anger with loud thunder.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴用雷声拟人化了愤怒。
words.en: To represent a thing or abstraction as a person; to embody in a person.

words.ex: He tried to impersonate a police officer.
words.ex_cn: 他试图冒充一名警察。
words.en: To impersonate someone means to pretend to be that person, either to deceive people or to entertain them.

words.ex: He works hard to emulate his older brother.
words.ex_cn: 他努力赶上他的哥哥。
words.en: To emulate someone or something means to try to be like them or to do something in the same way that they do it.

words.ex: He contends that education is the key to success.
words.ex_cn: 他主张教育是成功的关键。
words.en: If you contend with someone or contend with something, you have to deal with a difficult situation or problem. If you contend that something is true, you state or argue that it is true.

words.tr: v. 求爱；求婚；寻求支持
words.ex: He tried to woo her with flowers and chocolates.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用鲜花和巧克力追求她。
words.en: If you woo someone, you try to persuade them to marry you or to have a relationship with you, or you try to gain their support or favor.

words.ex: The kids made a ruckus in the living room.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在客厅里闹出了很大的动静。
words.en: A ruckus is a noisy situation or argument.

words.ex: He took out a mortgage to buy his first house.
words.ex_cn: 他申请了一笔抵押贷款来购买他的第一套房子。
words.en: A mortgage is a loan of money which you get from a bank or building society in order to buy a house.

words.ex: He sent a remittance to his family last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周给家人汇了一笔款。
words.en: A remittance is a sum of money that you send to someone.

words.tr:
n. 发票；发货单；
v. 开发票；记清单；
words.ex: He paid the bill after receiving the invoice.
words.ex_cn: 他收到发票后付了款。
words.en: An invoice is a document that lists goods or services that have been provided and says how much money you owe for them.

words.ex: Free lunch is a perk of this job.
words.ex_cn: 免费午餐是这份工作的一个额外补贴。
words.en: If someone perks up or if something perks them up, they become more cheerful or lively.

words.ex: He brokered a deal between the two companies.
words.ex_cn: 他为两家公司安排了协商并达成协议。
words.en: A broker is a person whose job is to buy and sell shares, foreign money, or goods for other people.

words.tr: n. 额外费用；保险费；溢价；
words.ex: You need to pay a premium for faster delivery.
words.ex_cn: 你需要支付额外费用才能享受更快的配送。
words.en: A premium is an amount of money that you pay regularly to an insurance company for an insurance policy, or an amount of money that is more than usual for a product or service because it is of higher quality.

words.tr: n. 保持器；保留金；家仆
words.ex: The dentist gave me a retainer to wear at night.
words.ex_cn: 牙医给了我一个保持器，让我晚上戴着。
words.en: A retainer is a fee that you pay to someone in order to make sure that they will be available to do work for you when you need them to.

words.ex: The committee will convene tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 委员会明天将召开会议。
words.en: If someone convenes a meeting or conference, they arrange for it to take place. They can also be said to convene when they meet.

words.ex: The two roads converge at the town center.
words.ex_cn: 这两条路在镇中心交汇。
words.en: If roads or lines converge, they meet or join at a particular place.

words.tr:
v. 挤作一团
n. 挤作一团
words.ex: The team huddled together to plan their next move.
words.ex_cn: 团队聚在一起规划下一步行动。
words.en: If people huddle together, they stand, sit, or lie close to each other because they are cold or frightened.

words.tr: v. 招手示意；举手召唤；引诱
words.ex: He beckoned to the boy to come closer.
words.ex_cn: 他向那个男孩招手示意过来。
words.en: If you beckon to someone, you signal to them to come to you, usually by a gesture of your hand.

words.ex: The band will disband next month.
words.ex_cn: 这个乐队下个月将解散。
words.en: If someone disbands a group of people, or if the group disbands, it stops operating as a single unit.

words.ex: He showed his portfolio to the art teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他向美术老师展示了他作品集。
words.en: A portfolio is a set of pictures by someone, or photographs of examples of their work, which they use when entering competitions or applying for work.

words.tr: v. 承担经济责任；承保；承销
words.ex: The bank will underwrite the new project.
words.ex_cn: 银行将为这个新项目提供担保。
words.en: To agree to pay for a possible loss or damage, especially in insurance; to agree to buy all the shares that are not bought by the public in a new company, or to arrange for this to be done.

words.tr: v. 以低于市价售出；抛售
words.ex: The store undersells other shops by lowering prices.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店通过降价来以低于市价售出商品。
words.en: To sell something at a lower price than competitors or to undervalue something.

words.tr: v. 轻描淡写；打折扣地说；少说
words.ex: He understated the cost of the repair.
words.ex_cn: 他轻描淡写了维修的费用。
words.en: If you understate something, you describe it in a way that suggests it is less important or serious than it really is.

words.tr:
adj. 半生不熟的；煮得嫩的
v. 使煮得嫩；使做得不够；不尽全力做；“underdo”的过去分词
words.ex: The steak is underdone.
words.ex_cn: 这块牛排还没熟。
words.en: If food is underdone, it has not been cooked for long enough and is not ready to eat.

words.tr: n. 参与人（数）；装束；产量；清理
words.ex: The turnout for the election was very high.
words.ex_cn: 这次选举的投票率很高。
words.en: The number of people attending or participating in an event, especially a political meeting or election.

words.tr: n. 工作量；生产量；吞吐量
words.ex: The factory increased its throughput last month.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂上个月提高了工作量。
words.en: The amount of work or goods produced by a machine, system, or factory in a given period of time.

words.ex: The norm in this school is to arrive on time.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校的准则就是准时到校。
words.en: A norm is an official standard or level that organizations are expected to reach.

words.tr: n. 层次体系；等级制度；
words.ex: The company has a clear hierarchy from manager to worker.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司有一个从经理到员工的明确层次体系。
words.en: A hierarchy is a system in which people or things are arranged according to their importance.

words.tr: n. 装饰船头的人像；傀儡领袖；有名无实的首脑；
words.ex: The old ship had a wooden figurehead of a lion.
words.ex_cn: 那艘旧船的船头有一个木制的狮子像。
words.en: A figurehead is a person who is the head of an organization or country in name only, without any real power or authority.

words.ex: The manager will empower the team to make decisions.
words.ex_cn: 经理将授权团队做决定。
words.en: To give someone the authority or power to do something.

words.tr:
n. 授权；任期；委任；命令
v. 授权；委任
words.ex: The government has a mandate from the people to change the law.
words.ex_cn: 政府得到了人民的授权来修改法律。
words.en: If someone is given a mandate to carry out a particular policy or task, they are given the official authority to do it.

words.ex: The power will devolve to the local government.
words.ex_cn: 权力将下放给地方政府。
words.en: If you devolve power, authority, or responsibility to a less powerful person or group, or if it devolves upon them, it is transferred to them.

words.ex: The country seeks hegemony over its neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家试图对邻国实现霸权。
words.en: Hegemony refers to the dominance or leadership of one group or state over others, especially in a political or cultural context.

words.ex: Europeans colonized many parts of Africa in the 1800s.
words.ex_cn: 欧洲人在19世纪开拓了非洲的许多地区。
words.en: To colonize means to send people to live in and govern another country.

words.tr: n. 投票；选举权；参政权
words.ex: Women won suffrage in 1920.
words.ex_cn: 女性在1920年获得了选举权。
words.en: Suffrage is the right to vote in political elections.

words.ex: He bought a franchise to open a coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他购买了一个特许经营权来开一家咖啡店。
words.en: A franchise is an authorization granted by a government or company to an individual or group enabling them to carry out specified commercial activities, e.g., acting as an agent for a company's products.

words.tr: v. 委托；交付；托运；寄售
words.ex: He will consign the package to the post office.
words.ex_cn: 他将把包裹寄到邮局。
words.en: If you consign something to someone, you give it to them to keep or to sell.

words.tr: adj. 负有责任的；应作解释的
words.ex: He is accountable for his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他要为自己的错误负责。
words.en: If you are accountable to someone for something that you do, you are responsible for it and must be prepared to justify your actions to that person.

words.ex: He opted to stay home instead of going out.
words.ex_cn: 他选择待在家里而不是出去。
words.en: If you opt for something, or opt to do something, you choose it or decide to do it in preference to anything else.

words.ex: He obsesses over small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他 obsesses 于微小的错误。
words.en: If something or someone obsesses you, you think or worry about them all the time and you cannot think about anything else.

words.tr:
v. 使混乱；使糊涂；胡乱应付
n. 混乱；糊涂
words.ex: He muddled the instructions and got confused.
words.ex_cn: 他把说明搞混了，感到困惑。
words.en: If you muddle things or people, you get them mixed up, so that you do not know which is which.

words.tr:
adj. 困惑的；发呆的
v. 使困惑；使茫然；“bemuse”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He looked bemused when the teacher asked a strange question.
words.ex_cn: 当老师问了一个奇怪的问题时，他看起来很困惑。
words.en: If you are bemused, you are puzzled or confused.

words.tr:
n. 名声；名誉；名望
v. 认为；以为
words.ex: He is of good repute in his town.
words.ex_cn: 他在镇上声誉很好。
words.en: The opinion generally held of someone or something; the state of being regarded in a particular way.

words.ex: He is a scientist of great renown.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位享有盛誉的科学家。
words.en: Renown is the state of being known and talked about by many people because of your achievements, qualities, or actions.

words.ex: He uses a fake name for anonymity.
words.ex_cn: 他用假名来保持匿名。
words.en: The condition of being anonymous; the state of not having one's name or identity known.

words.ex: Loud noise aggravates his headache.
words.ex_cn: 噪音加重了他的头痛。
words.en: If someone or something aggravates a situation, they make it worse.

words.ex: The loud noise exasperates me.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让我感到烦躁。
words.en: If someone or something exasperates you, they annoy you and make you feel frustrated or impatient.

words.ex: He practices martial arts every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天练习武术。
words.en: Martial is used to describe things relating to soldiers or war.

words.tr: n. 停战（协定）；休战（协定）
words.ex: The two sides agreed to a truce.
words.ex_cn: 双方同意停火。
words.en: A truce is an agreement between enemies or opponents to stop fighting or arguing for a certain time.

words.ex: This is his first foray into painting.
words.ex_cn: 这是他首次涉足绘画。
words.en: A foray is a sudden and brief incursion or attack into enemy territory, especially to obtain something; a raid. It can also refer to an initial attempt to become involved in a different activity or profession.

chapters.name: Part II 专八最常考词汇 Lesson 9

words.ex: The onslaught of rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 大量倾泻的雨水淹没了街道。
words.en: An onslaught is a very powerful, often violent, attack against someone or something.

words.tr: n. 防御土墙；城墙；壁垒
words.ex: The old castle had a high rampart around it.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的城堡周围有一道高高的城墙。
words.en: A rampart is a wide, high wall of earth, stone, or other material built around a place to protect it from attack.

words.ex: The castle is a bastion of safety.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡是安全的堡垒。
words.en: A bastion is a projecting part of a fortification built at an angle to the line of a wall, so as to allow defensive fire in several directions.

words.tr: n. 解雇；活动停止期间
words.ex: He got a layoff last month.
words.ex_cn: 他上个月被裁员了。
words.en: A layoff is the termination of employment of an employee or, more commonly, a group of employees for business reasons, such as the decision of the company to downsize its operations.

words.ex: She bought a new outfit for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一套新衣服。
words.en: An outfit is a set of clothes worn together, especially for a particular occasion or purpose.

words.tr:
adj. 使人厌恶的；令人不快的；令人恶心的
v. 患病；恶心；（使）厌倦；“sicken”的现在分词
words.ex: The smell of rotten food is sickening.
words.ex_cn: 腐烂食物的气味令人作呕。
words.en: If you describe something as sickening, you mean that it makes you feel disgusted or horrified.

words.tr:
adj. 肮脏恶臭的；
v. 对…犯规；
words.ex: The foul smell came from the garbage bin.
words.ex_cn: 那股恶臭来自垃圾桶。
words.en: If you describe something as foul, you mean it is dirty and smells or tastes unpleasant. In sports, a foul is an act that is against the rules of the game.

words.tr: adj. 狂喜的；欣喜若狂的
words.ex: She was ecstatic when she won the prize.
words.ex_cn: 她赢得奖品时欣喜若狂。
words.en: If you are ecstatic, you feel very happy and full of excitement.

words.ex: The children shouted with glee when they saw the ice cream truck.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们看到冰淇淋车时高兴地大喊。
words.en: Glee is a feeling of great happiness, usually because something good has happened.

words.ex: The buoyancy of the water helps the boat float.
words.ex_cn: 水的浮力帮助船漂浮。
words.en: Buoyancy is the ability of something to float in a liquid or to rise in air or gas.

words.ex: He showed distaste for loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 他对嘈杂的声音感到反感。
words.en: If you feel distaste for someone or something, you dislike them and consider them to be unpleasant, unattractive, or morally unacceptable.

words.ex: He attests that the document is true.
words.ex_cn: 他证明这份文件是真实的。
words.en: To attest something means to declare or affirm that it is true or genuine, often in a formal or legal context.

words.ex: He tried to disprove the theory with new data.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用新数据驳斥这个理论。
words.en: To disprove something means to show that it is not true or correct.

words.tr:
v. 使滞留；使搁浅；
n. 方面；
words.ex: The storm stranded the travelers on the island.
words.ex_cn: 风暴使旅行者滞留在岛上。
words.en: If someone is stranded, they are left in a place that is difficult for them to get away from. A strand of something such as hair, wire, or thread is a single thin piece of it.

words.ex: A sliver of wood stuck in his finger.
words.ex_cn: 一小片木头扎进了他的手指。
words.en: A sliver is a small, thin piece of something that has been cut, broken, or torn off from a larger piece.

words.ex: The axe will cleave the wood in two.
words.ex_cn: 斧头会把木头劈成两半。
words.en: To split or sever something, especially along a natural line or grain; to adhere firmly and closely or loyally and unwaveringly to something.

words.ex: He fractured his arm during the soccer game.
words.ex_cn: 他在足球比赛中摔断了手臂。
words.en: If something such as a bone fractures or is fractured, it breaks or cracks.

words.ex: The storm left only wreckage on the beach.
words.ex_cn: 风暴在海滩上只留下了残骸。
words.en: The remains of something that has been badly damaged or destroyed.

words.tr:
v. 衰落；减弱；缺；亏
n. 衰退；减弱；缺；亏
words.ex: The moon begins to wane after the full moon.
words.ex_cn: 满月之后，月亮开始变暗。
words.en: If something wanes, it becomes gradually weaker or less, often so that it eventually disappears.

words.ex: The ground began to subside after the heavy rain.
words.ex_cn: 大雨之后，地面开始下陷。
words.en: If a feeling or noise subsides, it becomes less strong or loud.

words.tr:
n. 砍痕；伤痕；斜线号；削减
v. 砍；大幅度削减
words.ex: The tree has a deep slash on its trunk.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树的树干上有一道深深的砍痕。
words.en: To cut something with a sharp object in a violent way; to reduce something by a large amount suddenly.

words.ex: The war impoverished many families.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争使许多家庭变得贫困。
words.en: To make someone poor or to reduce the quality, strength, or richness of something.

words.ex: Babies have an innate ability to cry.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿生来就有哭泣的能力。
words.en: An innate quality or ability is one that you were born with, not one you have learned.

words.tr: adj. 固有的；内在的；本身的；
words.ex: Honesty is an intrinsic part of her character.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是她性格中固有的部分。
words.en: belonging to a thing by its very nature

words.tr: adj. 本质上的；实质性的；
words.ex: The change was substantive, not just cosmetic.
words.ex_cn: 这个改变是本质上的，而不仅仅是表面上的。
words.en: Something that is substantive is significant, meaningful, or important in a way that is not just superficial or formal.

words.ex: His smile evinces joy.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑流露出快乐。
words.en: To show clearly that you have a particular quality, feeling, or ability.

words.ex: The word 'home' connotes comfort and safety.
words.ex_cn: ‘家’这个词意味着舒适和安全。
words.en: If a word or name connotes something, it makes you think of a particular idea or quality.

words.tr: n. 入学介绍；岗前训练；方向；取向；
words.ex: The school held an orientation for new students on Monday.
words.ex_cn: 学校在周一为新生举行了入学介绍。
words.en: The act of orienting or the state of being oriented; the determination of the relative position of something or someone (especially oneself).

words.ex: We planned our itinerary before the trip.
words.ex_cn: 我们在旅行前规划了路线。
words.en: An itinerary is a plan of a journey, including the route and the places that you will visit.

words.tr: n. 家具陈设；室内陈设品；
words.ex: The room has simple furnishings.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间有简单的家具陈设。
words.en: The articles of furniture and other items that are used to make a room or building suitable for living or working in.

words.tr: v. 符合；“fit”的现在分词； adj. 恰当的；适合的；
words.ex: This shoe fits my foot perfectly.
words.ex_cn: 这双鞋很合我的脚。
words.en: Appropriate or suitable for a particular purpose, person, occasion, etc.

words.tr: v. 使协调一致；使和谐；配上和音
words.ex: The two singers try to harmonize their voices.
words.ex_cn: 两位歌手试图让他们的声音和谐。
words.en: If two or more things harmonize, they combine in a pleasing way, or if you harmonize them, you make them combine in a pleasing way.

words.ex: The mixture is homogeneous and looks the same throughout.
words.ex_cn: 这种混合物是均一的，看起来处处都一样。
words.en: Something that is homogeneous is uniform in nature or character throughout.

words.ex: The machine will homogenise the milk.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器会将牛奶均质化。
words.en: To homogenise something means to change it so that all its parts or elements become the same or are evenly mixed.

words.ex: The machine will homogenize the milk.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器会将牛奶均质化。
words.en: To homogenize something means to make it the same throughout, or to make it uniform.

words.ex: The net is made of a fine mesh.
words.ex_cn: 这个网是由细密的网状物制成的。
words.en: A mesh is a material made of a network of wire or thread to catch or hold things, or to allow things to pass through it.

words.ex: I concur with your opinion.
words.ex_cn: 我同意你的观点。
words.en: If one person concurs with another person, the first person agrees with the second person.

words.ex: The team reached a consensus on the project plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队就项目计划达成了共识。
words.en: A consensus is general agreement among a group of people.

words.ex: He finally conceded defeat after the match.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后，他终于承认失败了。
words.en: If you concede something, you admit, often unwillingly, that it is true or correct.

words.tr:
n. 轮廓；外形；等高线
v. 画轮廓（画等高线）
adj. 显示轮廓的
words.ex: The map shows the contour of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图显示了山的轮廓。
words.en: The outline of a figure, body, or mass, especially the curved shape of a surface.

words.ex: The upkeep of the house costs a lot each month.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子的维护每月花费很多。
words.en: The process of keeping something in good condition, especially a building or a piece of equipment.

words.ex: She scoured the pan until it was clean.
words.ex_cn: 她把锅擦得干干净净。
words.en: If you scour something, you clean it by rubbing it hard with something rough.

words.ex: She will beautify her garden with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 她将用花朵美化她的花园。
words.en: To make something more attractive or beautiful.

words.tr:
v. 使模糊；使看不清；弄污
n. 模糊
words.ex: The rain made the lights blur.
words.ex_cn: 雨使灯光变得模糊。
words.en: If something blurs your vision, it makes you unable to see things clearly.

words.ex: Cleaning the whole house is a laborious task.
words.ex_cn: 打扫整个房子是一项耗时费力的任务。
words.en: If you describe a task or job as laborious, you mean that it takes a lot of time and effort.

words.ex: Climbing the mountain was an arduous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰巨的任务。
words.en: Something that is arduous is difficult and tiring, and involves a lot of effort.

words.tr:
n. 艰苦跋涉；
v. 长途跋涉；
words.ex: The trek across the mountains took five days.
words.ex_cn: 穿越群山的艰苦跋涉花了五天时间。
words.en: A trek is a long and often difficult journey, especially one made on foot.

words.tr:
v. 缓慢或吃力地走
n. 长途跋涉
words.ex: He trudges through the snow every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上跋涉穿过雪地。
words.en: To walk slowly and with heavy steps, typically because of exhaustion or harsh conditions.

words.tr: v. 摇摇欲坠；摇摆；玩跷跷板
words.ex: The child teeters on the edge of the pool.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在泳池边摇摇晃晃。
words.en: To move or balance unsteadily; sway back and forth.

words.tr:
v. 拖曳；搅乱；洗牌；移来移去
n. 拖着脚走；洗牌；混在一起
words.ex: He shuffle his feet across the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他拖着脚在地板上走。
words.en: To shuffle is to walk by dragging one's feet along or without lifting them fully from the ground. It also means to mix up the order of things, especially cards in a deck.

words.ex: Running a business entails hard work.
words.ex_cn: 经营企业必然需要努力工作。
words.en: If one thing entails another, it involves it or causes it.

words.ex: You must abide by the rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守规则。
words.en: If you can't abide someone or something, you dislike them very much.

words.ex: The bridge can withstand strong winds.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥能经受住强风。
words.en: If something or someone withstands a force or action, they survive it or do not give in to it.

words.tr: v. 戒绝；弃权；自我克制
words.ex: He abstains from eating sugar.
words.ex_cn: 他戒食糖。
words.en: If you abstain from something, you deliberately do not do it or have it, especially something you like or enjoy which might be considered bad for you.

words.ex: The old tool fell into disuse after the new one was invented.
words.ex_cn: 新工具发明后，旧工具就被弃而不用了。
words.en: The state of not being used or practiced anymore.

words.ex: The disposal of waste is important for the environment.
words.ex_cn: 废物的处理对环境很重要。
words.en: The act or process of getting rid of something, especially by throwing it away or selling it.

words.tr:
v. 安慰；慰问
n. 控制台；操纵台
words.ex: She whispered kind words to console her crying friend.
words.ex_cn: 她轻声说些安慰的话来安抚哭泣的朋友。
words.en: If you console someone who is unhappy about something, you try to make them feel more cheerful.

words.tr: adj. 痛苦的；严重的；剧烈的
words.ex: The injury caused him grievous pain.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤给他带来了巨大的痛苦。
words.en: If you describe something such as a loss or injury as grievous, you mean that it is extremely serious or worrying in its effects.

words.ex: The accident left him with a serious trauma on his leg.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故使他的腿受了严重的伤。
words.en: A trauma is a very distressing or disturbing experience.

words.ex: He made his decision after long deliberation.
words.ex_cn: 他在深思熟虑后做出了决定。
words.en: Deliberation is the long and careful consideration of a subject.

words.ex: He went for a walk irrespective of the rain.
words.ex_cn: 他不顾下雨去散步了。
words.en: If something is done or happens irrespective of particular factors, it is not influenced or affected by them.

words.tr: prep. 关于； v. 看待；“regard”的现在分词；
words.ex: He sent me an email regarding the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他给我发了一封关于会议的邮件。
words.en: You can use regarding to indicate the subject that is being talked or written about.

words.ex: They collude to cheat in the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他们串通在考试中作弊。
words.en: If one person colludes with another, they co-operate with them secretly or illegally.

words.ex: They conspire to cheat on the test.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋在考试中作弊。
words.en: If two or more people or groups conspire to do something illegal or harmful, they make a secret agreement to do it.

words.tr:
v. 密谋；激起…的兴趣
n. 阴谋诡计；密谋策划
words.ex: They intrigue to take over the company.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋接管这家公司。
words.en: If something intrigues you, it interests you a lot because it seems strange or mysterious.

words.ex: She tries to juggle her job and caring for her kids.
words.ex_cn: 她努力兼顾工作和照顾孩子。
words.en: If you juggle, you keep several objects in motion in the air at the same time by repeatedly throwing and catching them. Juggle can also mean to deal with several things at the same time, often in a skillful way.

words.tr:
n. 蓄意破坏
v. 蓄意破坏；暗中破坏
words.ex: He tried to sabotage the project.
words.ex_cn: 他试图破坏这个项目。
words.en: Sabotage is the act of deliberately destroying, damaging, or obstructing something, especially for political or military advantage.

words.ex: The earthquake devastated the small town.
words.ex_cn: 地震摧毁了这个小镇。
words.en: To devastate means to destroy or ruin something completely, or to cause someone to feel extreme sadness or shock.

words.ex: The train will derail if the tracks are broken.
words.ex_cn: 如果铁轨损坏，火车就会脱轨。
words.en: To cause a train or other vehicle to leave its tracks accidentally; to divert or cause to deviate from an intended course.

words.tr: v. 使粉碎；使破碎；使破灭；
words.ex: The stone shattered when it hit the ground.
words.ex_cn: 石头撞到地面时碎裂了。
words.en: If something shatters or is shattered, it breaks into a lot of small pieces.

words.tr: v. 熄灭；平息；抑制（欲望）；用水冷却
words.ex: He quenched the fire with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水熄灭了火。
words.en: To satisfy one's thirst or to extinguish a fire or to suppress a feeling or desire.

words.ex: The flowers will perish if you don't water them.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不给花浇水，它们会死。
words.en: If people or animals perish, they die as a result of very harsh conditions or as the result of an accident.

words.tr: n. 自卫；自保；自我保护
words.ex: The animal acted out of self-preservation when it ran away from the predator.
words.ex_cn: 当动物从捕食者身边逃跑时，它是出于自卫。
words.en: Self-preservation is the instinctive behavior that protects an organism from harm or death.

words.ex: He was arrested as an accomplice to the robbery.
words.ex_cn: 他因作为抢劫的帮凶而被逮捕。
words.en: An accomplice is someone who helps another person to commit a crime.

words.ex: The fugitive hid in the woods for weeks.
words.ex_cn: 这名逃亡者在树林里躲了几个星期。
words.en: A fugitive is someone who is running away or hiding, usually in order to avoid being caught by the police.

words.tr:
n. 掠夺物；掠夺；赃物
v. 掠夺；洗劫
words.ex: The pirates found loot on the sunken ship.
words.ex_cn: 海盗们在沉船中找到了战利品。
words.en: Loot refers to goods stolen from a place, especially during a war or riot. It can also mean to steal goods from a place, especially during a war or riot.

words.ex: He covets his neighbor's car.
words.ex_cn: 他垂涎邻居的车。
words.en: If you covet something, you have a very strong desire to possess it, especially something that belongs to someone else.

words.tr: adj. 可管理的；可应付的；可处理的；
words.ex: The project is manageable if we work together.
words.ex_cn: 如果我们一起合作，这个项目是可以管理的。
words.en: If you describe something as manageable, you mean that it is easy to control or deal with.

words.ex: He has a managerial role in the company.
words.ex_cn: 他在公司中担任管理职务。
words.en: relating to the job of a manager

words.tr: v. 哄；用好话劝诱；哄骗
words.ex: He tried to coax the cat out from under the bed.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄猫从床底下出来。
words.en: To coax someone means to persuade them to do something by gentle persuasion or flattery.

words.tr:
v. 吸引；诱惑；引诱
n. 诱惑；诱饵；吸引力
words.ex: The bright colors lure the birds to the feeder.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的颜色吸引鸟类来到喂食器。
words.en: If you lure someone, you tempt them to do something or to go somewhere, especially by offering some form of reward.

chapters.name: Part II 专八最常考词汇 Lesson 10

words.ex: She was frantic to catch the last bus.
words.ex_cn: 她急忙赶着赶最后一班公交车。
words.en: If someone is frantic, they are behaving in a wild and desperate way, often because they are frightened or worried.

words.tr: adj. 狂乱的；狂暴的；疯狂似的； v. “frenzy”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The crowd became frenzied when the singer appeared.
words.ex_cn: 当歌手出现时，人群变得狂乱。
words.en: If you describe an activity as frenzied, you mean that it is fast and energetic, but rather uncontrolled and often wild.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；难驾驭的；脾气不好的
words.ex: The fractious child refused to eat his vegetables.
words.ex_cn: 这个脾气暴躁的孩子拒绝吃蔬菜。
words.en: If you describe someone as fractious, you mean they are easily upset or annoyed, and often complain.

words.ex: He frets about his exam results.
words.ex_cn: 他为考试成绩感到烦躁不安。
words.en: If you fret about something, you worry about it.

words.tr: v. 使心神不宁；使不安；扰乱
words.ex: The loud noise unsettled the baby.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让婴儿不安。
words.en: To make someone feel anxious or uncertain.

words.tr: adj. 悲哀的；忧愁的；阴沉的
words.ex: He gave a doleful look after losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 输掉比赛后，他露出悲伤的表情。
words.en: A doleful expression, sound, or manner is very sad.

words.tr:
v. 检查；核对；
n. 检查；支票；阻止；
words.ex: Please check your homework before class.
words.ex_cn: 请在上课前检查你的作业。
words.en: To examine something in order to determine its accuracy, quality, or condition, or to make sure that something is correct or safe.

words.ex: His benevolence helped the poor family.
words.ex_cn: 他的仁慈帮助了这个贫困家庭。
words.en: The quality of being well meaning; kindness.

words.tr: adj. 有同情心的；表示怜悯的；
words.ex: She is a compassionate teacher who helps struggling students.
words.ex_cn: 她是一位有同情心的老师，帮助学习困难的学生。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as compassionate, you mean that they feel or show pity, sympathy, and understanding for people who are suffering.

words.tr: adj. 亲切的；和蔼的；温暖的
words.ex: He is a genial man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Friendly and cheerful.

words.tr: adj. 铁石心肠的；无情的；起老茧的
words.ex: He was callous to his friend's pain.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的痛苦无动于衷。
words.en: A callous person or action is very cruel and shows no concern for other people or their feelings.

words.tr: adj. 若无其事的；不在乎的；冷淡的
words.ex: He was nonchalant about the test result.
words.ex_cn: 他对考试结果表现得漫不经心。
words.en: If you describe someone as nonchalant, you mean that they appear not to worry or care about things and that they seem very calm.

words.tr: adj. 不屈不挠的；不松懈的；无情的
words.ex: He showed unrelenting effort to finish the race.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持不懈地努力完成比赛。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as unrelenting, you mean that they are continuing to do something in a very determined way, often without caring whether they hurt or embarrass other people.

words.ex: The treacherous road made driving very scary.
words.ex_cn: 这条危险的道路让驾驶非常可怕。
words.en: If you describe someone as treacherous, you mean that they are likely to betray you and cannot be trusted. If you say that something is treacherous, you mean that it is very dangerous and unpredictable.

words.tr: adj. 奴隶的；盲从的；无创意的
words.ex: He made a slavish effort to please his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他为了取悦老板，做出了奴隶般的努力。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as slavish, you are criticizing them for copying someone else's work or ideas in a way that lacks originality.

words.tr: adj. 不在乎的；不害臊的；不难为情的
words.ex: He was unabashed about his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的错误毫不在意。
words.en: If you describe someone as unabashed, you mean that they are not ashamed, embarrassed, or shy about something, especially something that might make other people feel uncomfortable.

words.ex: Dolphins are gregarious animals that swim in groups.
words.ex_cn: 海豚是群居动物，成群游泳。
words.en: Someone who is gregarious enjoys being with other people.

words.ex: He is obese because he eats too much junk food.
words.ex_cn: 他因为吃太多垃圾食品而肥胖。
words.en: If someone is obese, they are extremely fat.

words.tr: adj. 强健的；强壮的；结实的；
words.ex: The dog is robust and runs every day.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗很强健，每天跑步。
words.en: Strong and healthy; vigorous. (of an object) sturdy in construction.

words.tr:
adj. 裸体的
n. 裸体；裸体画；裸体像
words.ex: He painted a nude woman by the window.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一位在窗边的裸体女性。
words.en: A nude person is not wearing any clothes. A nude painting or sculpture shows a person who is not wearing any clothes.

words.ex: Honesty is a good trait.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一种好的特性。
words.en: A trait is a particular characteristic, quality, or tendency that someone or something has.

words.ex: Heredity determines eye color in humans.
words.ex_cn: 遗传决定人类的眼睛颜色。
words.en: Heredity is the process by which features and characteristics are passed on from parents to their children before the children are born.

words.tr: v. 遗赠；遗留；把…传下去
words.ex: He bequeathed his house to his daughter.
words.ex_cn: 他把房子遗赠给了他的女儿。
words.en: If you bequeath your money or property to someone, you legally state that they should have it when you die.

words.ex: He noticed the nuance in her voice.
words.ex_cn: 他注意到了她声音中的细微差别。
words.en: A very slight difference in meaning, sound, color, or someone's feelings that is not usually very obvious.

words.tr: adj. 边缘的；页边的；微不足道的；不重要的
words.ex: The village is on the marginal area of the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄位于城市的边缘地区。
words.en: If you describe something as marginal, you mean that it is small or not very important.

words.ex: His perception of the sound was very sharp.
words.ex_cn: 他对声音的感知非常敏锐。
words.en: Your perception of something is the way that you think about it or the impression you have of it.

words.tr: adj. 感觉不到的；极细微的
words.ex: The change was imperceptible to the naked eye.
words.ex_cn: 这个变化肉眼无法察觉。
words.en: Something that is imperceptible is so small or slight that it cannot be seen or noticed.

words.ex: Children are susceptible to colds.
words.ex_cn: 孩子容易感冒。
words.en: If you are susceptible to something or someone, you are very likely to be influenced by them.

words.ex: Measles is a communicable disease.
words.ex_cn: 麻疹是一种会传染的疾病。
words.en: A communicable disease is one that can be passed from one person or animal to another.

words.ex: The two twins are indistinguishable in the photo.
words.ex_cn: 照片中的这对双胞胎难以区分。
words.en: If one thing is indistinguishable from another, the two things are so similar that it is difficult to know which is which or to tell them apart.

words.tr: adj. 不加选择的；不加区别的；
words.ex: The bombing was indiscriminate and hurt many civilians.
words.ex_cn: 这次轰炸是不加选择的，伤害了许多平民。
words.en: If you describe an action as indiscriminate, you are critical of it because it does not involve any careful thought or choice.

words.ex: The cat hunched its back when it saw the dog.
words.ex_cn: 猫看到狗时，背部拱了起来。
words.en: A hunch is a feeling or guess based on intuition rather than known facts.

words.ex: I trusted my intuition and chose the right answer.
words.ex_cn: 我相信自己的直觉，选了正确的答案。
words.en: Intuition is the ability to understand or know something immediately, without the need for conscious reasoning.

words.ex: The dark clouds looked ominous before the storm.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨来临前，乌云显得不祥。
words.en: If you describe something as ominous, you mean that it worries you because it makes you think that something unpleasant is going to happen.

words.tr:
adj. 甜熟的；醇香的；柔和的；成熟的；沉醉的
v. （使）成熟；（使颜色）柔和；（使酒）更加醇香
words.ex: The apple became mellow after a few days.
words.ex_cn: 几天后，苹果变软了。
words.en: If someone mellows or if something mellows them, they become kinder or less extreme in their behavior, often as a result of becoming older or more experienced.

words.tr: adj. 红润的；红的；淡红色
words.ex: Her complexion was ruddy from the cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 她的脸色因寒冷的天气而变得红润。
words.en: Having a healthy red color, especially in the face.

words.ex: The lush grass looked green after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后，葱翠的草地显得格外绿。
words.en: A lush area has a lot of green, healthy plants, grass, and trees.

words.ex: The apple shrivels in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 苹果在阳光下皱缩。
words.en: If something shrivels or if you shrivel it, it becomes dryer and smaller, often with lines in its surface, as a result of losing the water it contains.

words.ex: The abrasive surface wore down the metal.
words.ex_cn: 磨损的表面磨耗了金属。
words.en: An abrasive substance is rough and can be used to clean surfaces or to make them smooth by rubbing. An abrasive person is someone who is harsh and rude.

words.tr: adj. 强制的；强迫的；强有力的
words.ex: The police used forcible entry to get inside.
words.ex_cn: 警察强行进入里面。
words.en: Forcible is used to describe something that is done using physical force or violence, or something that is done in a strong and effective way.

words.ex: The medicine is potent and works quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物非常有效，起效很快。
words.en: Something that is potent is very effective and powerful.

words.tr: adj. 无力的；虚弱的；阳痿的
words.ex: He felt impotent after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到无能为力。
words.en: If someone feels impotent, they feel that they have no power to influence people or events.

words.tr: v. 告诉；讲述；“tell”的现在分词； adj. 有力的；反映情况的；
words.ex: He told me the news.
words.ex_cn: 他告诉了我这个消息。
words.en: If something is telling, it shows the true nature of a situation or someone's feelings or character in a very clear way.

words.ex: The void on the page made the text look empty.
words.ex_cn: 页面上的空白让文字看起来空荡荡的。
words.en: If you describe a situation or a feeling as a void, you mean that it seems empty because there is nothing interesting or worthwhile about it.

words.ex: The view from the hill is panoramic.
words.ex_cn: 从山上望去，景色一览无余。
words.en: A panoramic view or picture is one that shows a wide area of land or sea.

words.ex: The report gives an overview of the project.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告对项目进行了概述。
