words.en: To blanch means to make something white or pale, often by removing color or by causing it to lose color. It can also refer to the process of briefly boiling vegetables and then plunging them into cold water to halt the cooking process.

words.tr:
n. 鹌鹑；鹌鹑肉 
v. 畏缩；胆怯
words.ex: The farmer raised quail for their eggs.
words.ex_cn: 农夫饲养鹌鹑来获取它们的蛋。
words.en: If someone quails, they feel or show fear or hesitation.

words.tr:
v. 颤抖；颤动；发抖
n. 颤抖
words.ex: The leaf quivers in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 树叶在风中颤抖。
words.en: To shake or tremble with a slight rapid motion; a case for carrying arrows.

words.ex: The earthquake caused a strong tremor in the building.
words.ex_cn: 地震使大楼发生了强烈的震动。
words.en: A tremor is a small earthquake or a shaking or vibrating movement, especially one caused by fear or nervousness.

words.tr:
v. 跳动；悸动；颤动
n. 跳动；搏动；悸动
words.ex: His heart throbbed with fear.
words.ex_cn: 他的心脏因恐惧而跳动。
words.en: If part of your body throbs, you feel a series of strong and usually painful beats there.

words.ex: The disease afflicted many people in the village.
words.ex_cn: 这种疾病使村子里许多人遭受痛苦。
words.en: If you are afflicted by pain, illness, or misfortune, it causes you great suffering and distress.

words.tr: v. 使恼怒；使厌烦；使烦恼
words.ex: The loud noise irks her every morning.
words.ex_cn: 每天早上，巨大的噪音都让她感到烦躁。
words.en: To irritate, annoy, or exasperate someone.

words.ex: The loud noise vexes my little brother.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的声音让我的小弟弟很烦。
words.en: If someone or something vexes you, they make you feel annoyed, puzzled, and frustrated.

words.tr: v. 骚扰；烦扰；屡次侵扰
words.ex: He harasses his coworkers with loud jokes.
words.ex_cn: 他用大声的笑话骚扰他的同事。
words.en: If someone harasses you, they trouble or annoy you, for example by attacking you repeatedly or by causing you as many problems as they can.

words.ex: He was arrested for molesting a child.
words.ex_cn: 他因骚扰儿童而被逮捕。
words.en: To molest someone means to assault or harass them, especially sexually.

words.ex: His talent overshadowed his brother's achievements.
words.ex_cn: 他的才华使他兄弟的成就黯然失色。
words.en: If an unpleasant event or feeling overshadows something, it makes it less happy or enjoyable.

words.tr:
v. 使困惑；难倒；阻碍
n. 挡板；遮护物；阻碍体
words.ex: The magic trick baffled the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: If something baffles you, you cannot understand it or explain it.

words.ex: The children walked carefully through the bog.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们小心地走过沼泽。
words.en: A bog is an area of wet muddy ground that is too soft to support a heavy body.

words.tr: v. 尝试；试图；“try”的现在分词； adj. 难对付的；令人厌烦的；
words.ex: He is trying to learn English.
words.ex_cn: 他正在尝试学习英语。
words.en: If you describe something as trying, you mean that it is difficult to deal with and causes you to feel annoyed or upset.

words.tr: adj. 心烦意乱的；忧心如焚的
words.ex: She was distraught when she lost her dog.
words.ex_cn: 当她丢失了她的狗时，她非常悲痛。
words.en: If someone is distraught, they are so upset and worried that they cannot think clearly.

words.tr: adj. 充满（不愉快事物）的；
words.ex: The journey was fraught with delays.
words.ex_cn: 这次旅程充满了延误。
words.en: If a situation or activity is fraught with problems or risks, it is full of them.

words.tr:
v. 坐立不安；烦躁；摆弄
n. 坐立不安；烦躁
words.ex: She couldn't sit still and kept fidgeting during the lecture.
words.ex_cn: 她无法静坐，在讲座中不停地烦躁不安。
words.en: If you fidget, you keep moving your hands or feet slightly or changing your position slightly, for example because you are nervous, bored, or excited.

words.tr: adj. 发烧的；紧张忙乱的；极度紧张（或兴奋）的
words.ex: He is feverish after running in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 他在太阳下跑步后发高烧。
words.en: If you are feverish, you are suffering from a fever, or you are extremely excited or worried about something.

words.ex: Hiking up the mountain was a strenuous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰苦的任务。
words.en: Requiring or using great effort or exertion.

words.tr: adj. 累断腰的；非常辛劳的
words.ex: He did backbreaking work in the fields every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天在田里干繁重的活。
words.en: If you describe a task as backbreaking, you mean that it is extremely hard physical work.

words.tr: adj. 要求高精度的；繁琐的
words.ex: The fiddly buttons on the remote are hard to press.
words.ex_cn: 遥控器上那些小按钮很难按。
words.en: If you describe a task or job as fiddly, you mean that it is very complicated and difficult to do, often because it involves small or delicate objects.

words.ex: He is an assiduous student who studies every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个勤奋的学生，每天都学习。
words.en: Someone who is assiduous works hard or does things very thoroughly.

words.ex: He is a studious student who always does his homework carefully.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个认真学习的学生，总是认真完成作业。
words.en: Someone who is studious spends a lot of time studying and reading.

words.tr: adj. 懒惰的；懒散的；好逸恶劳的
words.ex: He is indolent and never does his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他很懒，从不做作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as indolent, you mean that they are lazy.

words.tr: adj. 过分活跃的；多动的；亢奋的
words.ex: The hyperactive child runs around the room all day.
words.ex_cn: 这个多动的孩子整天在房间里跑来跑去。
words.en: If someone is hyperactive, they are extremely active and find it difficult to relax or concentrate on one thing for very long.

words.ex: He tried to hector the little boy into giving up his toy.
words.ex_cn: 他试图威吓那个小男孩，让他交出玩具。
words.en: If you say that someone is hectoring you, you do not like the way they are trying to make you do something by bothering you and talking to you aggressively.

words.tr:
n. 鬼；幽灵；间谍
v. 鬼怪般出没；吓唬
words.ex: The children were scared of the spook in the haunted house.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们害怕鬼屋里的鬼。
words.en: A spook is a ghost or a spy. It can also mean to frighten or scare someone.

words.tr:
n. 勒索；敲诈
v. 勒索；讹诈
words.ex: He threatened to tell the truth unless she paid him money — that's blackmail.
words.ex_cn: 他威胁说，除非她付钱，否则就说出真相——这就是敲诈。
words.en: Blackmail is the action of threatening to reveal a secret about someone, unless they do something you want, such as give you money.

words.ex: The gang tried to extort money from the shop owner.
words.ex_cn: 这个帮派试图向店主敲诈钱财。
words.en: To extort is to obtain something, especially money, through force, threats, or other unfair means.

words.ex: They tried to coerce him into signing the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图强迫他签署那份文件。
words.en: If you coerce someone into doing something, you make them do it, even though they do not want to.

words.tr: n. 强迫；强制；难以抗拒的冲动
words.ex: He felt a compulsion to check the door again.
words.ex_cn: 他感到一种必须再次检查门的强迫感。
words.en: A compulsion is a very strong desire to do something, which you find difficult to control.

words.tr: v. 把…强加给；使遭受；使承受
words.ex: The storm inflicted heavy damage on the village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴给村庄造成了严重破坏。
words.en: If you inflict something unpleasant on someone, you make them suffer it.

words.ex: They tried to foist inferior products on unsuspecting customers.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图将劣质产品蒙骗给毫无戒心的顾客。
words.en: If someone foists something on you, they force you to accept it, even though you may not want it.

words.ex: He tried to incite a riot with his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过演讲煽动暴乱。
words.en: To incite someone to do something means to encourage or persuade them to do it, often in a way that is negative or harmful.

words.ex: He tried to agitate the workers to strike.
words.ex_cn: 他试图鼓动工人罢工。
words.en: If you agitate something, you stir it up or shake it. If something agitates you, it makes you feel anxious or upset.

words.tr:
adj. 引火的；燃烧的；纵火的；煽动的
n. 燃烧弹
words.ex: The incendiary device set the building on fire.
words.ex_cn: 这个引火装置把大楼点燃了。
words.en: An incendiary device is designed to cause fires. Incendiary remarks or actions are likely to cause anger or violence.

words.ex: The speech stoked anger among the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 这篇演讲激起了人群的愤怒。
words.en: To stoke a fire means to add fuel to it to make it burn more strongly. It can also mean to encourage or increase strong feelings or emotions.

words.ex: The noise infuriates my neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 噪音让我的邻居非常生气。
words.en: To make someone extremely angry.

words.ex: His rude words inflamed the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话激怒了人群。
words.en: To inflame a situation or feeling means to make it much more intense or serious.

words.ex: The unfair rule enrage him.
words.ex_cn: 不公平的规则激怒了他。
words.en: To make someone extremely angry.

words.tr: v. 使发狂；使发疯；使发怒
words.ex: The loud noise madden him.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让他发狂。
words.en: To make someone extremely angry or annoyed.

words.tr:
v. 愠怒；生闷气
n. 愠怒；生闷气
words.ex: He sulked in his room after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 争吵后，他生闷气待在房间里。
words.en: If you sulk, you are silent and bad-tempered for a while because you are annoyed about something.

words.ex: He gave her a scowl when she was late.
words.ex_cn: 她迟到时，他皱了皱眉。
words.en: When someone scowls, they look at someone or something with an angry or irritated expression.

words.tr: v. 砍；劈；侵入（计算机系统）；“hack”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He hacked the tree with an axe.
words.ex_cn: 他用斧头砍树。
words.en: If someone hacks into a computer system, they break into the system, especially in order to get secret information.

words.tr: adj. 青黑色的；苍白的；暴怒的
words.ex: His face turned livid after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他的脸变得青黑色。
words.en: If you say that someone is livid, you mean that they are extremely angry.

words.ex: The roller coaster exhilarates the children.
words.ex_cn: 过山车让孩子们感到兴奋。
words.en: To make someone feel very happy and excited.

words.ex: He gratifies his parents by getting good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他通过取得好成绩来让父母感到欣慰。
words.en: If you are gratified by something, it gives you pleasure or satisfaction.

words.tr: v. 使带电；使电气化；使激动不已
words.ex: The new train system will electrify the entire region.
words.ex_cn: 新的火车系统将使整个地区电气化。
words.en: To electrify something means to make it operate using electricity or to make it more exciting or interesting.

words.tr: v. 幸灾乐祸；沾沾自喜；满足地看
words.ex: He gloats when his rival loses the game.
words.ex_cn: 当他的对手输掉比赛时，他幸灾乐祸。
words.en: To gloat means to observe or think about something with triumphant and often malicious satisfaction, gratification, or delight.

words.tr:
v. 偷看；窥视
n. 偷看；窥见
words.ex: He peeked through the keyhole.
words.ex_cn: 他从钥匙孔里偷看。
words.en: To peek means to look at something quickly and secretly, especially through a small opening or from behind something.

words.tr:
v. 目瞪口呆地看；裂开
n. 目瞪口呆地看；裂口
words.ex: The children gape at the magic show.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们张大嘴看着魔术表演。
words.en: To open the mouth wide; to stare with open mouth, as in wonder.

words.tr:
n. 谷歌（网络搜索引擎）；
vt. 用搜索引擎搜索（尤指用谷歌搜索引擎）；
words.ex: I use Google to find information online.
words.ex_cn: 我使用谷歌在网上查找信息。
words.en: To use the Google search engine to find information on the internet.

words.tr:
v. 眯着眼看；斜视
n. 斜视；一瞥
words.ex: He squints to see the small letters.
words.ex_cn: 他眯着眼睛看那些小字。
words.en: To squint means to look at something with your eyes partly closed in order to see better, or because of bright light. It can also refer to a condition where the eyes do not look in the same direction.

words.ex: He didn't flinch when the needle touched his skin.
words.ex_cn: 当针碰到他的皮肤时，他没有退缩。
words.en: If you flinch, you make a small sudden movement, especially when something surprises you or hurts you.

words.tr:
n. 皱眉蹙额；退缩
v. 皱眉蹙额；退避
words.ex: He let out a wince when he touched his sore arm.
words.ex_cn: 当他碰触到疼痛的手臂时，他皱了一下眉。
words.en: If you wince, you make a slight, sudden movement of your face, especially when you are in pain or when you see or hear something unpleasant.

words.tr: v. （使）无法理解；（因吃惊）犹豫不决
words.ex: The math problem boggles my mind.
words.ex_cn: 这道数学题让我困惑不已。
words.en: If you boggle at something, you are astonished or overwhelmed by it, often because it is very complicated or large.

words.tr:
v. 发抖；犹豫不决
n. 发抖；颤抖
words.ex: He dithered in the cold wind.
words.ex_cn: 他在寒风中发抖。
words.en: To be unable to make a decision quickly; to hesitate or waver.

words.tr:
v. 畏缩不前；犹豫；妨碍
n. 阻碍，妨碍
words.ex: He balks at paying high prices.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意支付高价。
words.en: If you balk at something, you hesitate to do it or agree to it, often because it is unpleasant or difficult.

words.ex: He wavers when choosing between two jobs.
words.ex_cn: 他在两个工作之间摇摆不定。
words.en: If you waver, you cannot decide about something or you are uncertain about what you should do.

words.ex: He cringed when he heard the loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到巨大的噪音时，他畏缩了。
words.en: If you cringe at something, you feel embarrassed or disgusted, and perhaps show this feeling in your expression or by making a slight movement.

words.tr:
n. 顾虑；顾忌；踌躇
v. 顾虑；有顾忌
words.ex: He had a scruple about lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他对于对朋友撒谎感到不安。
words.en: A scruple is a feeling of doubt or hesitation with regard to the morality or propriety of a course of action.

words.tr: adj. 神秘的；不可思议的；
words.ex: The uncanny silence in the forest made him nervous.
words.ex_cn: 森林里那神秘的寂静让他感到紧张。
words.en: If you describe something as uncanny, you mean that it is strange and difficult to explain.

words.tr: adj. 异想天开的；古怪的；反复无常的
words.ex: The little girl wore a whimsical hat with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 小女孩戴着一顶带有花朵的古怪帽子。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as whimsical, you mean that they are unusual, playful, and unpredictable, often in a way that you find charming or amusing.

words.tr:
adj. 怪诞的；丑陋奇异的；奇形怪状的
n. 奇形怪状的东西；奇异风格
words.ex: The painting showed a grotesque face with twisted eyes.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画上有一个扭曲眼睛的怪诞面孔。
words.en: If you say that something is grotesque, you mean that it is extremely unattractive, exaggerated, and often shocking or disturbing.

words.ex: The eerie silence made us feel scared.
words.ex_cn: 那怪异的寂静让我们感到害怕。
words.en: If you describe something as eerie, you mean that it seems strange and frightening, and makes you feel nervous.

words.tr:
n. 怪诞行为；
adj. 不正常的；怪异的；
words.ex: His freak of wearing socks with sandals surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他穿袜子配凉鞋的怪诞行为让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A freak is a person who is considered to be unusual because of their behaviour or interests, or a sudden and unexpected event or situation.

words.ex: The ancient symbol remains an enigma.
words.ex_cn: 这个古代符号仍然是一个谜。
words.en: An enigma is something that is mysterious and difficult to understand.

words.tr: adj. 假的；伪造的；欺骗性的；谬误的
words.ex: The data is spurious and cannot be trusted.
words.ex_cn: 这些数据是虚假的，不可信。
words.en: Something that is spurious seems to be genuine, but is false.

words.ex: His argument is fallacious because it ignores the facts.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点是错误的，因为它忽略了事实。
words.en: If an idea, argument, or reason is fallacious, it is wrong because it is based on a fallacy.

words.tr:
n. 愚蠢的错误；失误
v. 犯愚蠢的错误；失误；跌跌撞撞地走
words.ex: He made a big blunder in the math test.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学考试中犯了一个大错误。
words.en: A blunder is a stupid or careless mistake.

words.tr:
n. 倒塌；崩溃；暴跌；
v. 倒塌；崩溃；
words.ex: The collapse of the old bridge caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥的倒塌引起了诸多问题。
words.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

words.ex: Everyone is fallible, even teachers.
words.ex_cn: 每个人都会犯错，即使是老师。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is fallible, you mean that they are not perfect and are likely to make mistakes or to fail in what they are doing.

words.tr: n. 流产；早产；误投；失败
words.ex: She had a miscarriage last month.
words.ex_cn: 她上个月流产了。
words.en: A miscarriage is the premature expulsion of a fetus from the womb before it is able to survive independently, or a failure to achieve the intended result of a plan or action.

words.ex: I misplace my keys every morning.
words.ex_cn: 我每天早上都把钥匙弄丢。
words.en: If you misplace something, you lose it, usually only temporarily.

words.ex: This lock is foolproof and easy to use.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁是万无一失的，而且容易使用。
words.en: A foolproof plan, system, or method is so well designed that it cannot go wrong or be used wrongly.

words.ex: The pope is considered infallible in matters of faith by some Catholics.
words.ex_cn: 一些天主教徒认为教皇在信仰问题上是一贯正确的。
words.en: If a person or thing is infallible, they are never wrong or never fail.

words.tr: v. 神化；把…奉若神明；崇拜
words.ex: They deify their ancient heroes.
words.ex_cn: 他们崇拜自己的古代英雄。
words.en: To treat someone or something as a god or goddess, or to consider them as if they were divine.

words.ex: They pray to sanctify the new home.
words.ex_cn: 他们祈祷来圣化这个新家。
words.en: To sanctify something means to make it holy or to purify it, often through a religious ceremony or blessing.

words.tr:
n. 熏香；熏香的烟
v. 使愤怒；激怒
words.ex: The smell of incense fills the room.
words.ex_cn: 香火的气味充满了房间。
words.en: Incense is a substance that is burned for its pleasant smell, often used in religious ceremonies. As a verb, to incense means to make someone very angry.

words.ex: He made an impious joke about the sacred temple.
words.ex_cn: 他对神圣的寺庙开了一个不敬的玩笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as impious, you mean that they show a lack of respect for religious practices or beliefs.

chapters.name: Part III 核心词汇 Lesson 21

words.ex: The temporal change of seasons affects our daily life.
words.ex_cn: 季节的时间变化影响我们的日常生活。
words.en: Relating to time as opposed to eternity; relating to worldly life as opposed to spiritual life.

words.ex: His daily routine is mundane and boring.
words.ex_cn: 他的日常生活平凡而无聊。
words.en: Something that is mundane is very ordinary and not at all interesting or unusual.

words.ex: The pastoral man tends his sheep on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 这位牧人在山上照看他的羊。
words.en: Relating to the countryside or to the work of a shepherd; idyllically rural.

words.tr:
n. 不可知论者
adj. 不可知论的
words.ex: He is agnostic about religion.
words.ex_cn: 他对宗教持不可知论态度。
words.en: An agnostic is someone who believes that it is not possible to know whether God exists or not.

words.ex: I am enclosing the documents herewith.
words.ex_cn: 我随信附上文件。
words.en: used in formal writing to introduce a document or to say that something is included with a letter

words.ex: I agree to the terms hereto.
words.ex_cn: 我同意此处的条款。
words.en: To this matter or document.

words.ex: Heretofore, he did not understand the problem.
words.ex_cn: 到目前为止，他不明白这个问题。
words.en: Up to this time; until now.

words.ex: The solution lies herein.
words.ex_cn: 解决方法就在这里。
words.en: in this place or thing, or in this document

words.ex: The contract is valid hereof.
words.ex_cn: 就此而言，合同是有效的。
words.en: of or concerning this; as a part of this

words.ex: Henceforth, I will wake up early.
words.ex_cn: 从今以后，我会早起。
words.en: From this time on; from now on.

words.tr:
adv. 从今以后；此后
n. 死后；来世
words.ex: Hereafter, he will work harder.
words.ex_cn: 从此以后，他会更加努力。
words.en: in the future; after this time

words.ex: I hereby declare my agreement.
words.ex_cn: 我据此声明我的同意。
words.en: You use hereby when you are making an official statement or declaration, or when you are formally stating something.

words.tr: adv. 与此；与之；随即；立即
words.ex: He signed the contract, therewith agreeing to the terms.
words.ex_cn: 他签署了合同，从而同意了条款。
words.en: Therewith is used to indicate that something happens immediately after something else or as a result of it.

words.ex: He went thereto without hesitation.
words.ex_cn: 他毫不犹豫地去了那里。
words.en: To that place, thing, or matter.

words.tr: adv. 在其中；在那里；在那一点上
words.ex: The document outlines the terms and conditions therein.
words.ex_cn: 该文件概述了其中的条款和条件。
words.en: In that place, matter, or respect.

words.ex: He lied, and thereupon he was punished.
words.ex_cn: 他撒了谎，因此受到了惩罚。
words.en: Immediately after that; as a result of that.

words.ex: It was raining, nonetheless, we went for a walk.
words.ex_cn: 天下着雨，尽管如此，我们还是去散步了。
words.en: Nonetheless is used to indicate that something is true or happens in spite of what has just been said.

words.ex: Notwithstanding the rain, they went for a walk.
words.ex_cn: 虽然下着雨，他们还是去散步了。
words.en: In spite of; although.

words.tr: adv. 由于；就此程度而言
words.ex: He was late, insomuch as he missed the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他迟到了，因为他没赶上公交车。
words.en: to such an extent that

words.tr: adv. 在这个范围；到这种程度
words.ex: I agree with you insofar as you want to help others.
words.ex_cn: 在你想帮助别人的范围内，我同意你。
words.en: to the degree or extent that

words.ex: The innermost part of the box was empty.
words.ex_cn: 盒子最内部是空的。
words.en: The innermost part of something is the part that is farthest from its edges or its surface.

words.tr: adj. 最后部的；在最后面的；“hind”的最高级
words.ex: The hindmost child in the line could not see the stage.
words.ex_cn: 队列最后面的孩子看不到舞台。
words.en: Situated at the very end; farthest back.

words.ex: He did an in-depth study of the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题进行了深入的研究。
words.en: If you do something in depth, you do it very thoroughly and consider all the details.

words.tr: adv. 末端向前；头尾相接
words.ex: The box fell endways on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 箱子侧着掉在了地上。
words.en: with the end foremost or toward the viewer

words.tr:
adj. 半开的；微启的
adv. 微开地；半开地
words.ex: The door was ajar so I pushed it open.
words.ex_cn: 门半开着，所以我推开了它。
words.en: If a door is ajar, it is slightly open.

words.ex: They walked abreast down the street.
words.ex_cn: 他们并肩走在街上。
words.en: If people or things are abreast, they are lined up next to each other, side by side, and often facing the same direction.

words.ex: He is at the forefront of new technology.
words.ex_cn: 他处于新技术的前沿。
words.en: The forefront is the most forward part of something, especially in a literal or metaphorical sense, indicating the leading position in a particular field or activity.

words.tr: n. 前景；最显著的位置；
words.ex: The trees in the foreground are very tall.
words.ex_cn: 前景中的树很高。
words.en: The part of a view that is nearest to the observer, especially in a picture or photograph; the most important or prominent position.

words.tr: v. 预先警告；事先告诫
words.ex: He forewarned us about the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他提前警告我们会有风暴。
words.en: If you forewarn someone about something, you warn them in advance that it is going to happen.

words.ex: The dark clouds forebode a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something forebodes a future event, it suggests that it is going to happen.

words.ex: The dark clouds foreshadow a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something foreshadows an event or situation, it suggests that it will happen.

words.ex: He had foreknowledge of the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他事先知道会有风暴。
words.en: Knowledge of something before it happens or exists.

words.ex: Her forethought in planning the event ensured its success.
words.ex_cn: 她在计划活动时的事先考虑确保了活动的成功。
words.en: If you use forethought, you think carefully before you do something in order to avoid problems or to make sure it is successful.

words.ex: The horse-drawn carriage was a forerunner of the car.
words.ex_cn: 马车是汽车的先驱。
words.en: A forerunner is someone or something that comes before another and is often considered as a sign of what is to follow.

words.ex: The dark clouds are a harbinger of storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云是暴风雨的预兆。
words.en: A harbinger is something that shows that something is going to happen soon, especially something bad.

words.ex: The movie provided a foretaste of what the sequel might bring.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影预示了续集可能会带来的内容。
words.en: A foretaste is a small experience of something before it happens, which makes you want to experience it more.

words.ex: She had a premonition that something bad was going to happen.
words.ex_cn: 她有一种不祥的预感，觉得会有坏事发生。
words.en: A premonition is a feeling that something, especially something unpleasant, is going to happen.

words.ex: He is farsighted and needs glasses to read books.
words.ex_cn: 他有远视，读书时需要戴眼镜。
words.en: Having the ability to anticipate and plan for the future; having good judgment about what will be needed in the future.

words.tr: adj. 有先见之明的；深谋远虑的
words.ex: He is a provident man who saves money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有远见的人，会为未来存钱。
words.en: Making provision for the future; exercising foresight or forethought.

words.ex: The old woman prophesied rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 那位老妇人预告明天会下雨。
words.en: To say that something will happen in the future, especially as a result of divine inspiration.

words.tr: adj. 意料之外的；未预见到的；
words.ex: The storm caused unforeseen damage to the town.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴给小镇造成了意料之外的破坏。
words.en: If something is unforeseen, it was not expected to happen or known about beforehand.

words.ex: His supposition is that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他的假设是明天会下雨。
words.en: A supposition is a guess or a theory that you have about something, which may not be true.

words.tr: v. 预先假定；预料；以…为先决条件
words.ex: He presupposes that everyone likes coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他假设每个人都喜欢咖啡。
words.en: If one thing presupposes another, the first thing cannot be true or exist unless the second thing is true or exists.

words.tr:
v. 假定；要求
n. 假定；假设
words.ex: He postulates that all humans are equal.
words.ex_cn: 他假定所有人都是平等的。
words.en: If you postulate something, you suggest it as the basis for a theory, argument, or calculation.

words.ex: His conjecture was that the missing key was in the drawer.
words.ex_cn: 他猜测丢失的钥匙在抽屉里。
words.en: A conjecture is a conclusion that is based on information that is not certain or complete.

words.ex: He extrapolates the trend from last year's data.
words.ex_cn: 他从去年的数据中推断出趋势。
words.en: To extrapolate is to estimate or conclude something by extending or projecting known information.

words.tr:
v. 回火；适得其反
n. 逆火
words.ex: The engine backfired when he pressed the gas pedal.
words.ex_cn: 当他踩下油门时，发动机回火了。
words.en: If a plan or project backfires, it has the opposite result to the one that was intended.

words.ex: He had a flashback to his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他突然想起了自己的童年。
words.en: A flashback is a scene in a movie, novel, etc., set in a time earlier than the main story.

words.tr:
n. 鼻烟；烛花
v. 用鼻子使劲吸；熄灭；断气
words.ex: He takes snuff every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都吸鼻烟。
words.en: Snuff is powdered tobacco that people take by sniffing it into their noses. It can also refer to the act of extinguishing a candle or the burnt part of a candle wick.

words.tr:
n. 烟蒂；铅笔头； 残根；票根
v. 碰到某物；捻灭（香烟）
words.ex: He picked up a stub from the ground.
words.ex_cn: 他从地上捡起一个烟蒂。
words.en: A stub is a short piece of something that remains after the rest of it has been used or removed, such as a cigarette stub or a ticket stub.

words.tr:
v. 征募；征召
n. 应征士兵
words.ex: He was conscripted into the army last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年被征召入伍。
words.en: To conscript someone means to make them join the armed forces of a country, especially in a time of war.

words.tr:
n. 起义者；叛乱者；造反者
adj. 叛乱的；起义的
words.ex: The insurgent attacked the village at night.
words.ex_cn: 叛乱分子在夜里袭击了村庄。
words.en: An insurgent is a person who rises in active revolt against an established authority or government.

words.ex: He left his watch as a pawn at the shop.
words.ex_cn: 他把手表当成了典当品放在店里。
words.en: To pawn something means to leave it with a pawnbroker, who lends you money in exchange. The pawnbroker keeps the item until you pay back the money plus interest.

words.tr:
n. 尖木桩；警戒哨；纠察队（队员）
v. 进行罢工纠察
words.ex: The fence has wooden pickets to keep animals out.
words.ex_cn: 这个围栏有木制尖木桩，用来防止动物进入。
words.en: A picket is a person or group of people who stand outside a place of work or other venue to protest or to try to persuade others not to enter during a strike. It can also refer to a pointed stake or post driven into the ground, typically to form a fence or to tether a horse.

words.tr:
adj. 被敌人围困的；严阵以待的
v. 列阵；严阵以待；整军备战；“embattle”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The embattled president gave a speech.
words.ex_cn: 这位饱受争议的总统发表了一次演讲。
words.en: If you describe a person, group, or organization as embattled, you mean that they are having a lot of problems or difficulties.

words.tr: n. 前锋；前卫；先头部队；先驱
words.ex: He is at the vanguard of new technology.
words.ex_cn: 他在新技术的前沿。
words.en: The vanguard is the leading part of an advancing military formation. It has a broader meaning, signifying the forefront of any movement or field.

words.tr:
n. 护送；护航；护卫
v. 护航；护送
words.ex: The army sent a convoy to protect the trucks.
words.ex_cn: 军队派出护送队保护卡车。
words.en: A convoy is a group of vehicles or ships traveling together, typically accompanied by armed troops, warships, or other vehicles for protection.

words.ex: The hero will vanquish the dragon.
words.ex_cn: 英雄将战胜龙。
words.en: To vanquish someone means to defeat them completely in a battle or a competition.

words.ex: Her talent trumped his experience.
words.ex_cn: 她的才华胜过了他的经验。
words.en: In card games, a trump is a card of a suit which has been chosen to rank above the other suits. As a verb, to trump means to beat someone or something by doing or producing something better.

words.tr: v. 压制；平息；消除；减轻
words.ex: The police tried to quell the riot.
words.ex_cn: 警察试图平息暴乱。
words.en: To quell something, especially a feeling, means to stop it or reduce its intensity.

words.ex: The court will quash the false order.
words.ex_cn: 法院将撤销这个虚假的命令。
words.en: If a court or someone in authority quashes a decision or judgment, they officially reject it and say that it is not valid.

words.ex: The team trounced their rivals in the final match.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍在决赛中大胜对手。
words.en: To defeat someone decisively in a competition or fight.

words.ex: He was beset by problems at work.
words.ex_cn: 他被工作中的问题困扰。
words.en: If someone or something is beset by problems or fears, they have many problems or fears which affect them severely.

words.ex: The soldiers were bombarded with cannon fire.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们遭到炮火轰击。
words.en: To bombard someone or something means to attack them continuously with bombs, shells, or other missiles. It can also mean to subject someone to a lot of something, such as questions or information.

words.tr:
v. 击退；回绝；憎恶
n. 拒斥；击退；严拒
words.ex: The soldiers repulse the enemy attack.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们击退了敌人的进攻。
words.en: If you repulse someone, you reject them or make them feel disgusted.

words.ex: He faced expulsion for breaking the school rules.
words.ex_cn: 他因违反校规而被开除。
words.en: Expulsion is the act of forcing someone to leave a place, especially a school or a country, as a punishment or because they are not wanted there.

words.ex: The landlord will evict the tenant for not paying rent.
words.ex_cn: 房东会因为租客不付房租而将他驱逐。
words.en: To evict someone means to force them to leave a house or piece of land, usually because they have not paid the rent or have broken the law.

words.ex: The team will oust the coach after the loss.
words.ex_cn: 球队在输球后将撤换教练。
words.en: If someone is ousted from a position of power, job, or place, they are forced to leave it.

words.ex: He reject the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这份工作邀请。
words.en: If you reject something such as a proposal, a request, or an offer, you do not accept it or you do not agree to it.

words.ex: He used a stick to dislodge the rock from the path.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根棍子把石头从路上移出。
words.en: To dislodge something means to remove it from a place where it is fixed or held.

words.tr: n. 被排斥者；被抛弃者；
words.ex: He became an outcast after speaking the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他因为说出真相而被排斥。
words.en: An outcast is someone who is not accepted by a group of people or by society.

words.tr: adj. 不可征服的；不能战胜的
words.ex: He felt invincible after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 赢得比赛后，他觉得自己不可战胜。
words.en: If someone or something is invincible, they are impossible to defeat or overcome.

words.ex: The language barrier was insuperable for him.
words.ex_cn: 语言障碍对他来说是难以克服的。
words.en: If you describe a problem or obstacle as insuperable, you mean that it is impossible to overcome.

words.tr: adj. 无法克服的；难以解决的；不可逾越的
words.ex: The problem seemed insurmountable.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题似乎无法克服。
words.en: If you describe something as insurmountable, you mean that it is so great or severe that it cannot be dealt with.

words.tr:
v. 使堕落；误用；歪曲；使走邪路
n. 堕落者；性变态者；色狼
words.ex: He tried to pervert the truth with lies.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用谎言歪曲真相。
words.en: If you pervert something, you change it from what it should be or what it was originally intended to be into something that is wrong or harmful.

words.ex: They tried to subvert the government.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图颠覆政府。
words.en: To subvert means to undermine the power and authority of an established system or institution.

words.tr:
adj. 颠覆性的；破坏性的
n. 颠覆分子；危险分子
words.ex: The subversive poster tried to break the government's rules.
words.ex_cn: 那张颠覆性的海报试图破坏政府的规则。
words.en: A subversive person or activity is one that is intended to weaken or destroy a political system or government.

words.ex: He contorts his face to make the kids laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他扭曲面部表情来逗孩子们笑。
words.en: If someone's face or body contorts or is contorted, it moves into an unnatural and unattractive shape or position.

words.tr:
v. 使翘棱；使扭曲变形
n. 弯曲；歪曲
words.ex: The heat will warp the metal.
words.ex_cn: 热量会使金属变形。
words.en: To warp is to bend or twist something out of its natural shape, often as a result of heat or moisture. It can also refer to the state of being bent or twisted.

words.ex: He forbears from yelling when he is angry.
words.ex_cn: 他生气时忍住不喊叫。
words.en: If you forbear from doing something, you do not do it although you have the opportunity or the right to do it.

chapters.name: Part III 核心词汇 Lesson 22

words.tr: v. 预先阻止；抢先一步
words.ex: He forestalls problems by planning ahead.
words.ex_cn: 他通过提前计划来防止问题。
words.en: To forestall something means to prevent it from happening or to act before someone else does in order to prevent them from doing something.

words.ex: The medicine helps inhibit pain.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物有助于抑制疼痛。
words.en: If something inhibits an event or process, it prevents it or slows it down.

words.tr:
v. 为 ... 上脚镣；束缚；限制
n. 脚镣；桎梏；束缚
words.ex: The prisoner was fettered with chains.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯被锁链束缚着。
words.en: A fetter is a chain or shackle for the feet, or something that confines or restrains.

words.tr:
n. 缰绳；驾驭；控制
v. 控制；驾驭
words.ex: He uses a leather rein to control the horse.
words.ex_cn: 他用皮缰绳来控制马。
words.en: A rein is a long, narrow strap attached at one end to a horse's bit, typically used in pairs to guide or check a horse while riding or driving.

words.tr:
n. 笼子；栏舍
v. 把…关起来
words.ex: The chickens live in a small coop.
words.ex_cn: 鸡住在小笼子里。
words.en: A coop is a cage or small building in which chickens are kept.

words.tr:
n. 马笼头；缰绳；约束
v. 套笼头；表示恼怒；抑制
words.ex: He pulled the bridle to stop the horse.
words.ex_cn: 他拉了一下缰绳让马停下来。
words.en: A bridle is a set of straps that fits around a horse's head and is used to control the horse. As a verb, to bridle means to put a bridle on a horse or to restrain or control something.

words.tr:
n. (从事某项活动的)规定期限
v. 吝惜；节省
words.ex: He did a short stint as a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他短暂地当过一段时间老师。
words.en: A stint is a fixed period of time during which someone does a particular job or activity.

words.tr: adj. 混乱的；杂乱的；失控的
words.ex: The project went haywire when the main contractor left.
words.ex_cn: 当主要承包商离开时，项目变得一团糟。
words.en: If something goes haywire, it stops working properly and becomes uncontrollable.

words.ex: The government decided to deregulate the airline industry.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定解除对航空业的管制。
words.en: To remove regulations or controls from something, especially an industry or sector.

words.ex: The bicycle's freewheel allows the rider to coast without pedaling.
words.ex_cn: 自行车上的自由飞轮使骑车人可以在不踩踏板的情况下滑行。
words.en: To freewheel means to move or operate freely without constraint or control, often implying a lack of concern for the consequences.

words.ex: He is a freelance graphic designer.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名自由职业的平面设计师。
words.en: A freelance person is someone who does particular pieces of work for different organizations, rather than working all the time for a single organization.

words.tr: adj. 死后的；死后出版的；遗腹的
words.ex: He received a posthumous award for his bravery.
words.ex_cn: 他因勇敢而被追授了奖项。
words.en: Posthumous means occurring, awarded, or appearing after the death of the originator.

words.ex: He tried to falsify the report.
words.ex_cn: 他试图篡改报告。
words.en: To falsify means to change something in order to deceive people, or to make a false statement.

words.tr: v. 拨弄；玩弄；篡改；收买
words.ex: Don't tamper with the machine.
words.ex_cn: 不要拨弄这台机器。
words.en: If someone tampers with something, they interfere with it or make unauthorized changes to it, often in order to cause damage or make it work differently.

words.ex: He tried to counterfeit money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图伪造货币。
words.en: Made in exact imitation of something valuable with the intention to deceive or defraud.

words.ex: The scientist tried to replicate the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家试图复制这个实验。
words.en: To replicate something means to do or make something again in exactly the same way.

words.ex: The email was bogus and tried to steal my password.
words.ex_cn: 这封邮件是假的，试图窃取我的密码。
words.en: If you describe something as bogus, you mean that it is not genuine, true, or real.

words.ex: The child mimics her mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子模仿她妈妈的声音。
words.en: If someone or something mimics another person or thing, they try to be like them or copy their behavior or characteristics.

words.ex: The game simulates real traffic conditions.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏模拟了真实的交通状况。
words.en: To simulate is to create a model or representation of a situation, process, or system for the purpose of study, analysis, or training. It involves imitating the conditions of a real event or environment to understand its effects or to practice responses to it.

words.ex: He feigns sleep to avoid talking.
words.ex_cn: 他假装睡觉以避免交谈。
words.en: If someone feigns a particular feeling, attitude, or physical condition, they try to make other people think that they have it or are experiencing it, although this is not true.

words.tr:
n. 化妆舞会；伪装
v. 伪装；冒充
words.ex: We went to a masquerade last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚去参加了一个化妆舞会。
words.en: A masquerade is a party or dance where people wear masks and costumes, or it refers to the act of pretending to be someone or something else.

words.ex: The soldier wore camouflage to hide in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 士兵穿着伪装服在森林中隐藏自己。
words.en: Camouflage is the way in which some animals are colored and shaped so that they cannot easily be seen in their natural surroundings.

words.tr:
n. 拙劣的模仿（作品）
v. 拙劣模仿
words.ex: The film is a parody of classic horror movies.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是对经典恐怖电影的滑稽模仿。
words.en: A parody is a humorous or satirical imitation of a serious piece of literature or writing.

words.ex: He spoke in the guise of a friend.
words.ex_cn: 他以朋友的伪装说话。
words.en: An external form, appearance, or manner of presentation, typically concealing the true nature of something.

words.ex: The government will expropriate the land for the new road.
words.ex_cn: 政府将征用这块土地用于新建道路。
words.en: If a government or other authority expropriates someone's property, they take it away from them for public use or benefit.

words.ex: The police impounded the stolen car.
words.ex_cn: 警察扣押了那辆被盗的汽车。
words.en: If something is impounded by police or other officials, they take it away because it is illegal or because it is evidence in a criminal case.

words.tr:
n. 没收物；罚金
v. 丧失；被没收
words.ex: He had to pay a forfeit for breaking the rule.
words.ex_cn: 他因违反规定不得不支付没收物。
words.en: If you forfeit something, you lose it or are forced to give it up because you have broken a rule or done something wrong.

words.tr:
v. 发劈啪声；发尖而轻的爆裂声
n. 劈啪响；裂纹
words.ex: The fire crackles in the hearth.
words.ex_cn: 壁炉里的火噼啪作响。
words.en: If something crackles, it makes a rapid series of short, sharp noises.

words.tr:
v. 咯咯叫；咯咯地笑
n. 咯咯叫声；咯咯的笑声
words.ex: The witches cackle in the dark forest.
words.ex_cn: 女巫们在黑暗的森林里咯咯大笑。
words.en: If someone cackles, they laugh in a loud, unpleasant way, especially at something wicked or cruel.

words.tr:
n. 咯吱声或叽嘎声
v. 发出咯吱声或叽嘎声
words.ex: The door creaked when he opened it.
words.ex_cn: 他开门时，门发出了吱呀声。
words.en: If something creaks, it makes a short, high-pitched sound when it moves.

words.tr:
v. 嘶嘶地冒泡；发出嘶嘶声
n. 嘶嘶声；气泡；起泡饮料（尤指香槟）
words.ex: The soda began to fizz as soon as it was opened.
words.ex_cn: 苏打水一打开就开始起泡。
words.en: To fizz means to make a hissing or bubbling sound.

words.tr:
v. 发出（油煎食物的）咝咝声
n. 咝咝声
words.ex: The bacon sizzle in the pan.
words.ex_cn: 培根在平底锅里滋滋作响。
words.en: If something sizzles, it makes a sound like the sound that hot oil makes when you put food into it, or like the sound of water falling onto a hot surface.

words.tr:
v. 滴嗒地响；发出急速轻拍声
n. （急促的）啪嗒声；急速的轻拍声
words.ex: The rain patters on the roof.
words.ex_cn: 雨滴嗒地响在屋顶上。
words.en: If something patters, it makes a series of quick, light, tapping sounds.

words.tr:
n. 哔哔声
v. 发哔哔声
words.ex: The machine bleeped when the button was pressed.
words.ex_cn: 当按钮被按下时，机器发出了哔哔声。
words.en: A bleep is a short high-pitched sound, especially one that is made by an electronic device.

words.tr:
v. （使）发出沙沙；偷窃（牲口）
n. 沙沙声；瑟瑟声
words.ex: The wind rustled the leaves.
words.ex_cn: 风使树叶发出沙沙声。
words.en: If something rustles, it makes soft sounds as it moves lightly and gently, for example through the air or over dry leaves.

words.tr:
v. 汩汩地流；作咯咯声
n. 汩汩声；咯咯声
words.ex: The stream gurgles over the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 小溪在石头上汩汩流淌。
words.en: To make a bubbling sound, typically as a result of liquid flowing irregularly or of a person making a similar sound.

words.tr:
n. 叮当声；广告歌
v. （使）发出叮当声
words.ex: The bells make a happy jingle in winter.
words.ex_cn: 冬天里，铃铛发出愉快的叮当声。
words.en: A jingle is a short, simple tune, often with words, that is used to advertise a product or service on the radio or television.

words.tr:
n. 隆隆声；辘辘声
v. 隆隆作响；辘辘行驶
words.ex: The dog let out a low rumble.
words.ex_cn: 狗发出了一声低沉的咆哮。
words.en: To make a continuous deep, resonant sound; to speak in a low, deep voice.

words.tr:
v. 发出（响亮而刺耳的声音）
n. 响亮刺耳的声音
words.ex: The car alarm blares loudly at night.
words.ex_cn: 汽车警报在夜里大声响着。
words.en: If something such as a siren or radio blares or if you blare it, it makes a loud, unpleasant noise.

words.tr:
n. 长声尖叫；长而尖的声音
v. 尖声长叫
words.ex: The child let out a loud squeal when she saw the spider.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子看到蜘蛛时，发出了一声长长的尖叫。
words.en: If someone or something squeals, they make a long, high-pitched sound.

words.tr:
n. 吱吱声；尖叫声
v. 短促而尖厉地叫；吱吱叫
words.ex: The mouse makes a small squeak.
words.ex_cn: 老鼠发出一声小小的吱吱声。
words.en: If something or someone squeaks, they make a short, high-pitched sound.

words.tr:
n. 尖叫声；尖锐的声音
v. 发出尖锐刺耳的声音
words.ex: The cat let out a loud screech.
words.ex_cn: 猫发出了一声尖叫声。
words.en: If a vehicle screeches, its wheels make a high-pitched noise as it moves along or stops.

words.tr:
v. 咯咯地叫；大声抱怨
n. 刺耳的叫声；大声抱怨
words.ex: The parrot squawked loudly when it saw the visitor.
words.ex_cn: 鹦鹉看到访客时咯咯地叫了起来。
words.en: To squawk means to make a loud, harsh noise, often used to describe the sound made by birds. It can also mean to complain loudly or protest about something.

words.tr:
n. 颤声；颤音；啭鸣
v. 发颤声；啭鸣；发短促的响声
words.ex: The bird sang a beautiful trill.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿唱出了一段优美的颤声。
words.en: A trill is a musical effect where a note is alternated rapidly with the note above it.

words.tr:
n. 猫头鹰叫声；汽笛响声；叫嚣声
v. 作猫头鹰叫声；汽笛等嘟嘟响；大声叫嚣
words.ex: The hoot of an owl echoed through the night.
words.ex_cn: 猫头鹰的叫声在夜晚回荡。
words.en: To make the sound that an owl makes, or to make a similar sound as a signal or in disapproval.

words.tr:
n. 雁叫声；汽车喇叭声
v. （使汽车喇叭）鸣响；（雁）叫
words.ex: The honk of the geese echoed over the lake.
words.ex_cn: 大雁的叫声在湖面上回荡。
words.en: 1. The sound made by a car horn. 2. The cry of a goose. 3. To make a sound like a car horn or a goose.

words.ex: The bird made a soft chirp in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在早晨发出轻柔的唧唧声。
words.en: If a bird or an insect chirps, it makes short high-pitched sounds.

words.tr:
n. 嘘声；不满之声
v. 发嘘声
words.ex: The audience started catcalling when the speaker made a controversial statement.
words.ex_cn: 当演讲者发表有争议的言论时，观众开始发出嘘声。
words.en: A catcall is a loud whistle or a comment shouted by someone in a crowd, usually expressing disapproval or mockery.

words.tr:
int. 呸；嘘
n. 嘘声
v. 发出嘘声
words.ex: The crowd gave a loud boo when the player missed the goal.
words.ex_cn: 当球员错失进球时，观众发出了大声的嘘声。
words.en: If you boo a speaker or performer, you shout 'boo' or make other loud sounds to indicate that you do not like them, their opinions, or their performance.

words.tr:
v. 鸣；敲；报时
n. 铃声；钟声
words.ex: The clock chimes at noon.
words.ex_cn: 钟在正午报时。
words.en: To make a ringing sound, especially a bell, or to be in agreement.

words.tr: v. 置于某物之上；添加
words.ex: He superimposes a map on the photo.
words.ex_cn: 他把地图叠加在照片上。
words.en: To superimpose something means to place or lay one thing over another, typically so that both are still evident.

words.ex: He juxtaposes old photos with new ones.
words.ex_cn: 他把老照片和新照片放在一起。
words.en: To place or deal with close together for contrasting effect.

words.ex: Cats and dogs can coexist in the same house.
words.ex_cn: 猫和狗可以在同一个房子里共存。
words.en: To exist together at the same time or in the same place.

words.tr: v. 使（尤指不好的情形、体系、信仰）持续、长存；
words.ex: The system perpetuates inequality among the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这个体系使贫困人群的不平等持续存在。
words.en: To perpetuate something means to cause it to continue, especially for a long time.

words.ex: He has an abiding love for music.
words.ex_cn: 他对音乐有着持久的热爱。
words.en: If you have an abiding feeling for someone or something, you have a feeling that lasts for a long time.

words.ex: The game has a cyclic pattern of wins and losses.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏有输赢循环的模式。
words.en: Something that is cyclic happens in cycles or regularly repeats.

words.ex: The economy has a cyclical pattern of growth and decline.
words.ex_cn: 经济有增长和衰退的周期性模式。
words.en: Relating to or occurring in cycles; regularly repeated.

words.ex: The joy was transient, like a brief smile.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是短暂的，像一个短暂的微笑。
words.en: If you describe something as transient, you mean that it lasts only for a short time.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的； v. “fleet”的现在分词；
words.ex: The smile was fleeting.
words.ex_cn: 那个微笑是短暂的。
words.en: If you describe something as fleeting, you mean that it lasts only for a very short time.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的；瞬间的；刹那间的
words.ex: The light made a momentary flash.
words.ex_cn: 灯光闪了一下，但只持续了一瞬间。
words.en: lasting for a very short time

words.tr: adj. 短暂的；朝生暮死的
words.ex: The flowers are ephemeral and last only one day.
words.ex_cn: 这些花是短暂的，只持续一天。
words.en: Something that is ephemeral lasts for only a very short time.

words.tr: adj. 很快消失的；渐消散的；短暂的
words.ex: The evanescent mist disappeared at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 那消散的薄雾在日出时消失了。
words.en: Something that is evanescent quickly disappears or fades away.

words.ex: He fell into oblivion after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故后，他被遗忘了。
words.en: A state of being forgotten or unknown.

words.ex: He bought a flower in remembrance of his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一朵花以纪念他的母亲。
words.en: The act of remembering something or someone, or a memory of someone or something.

words.ex: He equates success with happiness.
words.ex_cn: 他把成功等同于幸福。
words.en: To consider one thing to be the same as or equal to another thing.

words.ex: The judge made an equitable decision.
words.ex_cn: 法官做出了一个公平的决定。
words.en: Fair and impartial; treating everyone equally.

words.tr: adj. 公正的；不偏不倚的；
words.ex: The judge was impartial in the trial.
words.ex_cn: 法官在审判中是公正的。
words.en: Someone who is impartial is not directly involved in a particular situation, and is therefore able to give a fair opinion or decision about it.

words.ex: The judge was disinterested in the case.
words.ex_cn: 法官对这个案件持客观态度。
words.en: If someone is disinterested in something, they have no personal involvement or investment in it and are therefore able to judge it fairly.

words.ex: His salary is commensurate with his experience.
words.ex_cn: 他的薪水与他的经验相称。
words.en: If the level of one thing is commensurate with another, the first level is in proportion to the second.

words.tr: adj. 同等的；相等的；相当于
words.ex: Lying is tantamount to cheating.
words.ex_cn: 撒谎等于欺骗。
words.en: If you say that one thing is tantamount to a second, more serious thing, you are emphasizing how bad, unacceptable, or unfortunate the first thing is by comparing it to the second.

words.tr:
n. 一双；一对；
v. （使）配对；
words.ex: He bought a pair of shoes for his son.
words.ex_cn: 他为儿子买了一双鞋。
words.en: A pair of things are two things of the same size and shape that are intended to be used together, or that are regarded as a unit.

words.ex: The meeting will adjourn at 5 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 会议将在下午5点休会。
words.en: If a meeting or trial is adjourned, or if it adjourns, it is stopped for a short time.

words.tr:
v. 中止；中断；放弃；堕（胎）
n. 中止计划
words.ex: He decided to abort the mission because it was too dangerous.
words.ex_cn: 他决定中止任务，因为太危险了。
words.en: If an unborn baby is aborted, the pregnancy is ended deliberately and the baby is not born alive.

words.tr: v. 到达…的顶点；达到高潮；告终
words.ex: The concert culminated with a loud fireworks show.
words.ex_cn: 音乐会以一场响亮的烟花表演结束。
words.en: If an event or series of events culminates in something, it ends with it, having developed until it reaches this point.

words.tr: adj. 断断续续的；一阵阵的
words.ex: He had fitful sleep last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚睡得断断续续。
words.en: Something that is fitful happens for irregular periods of time or occurs at irregular times, rather than being continuous.

words.tr:
adj. 不停的；直达的；
adv. 不停地；直达地；
words.ex: The train makes a nonstop journey from Beijing to Shanghai.
words.ex_cn: 这列火车从北京到上海是不停站的。
words.en: If something is nonstop, it continues without any pauses or interruptions.

words.tr: adj. 不断的；不停的；连续的
words.ex: The baby cried with incessant noise.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿不停地哭闹。
words.en: If you say that something is incessant, you are emphasizing that it continues without stopping.

words.tr: n. 名人；要人；人物；角色
words.ex: The personage gave a speech at the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 这位人物在仪式上发表了演讲。
words.en: A personage is a person, especially someone who is famous or important in some way.

words.ex: The hero in the story is an archetype of courage.
words.ex_cn: 故事中的英雄是勇气的原型。
words.en: An archetype is a very typical example of a certain person or thing.

words.ex: She is the quintessence of grace.
words.ex_cn: 她是优雅的典范。
words.en: The quintessence of something is the most perfect or typical example of it.

words.ex: He gave a synopsis of the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他简要介绍了这部电影。
words.en: A synopsis is a brief summary or general survey of something.

chapters.name: Part III 核心词汇 Lesson 23

words.tr: n. 可能发生的情况；设想；
words.ex: It's a possible scenario that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天会下雨是一个可能发生的情况。
words.en: A scenario is a description of a possible course of action or events.

words.ex: He performed a mime on the street.
words.ex_cn: 他在街上表演了哑剧。
words.en: A mime is a form of performance art where the performer uses gestures and movements without speech to convey a story or emotion. As a verb, to mime means to imitate or mimic actions or expressions without using words.

words.tr: v. 起绰号；把…称作；配音；译制
words.ex: They dubbed him 'Captain Cool' for his calm style.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他冷静的风格给他起了个绰号叫‘冷静队长’。
words.en: To give a name, title, or nickname to someone or something; to provide a film or television program with a soundtrack in a different language from the original.

words.tr:
n. 候补演员
v. 练习当候补演员
words.ex: He is the understudy for the main actor.
words.ex_cn: 他是主角的替补演员。
words.en: An understudy is an actor who learns the part of another actor in a play so that they can take their place if necessary.

words.ex: The movie's premiere was held last night.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的首映昨晚举行。
words.en: The first public performance of a play, film, or other form of entertainment.

words.ex: The book begins with a short prologue.
words.ex_cn: 这本书以一个简短的序言开始。
words.en: A prologue is an introduction to a book, play, or other written work that sets the scene or provides background information.

words.tr:
n. 亲笔签名；亲笔稿
v. 亲笔签名于；亲笔书写
words.ex: He asked the singer for an autograph.
words.ex_cn: 他向歌手要了一张签名。
words.en: An autograph is a person's own signature, especially that of a famous person, or a manuscript in the author's own handwriting.

words.tr:
v. 乱写；乱画；涂鸦
n. 乱画；乱写；涂鸦
words.ex: He doodled on his notebook during class.
words.ex_cn: 他在上课时在笔记本上乱画。
words.en: If you doodle, you draw small, simple pictures or patterns on a piece of paper, often while you are thinking about something else.

words.tr:
v. 潦草地写；涂写
n. 潦草的笔迹
words.ex: He scrawled his name on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在纸上潦草地写了自己的名字。
words.en: If you scrawl something, you write it in a careless and untidy way.

words.tr:
adj. 逐字的；一字不差的
adv. 逐字地；一字不差地
words.ex: He repeated the words verbatim.
words.ex_cn: 他一字不差地重复了那些话。
words.en: Using exactly the same words as were used originally.

words.ex: The handwriting is legible and easy to read.
words.ex_cn: 字迹清晰，容易辨认。
words.en: If writing or print is legible, it is clear enough to read.

words.tr: adj. 该诅咒的；恶劣的；极坏的
words.ex: The food was execrable.
words.ex_cn: 这食物糟糕透顶。
words.en: If you describe something as execrable, you mean that it is extremely bad or unpleasant.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊其词的；难以解释的
words.ex: His answer was equivocal.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可。
words.en: If you are equivocal, you are deliberately vague in what you say, because you want to avoid speaking the truth or making a decision.

words.ex: He accepted a nominal fee for the service.
words.ex_cn: 他为这项服务收取了微不足道的费用。
words.en: If you say that something is nominal, you mean that it is very small in comparison to the real value or importance of something.

words.ex: The committee decided to denominate the new park 'Green Haven.'
words.ex_cn: 委员会决定将新公园命名为'绿洲'。
words.en: To give a name to something or someone, often in a formal or official way.

words.tr: v. 给…洗礼；施洗礼时命名；开始使用
words.ex: They will christen the new ship tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天将为这艘新船命名。
words.en: To christen someone means to give them a name at a Christian baptism ceremony, or to give a name to something in a ceremony that is not religious.

words.ex: The scandal brought the company into disrepute.
words.ex_cn: 这起丑闻使该公司声名狼藉。
words.en: If someone or something is in disrepute, they have a bad reputation because people think they have done something bad or wrong.

words.tr: v. 置于…之间；插入；插嘴；介入
words.ex: The mediator tried to interpose before the situation escalated.
words.ex_cn: 调解人试图在局势升级之前进行干预。
words.en: If you interpose something between two people or things, you place it between them. If you interpose, you interrupt with a comment or question.

words.ex: He interjected during the meeting to ask a question.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议中插话问了一个问题。
words.en: To say something that interrupts someone who is speaking.

words.tr: n. 间歇；插曲；幕间节目
words.ex: He took an interlude to drink water.
words.ex_cn: 他休息了一下喝水。
words.en: An interlude is a short period of time that comes in the middle of something, or a short piece of music, talk, or entertainment that comes between the main parts of a performance or event.

words.ex: The interplay between light and shadow creates beauty.
words.ex_cn: 光与影的相互作用创造了美。
words.en: The way in which two or more things have an effect on each other.

words.ex: The phone has a simple interface.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一个简单的界面。
words.en: An interface is a point where two systems, subjects, organizations, etc. meet and interact.

words.ex: He adulterates milk with water to make more money.
words.ex_cn: 他往牛奶里加水以赚更多钱。
words.en: To make something poorer in quality by adding another substance to it.

words.tr:
v. 使混乱；使杂乱
n. 杂乱；混乱
words.ex: He jumbled the letters and could not read the word.
words.ex_cn: 他把字母弄乱了，无法认出这个单词。
words.en: To mix things together in a confused or untidy way.

words.ex: The cat got entangled in the string.
words.ex_cn: 猫被绳子缠住了。
words.en: If something is entangled in something else, it is caught or twisted around it, or mixed with it so that it is difficult to separate the two things.

words.ex: She wreathe the flowers around the door.
words.ex_cn: 她把花缠绕在门周围。
words.en: To twist or entwine something around something else, often in a decorative manner.

words.ex: He bought some miscellaneous items at the store.
words.ex_cn: 他在商店里买了一些各种各样的东西。
words.en: Consisting of a variety of ingredients or parts.

words.tr: adj. 异种的；异质的；由不同成份形成的
words.ex: The class is heterogeneous, with students from many countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级是多元的，有来自许多国家的学生。
words.en: A heterogeneous group consists of many different types of things or people.

words.tr:
adj. 杂色的；混杂的
n. 杂色；混杂
words.ex: The motley crowd cheered at the parade.
words.ex_cn: 这群杂乱的人群在游行中欢呼。
words.en: If you describe a group of things or people as motley, you mean that they are very different from each other and do not seem to belong together.

words.ex: He arranged the books in a haphazard way.
words.ex_cn: 他随意地摆放了书。
words.en: If you describe something as haphazard, you are critical of it because it is not at all organized or is not arranged according to a plan.

words.ex: Her terse reply left no room for further discussion.
words.ex_cn: 她简洁的回答没有留下进一步讨论的余地。
words.en: A terse statement or comment is brief and to the point, often seeming rude or unfriendly because of its brevity.

words.tr: adj. 轻率的；肤浅的；易做到的
words.ex: He gave a facile answer to the hard question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个难题给出了一个简单的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone's arguments or suggestions as facile, you are criticizing them because their ideas are too simple and indicate a lack of careful, intelligent thinking.

words.ex: The glass is translucent, so you can see light through it.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃是半透明的，所以你能看到光透过它。
words.en: If a material or substance is translucent, it is almost transparent, allowing some light to pass through it but not detailed shapes.

words.tr: adj. 不透明的；难懂的；晦涩的
words.ex: The glass is opaque, so I cannot see through it.
words.ex_cn: 这扇玻璃是不透明的，所以我看不到它后面的东西。
words.en: If an object or substance is opaque, you cannot see through it.

words.tr:
adj. 化身的；人体化的
v. 化身为；体现
words.ex: He is the incarnate form of justice.
words.ex_cn: 他是正义的化身。
words.en: If you say that someone is a quality incarnate, you mean that they represent that quality or are typical of it in an extreme form.

words.tr: v. 成为现实；成有形；实现；现身
words.ex: The dream did not materialize.
words.ex_cn: 这个梦想没有实现。
words.en: To materialize means to become actual fact; to happen or to appear in physical form.

words.tr: v.  系统化；图形化；扼要表示
words.ex: The professor tried to schematize the complex process for his students.
words.ex_cn: 教授试图为学生们系统化复杂的流程。
words.en: To arrange or represent something according to a plan, system, or scheme.

words.ex: This rule pertains to all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: If one thing pertains to another, it relates, belongs, or applies to it.

words.ex: His answer was pertinent to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答与问题相关。
words.en: Something that is pertinent is relevant to a particular subject.

words.ex: The extraneous noise made it hard to concentrate.
words.ex_cn: 那些无关的噪音让人难以集中注意力。
words.en: Something that is extraneous is not relevant or essential to the subject you are dealing with.

words.ex: This color befits the room.
words.ex_cn: 这个颜色适合这个房间。
words.en: To be suitable or appropriate for someone or something.

words.tr: n. 不适合的东西；不适应环境的人
words.ex: That old chair is a misfit in the new room.
words.ex_cn: 那把旧椅子在这个新房间里格格不入。
words.en: A misfit is a person who is not suited to a situation or who does not fit in well with the other people in a group.

words.ex: Her resilience helped her recover after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 她的复原力帮助她在事故后恢复。
words.en: The capacity to recover quickly from difficulties; toughness.

words.ex: His answer was apposite to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答与问题很贴切。
words.en: Something that is apposite is suitable for or appropriate to what is happening or being discussed.

words.tr:
n. 权宜之计；应急办法
adj. 权宜的
words.ex: Closing the factory was an expedient to save money.
words.ex_cn: 关闭工厂是为了省钱的权宜之计。
words.en: An expedient action or solution to a problem is one that is convenient or practical, although it may not be morally right.

words.tr: adj. 符合礼仪的；得体的；高雅的
words.ex: She behaved in a decorous way at the dinner party.
words.ex_cn: 她在晚宴上举止得体。
words.en: If you say that something is decorous, you mean that it is dignified, proper, and socially acceptable.

words.tr: adj. 不恰当的；不得体的；无吸引力的
words.ex: It is unbecoming to shout at teachers.
words.ex_cn: 对老师大喊大叫是不合适的。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour or remarks as unbecoming, you mean that they are shocking and unsuitable for that person.

words.tr: adj. 权宜的；临时凑合的；
words.ex: He used a makeshift table made of boxes and a board.
words.ex_cn: 他用箱子和木板做了一个权宜的桌子。
words.en: A makeshift object or arrangement is one that is made or done quickly and without much skill, using whatever is available at the time.

words.tr:
adj. 代理的；代用的
n. 代理人；代用品
words.ex: He acted as a surrogate father to the child.
words.ex_cn: 他作为孩子的代理父亲。
words.en: A surrogate is a person or thing that takes the place of or acts for another, especially in a role or function that is typically filled by someone else.

words.ex: He paid in lieu of cash.
words.ex_cn: 他用其他方式支付而不是现金。
words.en: If you do, get, or give one thing in lieu of another, you do, get, or give it instead of the other thing, because the two things are considered to have the same value or importance.

words.ex: The cows trample the grass in the field.
words.ex_cn: 牛在田野里践踏草地。
words.en: If someone tramples something or tramples on it, they step heavily and carelessly on it and damage it.

words.ex: The stain on the carpet is a mar.
words.ex_cn: 地毯上的污渍是一个污点。
words.en: To mar something means to spoil or damage it.

words.ex: The heat made the metal deform.
words.ex_cn: 热量使金属变形。
words.en: To deform something means to change its shape, usually in a way that makes it less attractive or useful.

words.tr: v. 损伤…的外观；在…上乱涂乱画
words.ex: They deface the wall with graffiti.
words.ex_cn: 他们用涂鸦破坏了墙壁。
words.en: To deface something means to spoil its appearance by writing or drawing on it, or by damaging it in some other way.

words.tr:
v. （使）磨损；（使）烦躁；（使）紧张
n. 磨损处；吵闹；争吵
words.ex: The rope began to fray after years of use.
words.ex_cn: 这根绳子用了多年后开始磨损。
words.en: If something such as cloth or rope frays, or if something frays it, its threads or fibres start to come apart from each other and it becomes weaker. A situation of conflict or intense competition can also be referred to as a fray.

words.ex: The apple will decompose in the soil.
words.ex_cn: 苹果会在土壤中分解。
words.en: If something decomposes, or if it is decomposed, it decays or breaks down into smaller parts or substances.

words.tr: adj. 锯齿状的； v. “jag”的过去式；
words.ex: The jagged edge of the rock cut his hand.
words.ex_cn: 岩石的锯齿状边缘割伤了他的手。
words.en: Something that is jagged has a rough, uneven shape or edge with lots of sharp points.

words.ex: He got edgy when the train was late.
words.ex_cn: 当火车晚点时，他变得急躁了。
words.en: If someone is edgy, they are nervous and anxious, and likely to become easily upset or angry.

words.ex: Her strident voice broke the silence.
words.ex_cn: 她尖锐的声音打破了寂静。
words.en: If you use strident to describe someone or the way they express themselves, you mean that they make their feelings or opinions known in a very strong way that perhaps makes people uncomfortable.

words.ex: He is greedy and always wants more candy.
words.ex_cn: 他很贪婪，总是想要更多的糖果。
words.en: If you describe someone as greedy, you mean that they want to have more of something such as food or money than is necessary or fair.

words.ex: A flurry of snow covered the streets last night.
words.ex_cn: 昨晚一阵风雪覆盖了街道。
words.en: A flurry is a sudden, short period of activity, emotion, or excitement, often accompanied by confusion or haste.

words.tr:
n. 狂风；暴风雪；大喊大叫
v. 狂风吹袭；哇哇地叫嚷
words.ex: A sudden squall knocked over the small boat.
words.ex_cn: 一阵突如其来的狂风掀翻了小船。
words.en: A squall is a sudden, violent gust of wind or a localized storm, especially one bringing rain, snow, or sleet. It can also refer to a loud, harsh cry or scream.

words.ex: The water forms a vortex down the drain.
words.ex_cn: 水在排水口形成一个漩涡。
words.en: A vortex is a mass of wind or water that spins around very fast and pulls objects into its empty center.

words.tr:
n. 大洪水；暴雨；泛滥
v. 泛滥；大量涌入
words.ex: The rain caused a deluge in the town.
words.ex_cn: 这场雨在镇上引发了洪水。
words.en: A deluge is a severe flood or a very heavy fall of rain that causes a lot of damage.

words.ex: A cascade of complaints flooded the office.
words.ex_cn: 大量投诉涌进了办公室。
words.en: A cascade is a small waterfall or a series of small waterfalls. As a verb, it means to flow or fall in or like a cascade.

words.tr:
v. 旋动；（使）成漩涡；盘旋
n. 漩涡；涡状形
words.ex: The milk swirls in the coffee.
words.ex_cn: 牛奶在咖啡里旋转。
words.en: If something swirls or if you swirl it, it moves around and around quickly.

words.tr:
n. 漩涡；涡流
v. 起漩涡；旋转；杂乱无章地移动
words.ex: The river has a small eddy near the rock.
words.ex_cn: 河里石头附近有一个小漩涡。
words.en: An eddy is a circular movement of water, air, or smoke that is different from the main current.

words.ex: The sea was choppy, making it difficult to sail.
words.ex_cn: 海面波涛汹涌，使得航行变得困难。
words.en: If the sea or a river is choppy, the water moves in a lot of small waves because it is windy or because the current is strong.

words.tr:
v. 使波动；使起伏
adj. 波动的；起伏的
words.ex: The hills undulate gently in the distance.
words.ex_cn: 远处的山丘轻轻起伏。
words.en: To move or cause to move in a smooth, wavelike motion.

words.tr:
n. 折痕；皱痕
v. 起皱；弄皱
words.ex: The paper has a deep crease from folding.
words.ex_cn: 这张纸因为折叠而有一道深深的折痕。
words.en: A crease is a line or mark made on cloth or paper when it is folded or crushed.

words.ex: He crinkled the paper in his hand.
words.ex_cn: 他用手把纸捏皱了。
words.en: If something crinkles or if you crinkle it, it becomes slightly creased or folded.

words.tr:
adj. 缩成皱纹的；使起波状的
v. （使）起皱褶；“corrugate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The box is made of corrugated cardboard.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子是由波纹纸板制成的。
words.en: Something that is corrugated has parallel rows of folds that look like a series of waves when viewed from the edge.

words.tr:
v. （使）倾斜；（使）偏向
n. 倾斜；企图
words.ex: The boy tilt the cup and spill the water.
words.ex_cn: 男孩把杯子倾斜，水洒了出来。
words.en: If you tilt an object or if it tilts, it moves into a sloping position with one end or side higher than the other.

words.tr: adj. 想复仇的；报复性的；怀恨的
words.ex: He was vindictive and refused to forgive her.
words.ex_cn: 他心怀报复，拒绝原谅她。
words.en: If you say that someone is vindictive, you are critical of them because they deliberately try to upset or cause trouble for someone who they think has done them harm.

words.ex: He wanted vengeance after his brother was hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他哥哥被伤害后，他想要报复。
words.en: Vengeance is the act of doing something harmful or unpleasant to someone because they have done something harmful or unpleasant to you.

words.tr: adj. 不能和解的；不能平息的
words.ex: He is an implacable enemy who never forgives.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个永不原谅的不可调和的敌人。
words.en: If you say that someone is implacable, you mean that they have very strong feelings of hostility or disapproval which nobody can change.

words.ex: A fleck of paint fell on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 一小片油漆掉在了地上。
words.en: A fleck is a small mark or spot, especially one that is different in color or texture from the area around it.

words.tr:
n. 污染；腐坏；玷污
v. 污染；使腐坏；玷污
words.ex: The water has a taint from the factory waste.
words.ex_cn: 这种水因工厂废料而受到污染。
words.en: If something is tainted, it is affected by something bad or undesirable.

chapters.name: Part III 核心词汇 Lesson 24

words.tr:
n. 瑕疵；污点；缺点
v. 玷污；损害
words.ex: The apple has a small blemish on its skin.
words.ex_cn: 这个苹果的表皮上有一个小瑕疵。
words.en: A blemish is a small mark or flaw that spoils the appearance of something.

words.ex: He sullied his reputation by lying.
words.ex_cn: 他通过撒谎玷污了自己的声誉。
words.en: To sully something means to spoil or reduce the value of something, especially someone's reputation or the purity of something.

words.tr:
v. 弄脏；亵渎；玷污
n. 小道；狭谷
words.ex: They defile the river with trash.
words.ex_cn: 他们用垃圾污染了这条河。
words.en: To defile something means to make it dirty or impure. As a noun, it refers to a narrow pass or gorge between mountains.

words.tr: adj. 质地薄的；肮脏的；低劣的
words.ex: The sleazy curtain let in too much light.
words.ex_cn: 那层薄薄的窗帘透进了太多光。
words.en: If you describe something as sleazy, you mean that it is of low quality or morally questionable, especially because it is associated with sex or crime.

words.tr: adj. 又黑又脏的；昏暗的；肮脏的
words.ex: The room was dingy and small.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间又脏又小。
words.en: If you describe a place or thing as dingy, you mean that it is rather dull and depressing to look at, and perhaps also dirty.

words.ex: He uses soap to cleanse his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他用肥皂洗手。
words.en: To cleanse something means to make it extremely clean, especially by using a special substance or process.

words.tr: adj. 贞洁的；忠贞的；朴素的
words.ex: She remained chaste despite the pressure.
words.ex_cn: 尽管有压力，她依然保持贞洁。
words.en: If you describe someone as chaste, you mean that they do not have sex with anyone, or they only have sex with their husband or wife.

words.tr:
v. 轻咬；啃；一点点地吃
n. 一小口；轻咬；少量
words.ex: The dog nibble the biscuit slowly.
words.ex_cn: 狗慢慢地轻咬着饼干。
words.en: To nibble means to take small bites of something, especially food.

words.ex: He imbibes coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都喝咖啡。
words.en: To imbibe means to drink, especially alcohol, or to absorb or take in something, such as knowledge or ideas.

words.tr:
n. 虹吸管
v. 用虹吸管吸；抽取；挪用
words.ex: He used a siphon to transfer gasoline from one tank to another.
words.ex_cn: 他用虹吸管将汽油从一个油箱输送到另一个油箱。
words.en: A siphon is a tube that is used to move liquids from one container to another at a lower level by atmospheric pressure and gravity.

words.tr:
n. 酒；酒宴；暴饮
v. 暴饮；痛饮
words.ex: He drinks too much booze at parties.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上喝太多酒。
words.en: To booze means to drink alcohol, especially in large quantities.

words.tr:
v. 狼吞虎咽；吞并；火鸡咯咯叫
n. 火鸡叫声
words.ex: The dog will gobble up its food quickly.
words.ex_cn: 狗会很快把食物狼吞虎咽地吃掉。
words.en: To eat something quickly and eagerly, often making a noise.

words.ex: The knight was impaled on the spear.
words.ex_cn: 骑士被长矛刺穿了。
words.en: To impale someone or something means to pierce them with a sharp object such as a spear or spike.

words.ex: The knight held a long lance in his hand.
words.ex_cn: 骑士手中握着一支长矛。
words.en: A lance is a long weapon used in the past by soldiers on horseback, consisting of a wooden shaft with a pointed metal end. As a verb, to lance means to pierce or cut open with a sharp instrument, especially a lance.

words.tr:
n. 鱼叉
v. 用鱼叉叉
words.ex: The fisherman threw a harpoon at the whale.
words.ex_cn: 渔夫向鲸鱼投掷了一支鱼叉。
words.en: A harpoon is a long spear-like instrument used in fishing to catch large fish or whales.

words.tr: v. 砍；劈；削成…形状；开辟；坚持；遵守
words.ex: He hews wood every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上砍柴。
words.en: To cut or shape something with a tool such as an axe, or to make something by cutting.

words.ex: He drew a loop with the pencil.
words.ex_cn: 他用铅笔画了一个圈。
words.en: A loop is a shape produced by a curve that bends round and crosses itself, or a piece of wire, string, etc. that has this shape. It can also refer to a repeated sequence of operations or events in a computer program or in a process.

words.tr: v. 劈砍；侵入（计算机等）
words.ex: He hacked the tree with an axe.
words.ex_cn: 他用斧头劈砍那棵树。
words.en: To hack means to cut or chop something with rough or heavy blows, or to gain unauthorized access to data in a system or computer.

words.ex: The farmer shears sheep every spring.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每年春天给羊剪毛。
words.en: To shear means to cut the wool off a sheep or to cut or trim something with scissors or shears.

words.ex: The artist incised the design into the wood.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家将设计雕刻在木头上。
words.en: To cut into a surface with a sharp tool; to carve or engrave.

words.ex: The boys are playing dice after school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们放学后玩掷骰游戏。
words.en: Small cubes marked on each side with spots numbering from one to six, used in games of chance; to cut food into small cubes.

words.tr:
n. 去骨鱼片；无骨肉片
v. 剔除（鱼或肉）的骨头
words.ex: He cooked a fish fillet for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他为晚餐烹制了一块鱼排。
words.en: A fillet is a piece of meat or fish that has no bones in it.

words.tr:
v. 切碎；剁碎；装腔作势地小步走
n. 绞碎的肉
words.ex: He minces garlic for the sauce.
words.ex_cn: 他把大蒜剁碎用来做酱。
words.en: To mince means to cut food, especially meat, into very small pieces, or to walk or speak in an affected manner.

words.ex: The brewery uses fresh mash to make beer.
words.ex_cn: 酿酒厂使用新鲜的麦芽浆来酿造啤酒。
words.en: To crush or smash something into a soft, pulpy mass.

words.ex: He kneads dough every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上揉面团。
words.en: To knead is to press and stretch dough or another substance with your hands in order to make it smooth and ready to use.

words.tr:
v. 剧烈搅动；（使）猛烈翻腾
n. 搅乳器
words.ex: The machine churns the butter in the cream.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器剧烈搅动奶油来制作黄油。
words.en: To churn means to stir or shake milk or cream in order to make butter, or to move something around violently in water or air.

words.tr:
v. 拂；掸；搅拌；急速地移动
n. 搅拌器；打蛋器
words.ex: She whisked the dust off the table.
words.ex_cn: 她拂去了桌子上的灰尘。
words.en: To move something or someone quickly and suddenly; to mix ingredients using a whisk.

words.ex: The slit in the curtain let in a thin beam of light.
words.ex_cn: 窗帘上的裂缝透进了一束细光。
words.en: A long, narrow cut or opening.

words.tr:
n. 碎片；细条；少量
v. 撕碎；切碎
words.ex: The dog found a shred of paper in the yard.
words.ex_cn: 狗在院子里找到一片纸屑。
words.en: A shred is a very small amount of something, especially a very small piece of paper or cloth. When you shred something, you cut it or tear it into very small pieces.

words.tr:
n. 辫子；穗带
v. 编辫子；编织
words.ex: She wore a long braid down her back.
words.ex_cn: 她身后垂着一条长长的辫子。
words.en: A braid is a complex structure or pattern formed by intertwining three or more strands of flexible material such as textile fibers, wire, or hair.

words.tr: n. 软帽；汽车发动机罩；阀帽
words.ex: The girl wore a white bonnet to the church.
words.ex_cn: 这个女孩戴着一顶白色软帽去教堂。
words.en: A bonnet is a type of hat that is tied under the chin and was traditionally worn by women and girls. It can also refer to the metal cover over the engine of a car.

words.tr:
v. 织补
n. 织补
words.ex: She darned her socks with blue thread.
words.ex_cn: 她用蓝色线织补了她的袜子。
words.en: To darn means to repair a hole in a piece of clothing by sewing stitches across the hole.

words.tr:
n. 褶；褶状物
v. 使打褶
words.ex: She ironed the pleat in her skirt.
words.ex_cn: 她把裙子上的褶皱熨平了。
words.en: A pleat is a fold in a piece of cloth, made by doubling the material over on itself and then pressing or stitching it into place.

words.tr: adj. 质量不一致的；时好时坏的；
words.ex: The paint on the wall is patchy.
words.ex_cn: 墙上的油漆质量不一致。
words.en: Something that is patchy occurs or exists in some places but not in others, or is sometimes good but sometimes bad.

words.tr:
v. 卷收；卷起；收拢
n. 卷收；卷起之物
words.ex: He furl the sail when the wind stopped.
words.ex_cn: 风停时，他把帆卷了起来。
words.en: To furl something means to roll or fold it up neatly and securely, especially something that is flexible or can be rolled up, like a sail or a flag.

words.ex: The diamond is encased in glass.
words.ex_cn: 钻石被包裹在玻璃里。
words.en: To encase something means to cover or surround it completely in a case or close-fitting covering.

words.tr: v. 使卷入；使陷入；牵连
words.ex: He didn't want to embroil his friend in the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他不想让朋友卷入这场争吵。
words.en: To involve someone in a difficult or complicated situation.

words.ex: The room is airy with windows on all sides.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间四面都有窗户，通风很好。
words.en: If a place or room is airy, it has a lot of fresh air because it is large or has a lot of windows.

words.ex: The room was stuffy and hard to breathe in.
words.ex_cn: 房间闷热得让人难以呼吸。
words.en: If you describe a place as stuffy, you mean that it is unpleasantly warm and has no fresh air.

words.tr: adj. 密封的；不透气的；与外界隔绝的
words.ex: The container was hermetic to ensure the contents stayed fresh.
words.ex_cn: 这个容器是密封的，以确保内容物保持新鲜。
words.en: If something is hermetic, it is so tightly sealed that no air can get in or out.

words.ex: He wrote a draft of the letter before sending it.
words.ex_cn: 他在发送之前写了这封信的草稿。
words.en: A draft is a preliminary version of a piece of writing, or a current of air in a room or other confined space. It can also refer to the act of selecting someone for a particular purpose or task, especially in sports or the military.

words.tr: adj. 拥挤的；堵塞的； v. “congest” 的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The road was congested with cars during rush hour.
words.ex_cn: 高峰时段，这条路被汽车挤满了。
words.en: If a place is congested, it is extremely crowded and blocked with traffic or people.

words.tr:
v. 疏浚；挖掘
n. 挖泥船；疏浚机
words.ex: They dredge the river to remove mud.
words.ex_cn: 他们疏浚河流以清除淤泥。
words.en: To dredge means to remove mud, sand, or other material from the bottom of a river, lake, etc., in order to make it deeper or to search for something.

words.ex: Workers excavate the old ruins with shovels.
words.ex_cn: 工人们用铲子挖掘古代遗址。
words.en: To excavate means to dig in the ground in order to find things that have been buried there, such as archaeological remains.

words.tr:
v. 挖洞；钻进；翻寻
n. 地洞
words.ex: The rabbit burrows under the tree.
words.ex_cn: 兔子在树下打洞。
words.en: A burrow is a hole or tunnel dug by a small animal, such as a rabbit or a mole, as a dwelling. As a verb, to burrow means to dig a hole or tunnel for habitation or refuge.

words.tr:
n. 小困难或障碍；划破处；钩丝处
v. 被钩住；划破；抢先获得
words.ex: He found a snag in the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他在计划中发现了一个问题。
words.en: A snag is a small problem or difficulty that you did not expect.

words.tr:
n. 跨栏；障碍；难关
v. 越过障碍；克服
words.ex: He jumped over the hurdle quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速跳过了跨栏。
words.en: A hurdle is a problem or difficulty that you must deal with before you can achieve something.

words.tr:
n. 僵局；和棋；僵持状态
v. 使陷入僵局
words.ex: The two players are in a stalemate.
words.ex_cn: 两位选手陷入了僵局。
words.en: A situation in which further action or progress by opposing parties seems impossible.

words.ex: The two teams are in a deadlock over the budget.
words.ex_cn: 两个团队在预算上陷入了僵局。
words.en: A deadlock is a situation in which no progress can be made or no agreement is reached, especially because of a disagreement between two or more parties.

words.tr:
n. 挂锁；扣锁
v. 用挂锁锁上
words.ex: He secured the gate with a padlock.
words.ex_cn: 他用挂锁锁住了大门。
words.en: A padlock is a lock which is used for fastening two things together, for example two parts of a door or a lid on a container. It consists of a block of metal with a U-shaped bar attached to it. One end of the bar is released by turning a key in the lock.

words.ex: She tinted the glass blue.
words.ex_cn: 她把玻璃染成了蓝色。
words.en: A tint is a small amount of a particular color, especially when it is used to make the main color lighter or darker.

words.tr:
v. 染上点颜色
n. 一丝痕迹；色调
words.ex: The sky has a tinge of pink at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 日落时，天空有一丝粉红色。
words.en: A tinge of a colour, feeling, or quality is a small amount of it.

words.ex: Rinse the dishes with water before drying them.
words.ex_cn: 在晾干盘子之前用清水冲洗。
words.en: To rinse something means to wash it in clean water in order to remove soap or dirt.

words.ex: The old building has a beautiful facade with stone pillars.
words.ex_cn: 这栋老建筑有一个带有石柱的漂亮正面。
words.en: The front of a building, especially an imposing or decorative one. Also, a superficial appearance or illusion of something.

words.ex: The diamond has many smooth facets.
words.ex_cn: 这颗钻石有许多光滑的小平面。
words.en: A particular aspect or feature of something.

words.ex: The park is in the vicinity of my house.
words.ex_cn: 公园在我家附近。
words.en: The area or region near or about a place; the surrounding district.

words.tr:
n. 侧面；侧翼；胁腹
v. 在…侧面（有）
words.ex: The soldiers moved to the flank to avoid the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们移动到侧翼以避开敌人。
words.en: The side of something, especially a part of the body between the ribs and the hip; to be situated on each side of or on one side of (something).

words.ex: The car made a lateral move to avoid the dog.
words.ex_cn: 汽车横向移动以避开狗。
words.en: Relating to the side or sides; situated at or extending to the side.

words.tr: adj. 多边的；多国参加的
words.ex: The multilateral agreement helped many countries work together.
words.ex_cn: 这个多边协议帮助许多国家共同合作。
