words.en: Involving or agreed upon by three or more parties, especially the governments of different countries.

words.tr:
adj. 在水上漂浮；有偿债能力
adv. 在水上漂浮；有偿债能力
words.ex: The boat stayed afloat during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 船在风暴中保持漂浮。
words.en: If someone or something is afloat, they are floating on water or in the air.

words.tr:
adv. 漂流地；漫无目的地
adj. 漂泊的；漫无目的的；脱落的
words.ex: The boat was adrift in the sea.
words.ex_cn: 小船在海上漂流。
words.en: If something is adrift, it is floating on the water and not fastened to anything or controlled by anyone.

words.ex: The boat went aground on the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 船在岩石上搁浅了。
words.en: If a ship runs aground, it touches the ground in a shallow part of a river, lake, or the sea, and gets stuck.

words.ex: The sailor fell overboard during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 水手在风暴中从船上掉入海中。
words.en: If someone falls overboard, they fall from a ship into the water. It can also mean doing something to an excessive degree.

words.ex: The small boat capsize in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 小船在风暴中倾覆了。
words.en: If a boat capsizes or if you capsize it, it turns over in the water.

words.tr: adj. 倾向一方的；不平衡的；悬殊的
words.ex: The game was lopsided, and one team won by 10 points.
words.ex_cn: 这场比赛比分悬殊，一支队伍以10分获胜。
words.en: Something that is lopsided is uneven because one side is lower or heavier than the other.

words.ex: The ship took on ballast to stay stable in rough water.
words.ex_cn: 船为了在恶劣水域中保持稳定，装载了压舱物。
words.en: Ballast is heavy material that is carried in a ship or hot-air balloon to make it more stable.

words.tr: v. 装载；装填；妥善放置
words.ex: He stowed the boxes in the truck.
words.ex_cn: 他把箱子装上了卡车。
words.en: To stow something means to pack it or store it neatly in a particular place.

words.tr:
v. 抵消；使平衡
n. 衡重体；平衡力
words.ex: The weight acts as a counterbalance to the arm.
words.ex_cn: 这个重量作为手臂的平衡物。
words.en: A counterbalance is a weight or force that balances or counteracts another.

words.ex: The frog is an amphibian.
words.ex_cn: 青蛙是一种两栖动物。
words.en: An amphibian is a type of animal that can live both on land and in water. Frogs, toads, and salamanders are examples of amphibians.

words.ex: He ran a 100-meter sprint in under 11 seconds.
words.ex_cn: 他在100米冲刺中跑出了不到11秒的成绩。
words.en: If you sprint, you run or ride as fast as you can over a short distance.

words.tr: v. 猛冲；猛投；猛烈碰撞
words.ex: The car hurtled down the hill.
words.ex_cn: 汽车飞速冲下山坡。
words.en: If someone or something hurtles somewhere, they move there very quickly, often in a uncontrolled way.

words.tr:
v. 小步疾走；急赶
n. 快跑声；疾走
words.ex: The mouse scurried under the table.
words.ex_cn: 老鼠迅速跑到了桌子底下。
words.en: If people or small animals scurry somewhere, they move there quickly and hurriedly, especially because they are frightened.

words.ex: The whisper was barely audible.
words.ex_cn: 那耳语几乎听不见。
words.en: If a sound is audible, it is loud enough for you to hear it.

words.ex: He tried to eavesdrop on their conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他试图偷听他们的对话。
words.en: To eavesdrop means to listen secretly to other people's conversations.

words.ex: The vernal equinox marks the beginning of spring.
words.ex_cn: 春分标志着春天的开始。
words.en: Relating to or occurring in spring.

words.ex: The seeds germinate in warm soil.
words.ex_cn: 种子在温暖的土壤中发芽。
words.en: To germinate means to begin to grow or develop, especially for a seed or spore.

words.ex: The gardener did a graft on the apple tree.
words.ex_cn: 园丁在苹果树上进行了嫁接。
words.en: Graft can refer to the act of joining parts from different plants so that they grow as one plant, or to the act of transferring living tissue from one part of the body to another. It can also refer to the practice of using one's position to gain money or advantages dishonestly.

words.ex: The child outgrew his shoes in one year.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子一年内就长高了，鞋子都穿不下了。
words.en: If you outgrow a particular way of behaving or thinking, you change and become more mature, so that you no longer behave or think in that way.

words.tr: v. 蔓延；散乱地分布；落伍
words.ex: Weeds straggle across the garden.
words.ex_cn: 杂草蔓延在整个花园里。
words.en: If people straggle, they move along slowly, spread out over a wide area, and are not in a group.

words.ex: He likes to ramble about his travels.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢漫谈他的旅行经历。
words.en: To walk for pleasure, especially in the countryside, without a definite route or destination.

chapters.name: Part III 核心词汇 Lesson 25

words.ex: The wind strews leaves on the ground.
words.ex_cn: 风把树叶吹得满地都是。
words.en: To scatter or spread things untidily over a surface or area.

words.ex: The news will disseminate quickly through social media.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻会通过社交媒体迅速传播。
words.en: To disseminate means to spread or distribute something, especially information, widely.

words.ex: She intersperses flowers in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 她在花园里分散地种着花。
words.en: To place something at intervals among other things.

words.tr:
n. 枯萎；凋谢；憔悴；
v. 枯萎；凋谢；憔悴；
words.ex: The flowers showed signs of wilt after the long heat.
words.ex_cn: 这些花在长时间高温后出现了枯萎的迹象。
words.en: If a plant wilts, it bends over because it is too dry, too hot, or too weak to stay upright.

words.ex: The chemicals were used to defoliate the trees.
words.ex_cn: 这些化学物质被用来使树木落叶。
words.en: To remove the leaves from a plant or tree, especially by using chemicals.

words.ex: The kernel of the computer is the operating system.
words.ex_cn: 计算机的核心是操作系统。
words.en: The kernel of something such as a nut or a seed is the part inside the shell. The kernel of an idea or a theory is the central and most important part of it.

words.ex: The corn has a dry husk around it.
words.ex_cn: 玉米外面有一层干外壳。
words.en: The outer covering of some fruits and seeds, especially when it is dry and hard.

words.ex: He will pare the apple with a knife.
words.ex_cn: 他将用刀削苹果。
words.en: To pare something means to cut off its outer layer or to reduce its size or amount by cutting or trimming.

words.ex: Humans domesticated dogs thousands of years ago.
words.ex_cn: 人类几千年前就驯养了狗。
words.en: To domesticate an animal or plant means to bring it under human control in order to provide food, power, or company.

words.ex: The hen incubate eggs until they hatch.
words.ex_cn: 母鸡孵化鸡蛋直到小鸡孵出。
words.en: to keep eggs warm so that they develop and hatch, or to keep cells, bacteria, etc. at a suitable temperature so that they develop

words.tr:
v. 指拨（款 项）；指定（特殊用途）
n. 耳记；特征
words.ex: The government will earmark money for schools.
words.ex_cn: 政府将为学校拨款。
words.en: To designate or set aside something, especially funds, for a specific purpose.

words.ex: The docile dog followed its owner quietly.
words.ex_cn: 这只温顺的狗安静地跟着主人。
words.en: A docile person or animal is quiet, not aggressive, and easily controlled.

words.tr:
v. 摇摆；摇动
n. 摇摆；爱说笑的人
words.ex: The dog wagged its tail happily.
words.ex_cn: 狗开心地摇着尾巴。
words.en: If a dog wags its tail, it moves its tail from side to side, often because it is happy or excited.

words.ex: He lives by hedonism, seeking pleasure every day.
words.ex_cn: 他奉行享乐主义，每天追求快乐。
words.en: Hedonism is the belief that gaining pleasure is the most important thing in life.

words.tr:
adj. 苦行的；禁欲主义的
n. 苦行者；禁欲者
words.ex: He lives an ascetic life with no luxury.
words.ex_cn: 他过着简朴的生活，没有任何奢侈。
words.en: An ascetic person has a way of life that is simple and strict, usually because of their religious beliefs.

words.tr:
adj. 极权主义的
n. 极权主义者
words.ex: No example sentences
words.ex_cn: 没有例句
words.en: A totalitarian political system is one in which there is only one political party which controls everything and does not allow any opposition parties.

words.tr: adj. 超现实主义的；离奇的；怪诞的
words.ex: The dream was surreal.
words.ex_cn: 这个梦很超现实。
words.en: If you describe something as surreal, you mean that the elements in it are combined in a strange way that you would not normally expect, like in a dream.

words.ex: The country fell into anarchy after the war.
words.ex_cn: 战争之后，这个国家陷入了混乱。
words.en: Anarchy is a state of disorder due to absence or nonrecognition of authority or other controlling systems.

words.ex: He refuses to accept the dogma of the church.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝接受教会的教条。
words.en: A principle or set of principles laid down by an authority as incontrovertibly true.

words.tr: adj. 教诲的；说教的；好教训人的
words.ex: The teacher gave a didactic speech to help students learn.
words.ex_cn: 老师发表了一篇富有教育意义的演讲来帮助学生学习。
words.en: Something that is didactic is intended to teach people something, especially a moral lesson.

words.ex: The teacher will delimit the scope of the exam.
words.ex_cn: 老师将限定考试的范围。
words.en: If you delimit something, you fix or establish its limits.

words.tr: adj. 不确定的；不明确的
words.ex: The result is indeterminate.
words.ex_cn: 结果是不确定的。
words.en: If something is indeterminate, you cannot say exactly what it is.

words.tr: adj. 不容置疑的；无可否认的
words.ex: The evidence is incontrovertible.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可辩驳的。
words.en: If something is incontrovertible, it is definitely true and cannot be disputed.

words.ex: His genius is indubitable.
words.ex_cn: 他的天才是不容置疑的。
words.en: If you describe something as indubitable, you mean that it is definitely true.

words.ex: He gave her a light pinch on the arm.
words.ex_cn: 他轻轻捏了她的胳膊一下。
words.en: To pinch someone or something means to squeeze them tightly between your thumb and finger, or between two surfaces, especially in a way that causes pain.

words.ex: The dog gave a small nip to his leg.
words.ex_cn: 狗轻轻咬了他的腿一口。
words.en: To nip means to pinch, squeeze, or bite something quickly and sharply. It can also refer to taking a small amount of a drink.

words.tr:
v. 猛拉；急抽
n. 猛拉；急抽
words.ex: He yanked the door open quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速把门拽开了。
words.en: To pull something suddenly and with force.

words.tr:
n. 连枷
v. 用连枷打；胡乱摆动；用力地挥动
words.ex: The farmer flails the wheat to separate the grains.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用连枷打小麦以分离谷粒。
words.en: A flail is a tool used for threshing grain, consisting of a long handle with a freely swinging stick or bar attached to it. As a verb, to flail means to wave or swing wildly; to thrash about.

words.tr: adj. 拉紧的；绷紧的；紧张的
words.ex: The sail was taut in the strong wind.
words.ex_cn: 帆在强风中绷得紧紧的。
words.en: If something such as a rope or wire is taut, it is stretched very tight. If muscles or parts of the body are taut, they are stretched tight, often because of physical effort or anxiety.

words.tr:
v. 感到刺痛；强烈地感到
n. 刺痛感；激动感
words.ex: Her fingers tingle when she holds ice.
words.ex_cn: 当她握着冰时，手指会发麻。
words.en: If you tingle, you feel a slight prickling or stinging sensation, often because you are excited or frightened.

words.ex: The child squirmed in his chair.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在椅子上扭动着。
words.en: If you squirm, you move your body from side to side, usually because you are nervous or uncomfortable.

words.tr:
n. 蠕动；扭动；蜿蜒
v. 蠕动；扭动；蜿蜒前进
words.ex: The worm made a small wriggle in the soil.
words.ex_cn: 这条蠕虫在泥土中蠕动了一下。
words.en: To move or cause to move with short, quick twisting or turning motions.

words.tr:
v. 扭动；摆动
n. 扭动；摆动
words.ex: The baby wiggles her toes when she laughs.
words.ex_cn: 当宝宝笑的时候，她会动动脚趾。
words.en: To move or cause to move up and down or from side to side with small rapid movements.

words.tr:
v. 扭动；翻滚；苦恼
n. 扭动；翻滚
words.ex: The child writhe in pain after falling.
words.ex_cn: 孩子摔倒后痛苦地扭动。
words.en: If you writhe, your body twists and turns violently backwards and forwards, usually because you are in great pain or discomfort.

words.tr:
v. 猛扭；扭伤；挣脱
n. 扳手；扳钳；（离别的）痛苦
words.ex: He wrenched the door open with all his strength.
words.ex_cn: 他用尽全力猛扭门，把它打开了。
words.en: A wrench is a tool used for gripping and turning nuts, bolts, pipes, etc. It can also refer to a sudden violent twist or pull, or a feeling of sadness or distress caused by separation.

words.tr:
v. 夺取；费力取得；歪曲
n. 扭；拧
words.ex: He wrests the ball from his opponent.
words.ex_cn: 他从对手那里抢走球。
words.en: To wrest something from someone means to take it from them with a lot of effort, often because they do not want to give it to you.

words.tr:
v. 挣扎；深陷困境
n. 比目鱼
words.ex: The fish floundered in the shallow water.
words.ex_cn: 鱼在浅水中挣扎。
words.en: If you flounder, you experience great difficulties and are likely to fail completely.

words.ex: The drought depletes the water supply.
words.ex_cn: 干旱耗尽了水源。
words.en: If you deplete something, you reduce the amount of it that is available or that exists.

words.tr: v. 大批杀死；大量毁灭
words.ex: The storm decimated the village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴摧毁了这个村庄。
words.en: To decimate something such as a group of people or animals means to destroy a very large number of them.

words.ex: The school will curtail recess time during exams.
words.ex_cn: 学校在考试期间将缩短课间休息时间。
words.en: If you curtail something, you reduce or limit it.

words.ex: The injury impaired his ability to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤损害了他走路的能力。
words.en: If something impairs something such as an ability or the way something works, it damages it or makes it worse.

words.tr: v. 使遭危险或伤害；危害；危及
words.ex: Pollution can endanger animals.
words.ex_cn: 污染会危及动物。
words.en: To put someone or something at risk or in danger.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；恶性的；致命的
words.ex: Smoking is a pernicious habit.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟是一种有害的习惯。
words.en: Having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way.

words.ex: The baleful glare of the enemy sent shivers down their spines.
words.ex_cn: 敌人恶意的目光让他们不寒而栗。
words.en: Baleful means threatening harm or evil.

words.ex: Smoking is injurious to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is injurious causes harm or damage.

words.ex: The snake released venom into its prey.
words.ex_cn: 蛇向猎物释放了毒液。
words.en: Venom is a poisonous substance secreted by animals such as snakes and spiders, used for defense or to kill prey.

words.ex: The virulent virus spread quickly through the town.
words.ex_cn: 这种剧毒的病毒迅速在小镇上传播。
words.en: A virulent disease or poison is extremely powerful and dangerous.

words.ex: The viral infection made him feverish for three days.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒引起的感染让他发烧了三天。
words.en: Relating to or caused by a virus; becoming very popular by circulating quickly from person to person, especially on the internet.

words.tr:
adj. 有害的；恶意的
v. 中伤；污蔑
words.ex: The virus is malign and spreads quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒是有害的，并且传播迅速。
words.en: If you malign someone, you say unpleasant and untrue things about them. If something is malign, it is harmful or evil.

words.tr: adj. 恶毒的；恶性的；恶意的
words.ex: His malignant words hurt everyone around him.
words.ex_cn: 他恶毒的话语伤害了周围的所有人。
words.en: If you say that someone is malignant, you mean they are very dangerous and cause harm to people.

words.ex: The benign teacher always helped students after class.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的老师总是在课后帮助学生。
words.en: A benign substance or process does not have any harmful effects.

words.tr:
v. 落下；
adj. 点亮的；
words.ex: The bird alighted on the tree.
words.ex_cn: 鸟落在了树上。
words.en: If someone alights from a vehicle or if they alight, they get out of it after a journey.

words.ex: He used a match to ignite the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他用火柴点燃了火。
words.en: If you ignite something or if it ignites, it starts burning or explodes.

words.tr: adj. 着火的；闪耀的；激动的
words.ex: The house was ablaze at night.
words.ex_cn: 那所房子在夜里着火了。
words.en: If something is ablaze, it is burning very fiercely.

words.ex: The sign says flammable near the gasoline.
words.ex_cn: 标志上写着汽油附近易燃。
words.en: Flammable materials or substances catch fire and burn easily.

words.ex: The sign says the material is inflammable.
words.ex_cn: 标志上说这种材料是易燃的。
words.en: Easily set on fire; capable of burning quickly and intensely.

words.tr:
v. 闷烧；冒烟；郁积
n. 闷烧
words.ex: The fire still smolders in the fireplace.
words.ex_cn: 火还在壁炉里闷烧。
words.en: To burn slowly with smoke but without flame, or to exist in a suppressed state.

words.tr:
v. 郁积；（无明火）闷烧；（眼睛）放电
n. 冒烟闷烧
words.ex: Anger smouldered in his heart for years.
words.ex_cn: 愤怒在他心中郁积了多年。
words.en: To burn slowly with smoke but without flame; to exist in a suppressed state; to feel strong emotions without showing them.

words.ex: The flame singed her hair.
words.ex_cn: 火焰烧焦了她的头发。
words.en: To burn superficially or lightly; scorch.

words.ex: The bomb will detonate at midnight.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹将在午夜爆炸。
words.en: To detonate something means to cause it to explode.

words.ex: The wound was cleaned with saline water.
words.ex_cn: 伤口用盐水清洗。
words.en: Saline is used to describe something that contains salt or is related to salt.

words.tr:
n. 泡菜；腌菜；腌汁；腌制品；困境
v. 腌制（泡菜等）
words.ex: He put a pickle on his sandwich.
words.ex_cn: 他在三明治上放了一颗酸黄瓜。
words.en: A pickle is a vegetable or fruit that has been preserved in vinegar or salt water, or a difficult situation.

words.ex: The milk froths when you steam it.
words.ex_cn: 当你用蒸汽加热牛奶时，它会起泡沫。
words.en: A mass of small bubbles formed in or on a liquid; foam.

words.ex: The soup was too watery and tasted bland.
words.ex_cn: 这汤太稀了，味道淡。
words.en: Something that is watery contains, resembles, or consists of water.

words.tr: adj. 浑浊的；污浊不清的；
words.ex: The river water looks turbid after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后河水看起来浑浊。
words.en: If you describe something as turbid, you mean that it is cloudy, dirty, or muddy.

words.tr: adj. 发粘的；俗气的；破烂的
words.ex: The glue was still tacky after an hour.
words.ex_cn: 一小时后，胶水仍然发粘。
words.en: If you describe something as tacky, you dislike it because it is cheap and badly made or vulgar.

words.ex: The bread became soggy after sitting in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 面包在雨中放了一会儿后变得湿软。
words.en: Something that is soggy is unpleasantly wet.

words.tr:
v. 使湿透；浸透
n. 弄湿；浸液
words.ex: The rain drenched his clothes.
words.ex_cn: 雨把他的衣服淋湿了。
words.en: To drench something or someone means to make them completely wet.

words.ex: The rain dampened the sound of the drums.
words.ex_cn: 雨减弱了鼓声。
words.en: To dampen something means to make it slightly wet, or to make it less strong or intense.

words.ex: They shouted, 'Welcome home!' when he walked through the door.
words.ex_cn: 当他走进门时，他们大喊：‘欢迎回家！’
words.en: A greeting used to express pleasure at someone's return to their home.

words.ex: The sun can dehydrate your skin quickly.
words.ex_cn: 太阳会很快使你的皮肤脱水。
words.en: To dehydrate something means to remove all the water from it, often in order to preserve it. If you dehydrate, you lose too much water from your body, usually because of illness or extreme heat.

words.tr: v. 无法做到；失败；“fail”的现在分词； adj. 减弱中的； n. 失败；
words.ex: He was failing to finish the race.
words.ex_cn: 他没能完成比赛。
words.en: A failing is a fault or a weakness in someone's character or abilities.

words.tr: adj. 无可挑剔的；无瑕疵的；
words.ex: Her impeccable manners impressed everyone at the dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她无可挑剔的礼仪让晚宴上的每个人都印象深刻。
words.en: If you describe something as impeccable, you are emphasizing that it is perfect and has no faults.

words.tr: adj. 清洁的；无瑕疵的；无过失的
words.ex: The kitchen was immaculate after she cleaned it.
words.ex_cn: 她打扫后，厨房非常干净。
words.en: If you describe something as immaculate, you mean that it is extremely clean, tidy, or neat.

words.ex: The matrix gave birth to all living things.
words.ex_cn: 母体孕育了所有生命。
words.en: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers, symbols, or expressions, arranged in rows and columns.

words.ex: Her kindness emanates from her smile.
words.ex_cn: 她的善良表现在她的微笑中。
words.en: To emanate means to come out from a source.

words.tr: v. 归于；委托；授权；信任
words.ex: They accredit the discovery to the scientist.
words.ex_cn: 他们将这一发现归功于这位科学家。
words.en: To officially recognize or approve someone or something as having a particular status or meeting certain standards.

words.tr:
n. 不信任；名誉丧失；信誉丧失
v. 不信；败坏名声；使丢脸
words.ex: His lies brought discredit to the company.
words.ex_cn: 他的谎言使公司失去了信任。
words.en: To discredit someone or something means to cause them to lose people's respect or trust.

words.ex: The trip is contingent on the weather.
words.ex_cn: 这次旅行取决于天气情况。
words.en: A contingent event or situation depends on something else in order to happen or exist.

words.tr: adj. 依照环境的；间接的；详细的
words.ex: He gave a circumstantial explanation based on the situation.
words.ex_cn: 他根据情况给出了一个依照环境的解释。
words.en: Circumstantial evidence is evidence that suggests something by implication rather than direct proof.

words.tr: phrase. 临时的；特别的；专为特定目的而设的
words.ex: They made an ad hoc decision to cancel the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他们临时决定取消会议。
words.en: Created or done for a particular purpose as necessary.

chapters.name: Part III 核心词汇 Lesson 26

words.tr: adj. 绝对的；确定无疑的；分类的
words.ex: He gave a categorical no to the offer.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个提议给出了明确的拒绝。
words.en: If you are categorical about something, you state your views very definitely and firmly.

words.tr: adj. 兼容的；可和谐共存的；
words.ex: This printer is compatible with my computer.
words.ex_cn: 这个打印机与我的电脑兼容。
words.en: If things, for example, systems, ideas, and beliefs, are compatible, they work well together or can exist together successfully.

words.tr:
adj. 不拘一格的；兼收并蓄的；折中的
n. 折中主义者
words.ex: He has an eclectic taste in music.
words.ex_cn: 他对音乐的品味很广泛多样。
words.en: An eclectic collection or group is a wide range of different things or people.

words.tr:
adj. 徒步的；在准备中的；在进行中
adv. 徒步地；在准备中地；在进行中
words.ex: The hikers went afoot through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者们徒步穿越了森林。
words.en: If you say that a plan or scheme is afoot, it is already happening or being planned.

words.tr: adj. 秘密的；鬼鬼祟祟的；偷偷摸摸的
words.ex: He gave a surreptitious glance at his phone during class.
words.ex_cn: 他在上课时偷偷瞥了一眼手机。
words.en: If something is done surreptitiously, it is done secretly, often because it would not be approved of.

words.ex: He gave a furtive look around before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前偷偷看了一眼四周。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as furtive, you disapprove of them behaving as if they want to keep something secret or hidden.

words.ex: Malaria is endemic in some parts of Africa.
words.ex_cn: 疟疾在非洲某些地区是地方性的。
words.en: If a disease or condition is endemic in a particular area, it is frequently or regularly found among the people living there.

words.tr: adj. 西洋的；西方的；欧美的；
words.ex: He likes occidental music more than traditional Chinese music.
words.ex_cn: 他更喜欢西洋音乐而不是中国传统音乐。
words.en: Relating to the countries of the West, especially Europe and America.

words.tr: v. 使加入国籍；使归化；移植
words.ex: He wants to naturalize in Canada.
words.ex_cn: 他想在加拿大归化为公民。
words.en: To naturalize someone means to make them a legal citizen of a country that they were not born in. It can also refer to the process of adapting plants or animals to a new environment.

words.tr:
adj. 本国的；地方的
n. 方言；土语
words.ex: He wrote the poem in the vernacular language.
words.ex_cn: 他用本国语言写了这首诗。
words.en: The vernacular is the language or dialect spoken by the ordinary people in a particular country or region.

words.ex: He is monolingual and only speaks English.
words.ex_cn: 他只会说英语，不懂其他语言。
words.en: Using or knowing only one language.

words.tr:
adj. 单色的；黑白的
n. 单色画；黑白照片
words.ex: The painting is monochrome, only black and white.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是单色的，只有黑色和白色。
words.en: Using only black, white, and shades of grey, or using only one colour.

words.tr:
n. 类似物
adj. 模拟的；指针式的
words.ex: The clock has analog hands.
words.ex_cn: 这个钟有指针。
words.en: An analog is something that is similar to something else in design, origin, use, etc., but is not exactly the same.

words.ex: This old phone is an analogue of the new smartphone.
words.ex_cn: 这部旧手机是这款智能手机的类似物。
words.en: Something that is similar to another thing in design, origin, use, etc., but not exactly the same.

words.tr: n. 喜爱；类同；密切关系；亲和力
words.ex: She has an affinity for painting.
words.ex_cn: 她喜爱绘画。
words.en: A natural liking for or attraction to someone or something.

words.ex: He likens his job to a puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的工作比作一个拼图。
words.en: To liken something to something else is to say that they are similar in some way.

words.tr: adj. 比喻的；象征的；写实的
words.ex: He used figurative language to describe his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他用了比喻性的语言来描述他的感受。
words.en: If you use a word or expression in a figurative sense, you use it with a more abstract or imaginative meaning than its ordinary literal one.

words.ex: The old man looked gaunt after his illness.
words.ex_cn: 这场病后，老人显得消瘦。
words.en: If someone looks gaunt, they look very thin, usually because they have been ill or worried.

words.tr: adj. 瘦弱的；憔悴的； v. “emaciate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The emaciated dog walked slowly down the street.
words.ex_cn: 那条瘦弱的狗慢慢走在街上。
words.en: Someone who is emaciated is extremely thin and weak because of illness or lack of food.

words.ex: The old man is infirm and needs help to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人身体虚弱，需要帮助才能走路。
words.en: If someone is infirm, they are weak or ill, and often old.

words.tr: adj. 憔悴的；形容枯槁的
words.ex: He looked haggard after working all night.
words.ex_cn: 他熬了一整夜后看起来憔悴不堪。
words.en: Someone who is haggard looks exhausted and unwell, often because they have been through a very difficult or stressful experience.

words.tr: adj. 皮包骨头的；极瘦的；
words.ex: The skinny dog had no meat on its bones.
words.ex_cn: 那只皮包骨头的狗身上一点肉都没有。
words.en: Very thin, especially in a way that is unattractive.

words.ex: The illness had enfeebled her to the point of immobility.
words.ex_cn: 疾病使她衰弱到几乎不能动弹的地步。
words.en: To make someone or something very weak.

words.ex: The illness debilitates him every winter.
words.ex_cn: 每年冬天，这场疾病都会使他虚弱。
words.en: To make someone weak and infirm.

words.tr: v. 衰弱；凋萎；憔悴；受折磨
words.ex: The prisoner languishes in a dark cell.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯在黑暗的牢房中饱受煎熬。
words.en: If someone languishes somewhere, they are forced to remain and suffer in an unpleasant situation.

words.ex: He has flabby arms from not exercising.
words.ex_cn: 他因为不锻炼，手臂松软。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as flabby, you are criticizing them for being soft and loose rather than firm and strong.

words.tr: adj. 松弛的；软弱的；无活力的
words.ex: The leaves looked flaccid after the long dry spell.
words.ex_cn: 长时间干旱后，树叶看起来软弱无力。
words.en: Lacking firmness, resilience, or muscle tone; soft and limp.

words.ex: The floppy ears of the dog waved when it ran.
words.ex_cn: 狗的松垂耳朵在它跑时晃动。
words.en: Something that is floppy is loose and soft, often hanging or bending in a way that suggests it lacks stiffness.

words.tr: adj. 无精打采的；疲倦无力的
words.ex: He gave a languid smile before lying down.
words.ex_cn: 他躺下前给了一个慵懒的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as languid, you mean that they show little energy or interest and are very slow and casual in their movements.

words.tr:
adj. 健壮的；硬朗的
v. 强拉硬拖
words.ex: He is still hale at age 80.
words.ex_cn: 他80岁了依然身体健康。
words.en: If you describe someone, especially an old person, as hale, you mean that they are healthy.

words.ex: He was adamant about not changing his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他坚定不移地不改变主意。
words.en: If someone is adamant about something, they are determined not to change their mind about it.

words.ex: He is a stalwart of the environmental movement.
words.ex_cn: 他是环保运动的坚定分子。
words.en: A stalwart person is someone who is very loyal and committed to a person, belief, or cause and is not likely to change their views or behavior.

words.tr: adj. 坚定的；不懈的；始终如一的
words.ex: He has unswerving loyalty to his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友有着坚定不移的忠诚。
words.en: If you describe someone's attitude, feeling, or way of behaving as unswerving, you mean that it is strong and firm and does not weaken or change.

words.tr: adj. 斯多葛派的；坚忍克己的
words.ex: He remained stoical after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后依然表现得冷静淡然。
words.en: If you are stoical, you do not show your feelings or complain even in a situation that is difficult or painful.

words.ex: The contract stipulates that payments must be made monthly.
words.ex_cn: 合同规定付款必须按月进行。
words.en: If you stipulate a condition or stipulate that something must be done, you say clearly that it must be done.

words.ex: The teacher elucidated the math problem with a simple diagram.
words.ex_cn: 老师用一个简单的图表阐明了这道数学题。
words.en: To make something clear or easy to understand by explaining or giving reasons.

words.ex: He overstates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸大自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you say that someone is overstating something, you mean they are describing it in a way that makes it seem more important or serious than it really is.

words.tr: n. 宣言；声明；格言；警句
words.ex: The judge's dictum was clear and final.
words.ex_cn: 法官的宣言清晰而最终。
words.en: A dictum is a formal pronouncement from an authoritative source; it can also be a short statement that expresses a general truth or principle.

words.tr: v. 慷慨陈词；高声朗诵
words.ex: He likes to declaim poetry in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在全班面前朗诵诗歌。
words.en: To declaim means to speak or recite something in a dramatic or impassioned way, often in public.

words.ex: He expounded his ideas clearly in the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上清楚地阐述了他的观点。
words.en: To expound means to explain something in detail, especially a theory, idea, or point of view.

words.tr:
v. 细述；叙述
n. 叙述；重新计票
words.ex: He tried to recount the accident to the police.
words.ex_cn: 他试图向警察重新叙述那场事故。
words.en: To recount means to tell someone about something that happened, often in detail; or to count something again to make sure the number is correct.

words.ex: He will enumerate the steps clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他将清晰地列出这些步骤。
words.en: To enumerate means to mention things one by one.

words.tr: v. 作现场解说；进行实况报道
words.ex: He will commentate on the football match tonight.
words.ex_cn: 他今晚将为这场足球比赛做解说。
words.en: To commentate means to provide a spoken commentary on a sports match or other event as it happens, especially on television or radio.

words.ex: He will delineate the plan clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他将清晰地描述这个计划。
words.en: To delineate something means to describe or portray it precisely.

words.tr: v. 暗指；（间接）提到；影射
words.ex: He alluded to the problem without naming it.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示了这个问题，但没有点明。
words.en: To allude to something means to mention it in an indirect way.

words.ex: He insinuated that she was lying.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示她在撒谎。
words.en: If you say that someone insinuates that something bad is the case, you mean that they say it in an indirect way.

words.ex: She had only the faintest inkling of what he was planning.
words.ex_cn: 她对他正在策划的事情只有一点模糊的概念。
words.en: An inkling is a slight knowledge or suspicion of something.

words.ex: He invoked the law to protect his rights.
words.ex_cn: 他援引法律来保护自己的权利。
words.en: If you invoke a law, rule, or principle, you refer to it as a reason or justification for something.

words.ex: He entreats his friend to help him.
words.ex_cn: 他恳求朋友帮助他。
words.en: To ask someone earnestly or anxiously to do something.

words.ex: She implored him to stay.
words.ex_cn: 她恳求他留下。
words.en: If you implore someone to do something, you ask them to do it in a forceful, emotional way.

words.ex: The two countries formed a confederate alliance to defend their borders.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家结成了同盟联盟以保卫它们的边界。
words.en: A confederate is someone who works with others to achieve a common goal, often in a political or military context. It can also refer to a member of a confederation, which is a union of states or groups united for a common purpose.

words.ex: The weather was congenial for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常适合野餐。
words.en: A congenial person, place, or environment is pleasant because it suits your character or nature.

words.tr:
n. 朋友；伙伴
v. 结为伙伴
words.ex: He is my best pal.
words.ex_cn: 他是我最好的朋友。
words.en: A pal is a friend or companion.

words.ex: He hobnobs with famous actors at parties.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上与著名演员亲近交往。
words.en: To associate familiarly or socially; to drink together.

words.ex: Align your goals with your actions.
words.ex_cn: 让你的目标与行动保持一致。
words.en: To arrange something in a straight line or in the correct position in relation to something else, usually so that it is parallel to it.

words.ex: The rupture in the pipe caused a flood.
words.ex_cn: 管道的破裂导致了洪水。
words.en: A rupture is a severe injury in which an internal part of your body tears or bursts open, or the act of breaking or bursting something.

words.ex: The car deviated from the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车偏离了道路。
words.en: To deviate means to do something that is different from the usual or common way of behaving.

words.ex: He digresses when he talks about his vacation.
words.ex_cn: 他谈论假期时会跑题。
words.en: If you digress, you move away from the subject you are talking or writing about and talk or write about something different for a while.

words.ex: We took a detour to avoid the traffic.
words.ex_cn: 我们绕道以避开交通拥堵。
words.en: A detour is a longer, less direct way to go somewhere, used to avoid a problem or to visit something along the way.

words.tr:
adv. 迷路地；误入歧途地
adj. 迷路的；误入歧途的
words.ex: The little dog went astray in the park.
words.ex_cn: 那只小狗在公园里走丢了。
words.en: If you go astray, you lose your direction when you are trying to go somewhere.

words.tr: adj. 游历的；游离不定的；行为不当的；出轨的
words.ex: The errant knight traveled far across the land.
words.ex_cn: 这位游历的骑士穿越了广袤的土地。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as errant, you mean that they have strayed from the proper course or standards.

words.ex: He used a stick to fend off the dog.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根棍子挡开了那只狗。
words.en: To fend means to defend or protect oneself from something, or to manage to survive or cope without help.

words.ex: He likes to seclude himself in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢把自己 secluded 在森林里。
words.en: To seclude means to keep someone away from other people, or to keep something away from other things.

words.tr: v. 隔离；使隔热；使隔音；使绝缘
words.ex: The walls insulate the house from cold air.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁将房子与冷空气隔离开。
words.en: To insulate something means to protect it from heat, cold, noise, or electricity by covering it in a material that prevents it from passing through.

words.ex: He stayed in quarantine for 14 days.
words.ex_cn: 他隔离了14天。
words.en: A quarantine is a period of time during which an animal or person that might have a disease is kept away from other people or animals so that the disease cannot spread.

words.ex: The new law impinges on people's privacy.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律侵犯了人们的隐私。
words.en: To impinge means to have an effect or influence, especially a negative one, on someone or something.

words.tr:
adj. 起作用的；运作中的
n. 技工；密探；特工
words.ex: The operative plan is to start tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 实施的计划是明天开始。
words.en: An operative system or plan is one that is in use or being used. An operative is someone who works for a government agency or a private company, often doing secret or confidential work.

words.ex: The operational system runs smoothly every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个运作系统每天运行顺畅。
words.en: If a system or service is operational, it is working or able to be used.

words.ex: This plan is viable and can be done with little money.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的，而且用很少的钱就能完成。
words.en: If something is viable, it is capable of doing what it is intended to do.

words.ex: The teacher gave formative feedback to help students improve.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了影响形成的学习反馈，以帮助学生改进。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by the formation or development of something.

words.ex: The practicality of this tool makes it popular among workers.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具的实用性使它在工人中很受欢迎。
words.en: The quality of being suitable for a particular purpose or situation; the ability to be put to practical use.

words.tr: adj. 无能的；不起作用的
words.ex: His attempts to solve the problem were ineffectual.
words.ex_cn: 他试图解决问题的尝试是无效的。
words.en: If someone or something is ineffectual, they lack the ability or power to achieve something.

words.tr: adj. 有免疫力的；免疫的；不受影响的；
words.ex: Children are immune to this disease after vaccination.
words.ex_cn: 儿童接种疫苗后对这种疾病有免疫力。
words.en: If you are immune to a particular disease, you cannot be affected by it. If you are immune to something such as criticism, it does not affect you.

words.tr:
v. 移动；操控；
n. （熟练地）移动；
words.ex: He manoeuvred the car into a small parking space.
words.ex_cn: 他把车开进了一个小停车位。
words.en: A manoeuvre is a movement or series of movements requiring skill and care, especially in military tactics or in driving a vehicle. It can also refer to a clever or cunning plan or action designed to turn a situation to one's own advantage.

words.tr:
n. 精巧动作；军事演习；花招
v. （熟练地）移动；操控；算计
words.ex: The dancer's maneuver was breathtaking.
words.ex_cn: 舞者的精巧动作令人叹为观止。
words.en: A maneuver is a movement or series of movements requiring skill and care.

words.tr:
v. 策划
n. 决策者；出谋划策者
words.ex: He is the mastermind behind the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个计划的幕后主谋。
words.en: A mastermind is someone who plans and directs a complex and often devious scheme or enterprise.

words.tr:
n. 索具装备；钻探设备；装备
v. 配备索具；操纵；舞弊
words.ex: He uses a rig to hold the camera steady.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个支架来固定相机。
words.en: To rig something means to arrange or set it up in a particular way, often in a temporary or makeshift manner. It can also refer to the equipment used in drilling for oil or gas, or the sails and ropes on a ship.

words.ex: He won the game with great finesse.
words.ex_cn: 他以高超的技巧赢得了比赛。
words.en: If you finesse something, you handle it in a skillful and often slightly deceptive way.

words.tr: v. 大批出没于；成群滋扰；遍布于；寄生
words.ex: The bugs infest the old house.
words.ex_cn: 这些虫子侵袭了这栋老房子。
words.en: If creatures such as insects or rats infest a place, they are present in large numbers and usually cause damage or disease.

words.ex: He infringes the rules by arriving late.
words.ex_cn: 他因迟到而违反了规则。
words.en: To infringe means to violate or break a law, agreement, or right.

words.ex: Don't meddle in my affairs.
words.ex_cn: 别插手我的事情。
words.en: To meddle means to interfere in something that is not one's concern.

words.tr: v. 侵入；侵占；侵犯；侵蚀
words.ex: The new building encroaches on the park.
words.ex_cn: 新建筑侵占了公园。
words.en: To gradually take something such as power or authority from someone else, often in a way that is not fair or legal.

chapters.name: Part III 核心词汇 Lesson 27

words.tr:
v. 非法侵入；侵扰；冒犯
n. 非法进入；冒犯
words.ex: He trespasses on private land.
words.ex_cn: 他擅自进入私人土地。
words.en: To trespass is to enter someone's land or property without their permission.

words.ex: He embezzled money from his company.
words.ex_cn: 他从公司贪污了钱。
words.en: To embezzle means to steal or misappropriate money placed in one's trust or belonging to one's employer.

words.ex: The police seized illicit drugs from the suspect.
words.ex_cn: 警察从嫌疑人那里没收了非法毒品。
words.en: Illicit activities or substances are not allowed by law or by social or religious custom.

words.tr:
v. 扭打；混战
n. 扭打；混战
words.ex: The two boys had a scuffle over the ball.
words.ex_cn: 两个男孩为了球打了一架。
words.en: A scuffle is a short, confused fight or struggle at close quarters.

words.ex: He is grappled with the math problem for hours.
words.ex_cn: 他花了好几个小时努力解决这道数学题。
words.en: To grapple with something means to try hard to understand or deal with a difficult problem or subject.

words.tr:
n. 舷窗；天窗；气窗；煤斗；煤箱
v. 碎步疾跑；急忙撤退；（故意）破坏；凿沉（船）
words.ex: The sailor cleaned the scuttle to let in more light.
words.ex_cn: 水手清洁了舷窗，以便让更多的光线照进来。
words.en: To scuttle means to run hurriedly or furtively with short quick steps. It can also refer to a small opening in a ship's deck or hull, or a container for coal.

words.tr:
n. （船舷上的）排水孔
v. 故意沉船；破坏计划
words.ex: The sailor cleaned the scupper to let water drain out of the boat.
words.ex_cn: 水手清理了排水孔，让水从船上流出去。
words.en: To scupper something means to cause it to fail or to be ruined, especially a plan or a project. As a noun, it refers to an opening in the side of a ship at deck level that allows water to run off.

words.tr:
v. 将死；完全击败
n. 将死；完全失败
words.ex: He shouted checkmate after capturing the king.
words.ex_cn: 他在吃掉国王后大喊将死。
words.en: In chess, checkmate is a situation in which you cannot stop your king being captured and so you lose the game.

words.tr:
n. 虱子；寄生虫；卑鄙的家伙
v. 办砸；除虱子
words.ex: The boy has a louse in his hair.
words.ex_cn: 那个男孩头发里有一只虱子。
words.en: A louse is a small, wingless, parasitic insect that lives on the skin of mammals and birds. It can also refer to a contemptible person.

words.ex: He passed the test by a fluke.
words.ex_cn: 他靠运气通过了考试。
words.en: A fluke is an unexpected stroke of good luck or a surprising success that happens by chance.

words.tr: adj. 精选的；用手挑选的
words.ex: He only hires hand-picked employees.
words.ex_cn: 他只雇佣精选的员工。
words.en: If someone is hand-picked, they are carefully chosen for a particular purpose or job.

words.ex: She wore a dainty necklace with tiny pearls.
words.ex_cn: 她戴了一条小巧精致的珍珠项链。
words.en: If you describe something as dainty, you mean that it is small, delicate, and pretty.

words.tr: adj. 轻飘的；缥缈的；虚空的；精致的；
words.ex: The ethereal scarf floated gently in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 那条轻飘的围巾在风中轻轻飘动。
words.en: Something that is ethereal is extremely delicate and light in a way that seems not to be of this world.

words.ex: The cake is yummy.
words.ex_cn: 这个蛋糕很好吃。
words.en: If you describe food as yummy, you mean that it tastes extremely good.

words.ex: The soup was palatable after adding salt.
words.ex_cn: 加了盐后，汤变得可口美味了。
words.en: If you describe food or drink as palatable, you mean that it tastes pleasant.

words.ex: The cactus has succulent leaves to store water.
words.ex_cn: 仙人掌有多汁的叶子来储存水分。
words.en: (of food) tender, juicy, and tasty; (of a plant) having thick, fleshy tissues adapted to water storage.

words.tr: adj. 美味的；甘美的；满足感官的；性感的
words.ex: The fruit was luscious and sweet.
words.ex_cn: 这种水果甘甜可口。
words.en: If you describe something as luscious, you mean that it is very pleasant to taste, smell, look at, or listen to.

words.tr: adj. 淡而无味的；枯燥乏味的
words.ex: The soup was insipid and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这汤淡而无味，很无聊。
words.en: If you describe food or drink as insipid, you mean that it is very weak, tasteless, or uninteresting.

words.ex: The milk turned rancid after being left out.
words.ex_cn: 牛奶被放在外面后变酸了。
words.en: If food is rancid, it tastes or smells bad because it is no longer fresh.

words.ex: The fetid smell came from the old trash.
words.ex_cn: 那股恶臭来自旧垃圾。
words.en: Having an extremely unpleasant smell.

words.tr: adj. 有...气味的；令人想起...的
words.ex: The garden is redolent of roses.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园弥漫着玫瑰的香气。
words.en: Strongly reminiscent or suggestive of something.

words.ex: The rotten food has a bad odor.
words.ex_cn: 腐烂的食物有一种难闻的气味。
words.en: An odor is a particular and distinctive smell.

words.ex: The food has a bad odour.
words.ex_cn: 这食物有一种难闻的气味。
words.en: An odour is a particular and distinctive smell.

words.ex: His bounty helped the poor family survive winter.
words.ex_cn: 他的慷慨帮助这个贫困家庭度过了冬天。
words.en: If you say that someone is bountiful or does something in a bountiful way, you mean that they are very generous or that they give a lot of something.

words.tr:
adj. 奢侈的；慷慨给予的；挥霍的；过多的
v. 浪费；挥霍；慷慨给予
words.ex: He threw a lavish party for his birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的生日举办了一场奢华的派对。
words.en: If you describe something as lavish, you mean that it is very elaborate and impressive and a lot of money has been spent on it. If you say that someone is lavish in the way they behave, you mean that they give, spend, or use a lot of something.

words.tr:
adj. 挥霍的；丰富的；慷慨的；不吝惜的
n. 浪子
words.ex: The prodigal son returned home after years.
words.ex_cn: 那个浪子多年后回到了家。
words.en: A prodigal person spends money or resources in a way that is not careful and is too generous.

words.tr: adj. 猪一般的；贪婪的；自私的
words.ex: He is hoggish and never shares his food.
words.ex_cn: 他很自私，从不分享他的食物。
words.en: If you describe someone as hoggish, you are criticizing them for being greedy or selfish.

words.tr:
n. 油炸馅饼
v. 挥霍；浪费
words.ex: He frittered away his inheritance on gambling.
words.ex_cn: 他把继承来的遗产挥霍在赌博上。
words.en: If someone fritters away time or money, they waste it on unimportant or unnecessary things.

words.tr: n. 网球拍；喧闹；非法勾当；
words.ex: He bought a new racket for tennis.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一副新的网球拍。
words.en: A racket is a piece of equipment used in sports such as tennis or badminton, consisting of a handle and a round or oval frame with a network of strings stretched across it. It can also refer to a loud, unpleasant noise or a dishonest or fraudulent scheme.

words.ex: The children were boisterous at the party.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在聚会上喧闹不已。
words.en: Someone who is boisterous is noisy, lively, and full of energy.

words.ex: The quiet park is restful after a long day.
words.ex_cn: 漫长的一天后，安静的公园有助于休息。
words.en: A restful place or period of time is one that is peaceful and allows you to relax.

words.tr: v. 躺；靠在；向后倾斜（坐椅）
words.ex: He reclines on the sofa after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后躺在沙发上。
words.en: To recline means to lean or lie back in a relaxed position with the body supported.

words.ex: The rain gave us a short respite from the heat.
words.ex_cn: 这场雨为我们带来了短暂的凉爽缓解。
words.en: A respite is a short period of rest or relief from something difficult or unpleasant.

words.ex: He is prone to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If you are prone to a particular problem or characteristic, you are likely to be affected by it or to have it.

words.ex: He ensconced himself in the armchair with a book.
words.ex_cn: 他把自己安顿在扶手椅里看书。
words.en: If you ensconce yourself somewhere, you settle yourself there in a safe, comfortable, or secret place.

words.ex: The chickens roost on the branch at night.
words.ex_cn: 鸡晚上栖息在树枝上。
words.en: A roost is a place where birds rest or sleep. As a verb, to roost means for birds to settle or rest, typically for the night.

words.ex: They will dismantle the old bridge next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周将拆除这座旧桥。
words.en: To dismantle something means to take it to pieces.

words.ex: The police helped to defuse the situation.
words.ex_cn: 警察帮助减少了危险。
words.en: To remove the fuse from (an explosive device) in order to prevent it from exploding; to reduce the danger or tension in (a situation).

words.tr: v. 拆除窃听器；排除故障
words.ex: The technician came to debug the phone.
words.ex_cn: 技术人员来拆除电话里的窃听器。
words.en: To debug is to identify and remove errors from computer hardware or software.

words.ex: He unraveled the knotted string.
words.ex_cn: 他把打结的绳子拆散了。
words.en: To unravel means to separate or disentangle the threads of a fabric or a rope, or to solve or explain something that is complicated or mysterious.

words.ex: He had to lug the heavy box across the room.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不用力拖动那个沉重的箱子穿过房间。
words.en: To carry or drag something heavy with great effort.

words.tr:
v. 非法制造或售卖
adj. 非法制造或售卖的；盗版的
n. 私货；靴帮
words.ex: He sold bootleg movies near the station.
words.ex_cn: 他在车站附近卖盗版电影。
words.en: Bootleg refers to something, especially alcohol or recordings, that is made, distributed, or sold illegally.

words.tr:
n. 抽奖售物
v. 抽奖赠送（货品）
words.ex: He bought a ticket for the raffle.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一张抽奖票。
words.en: A raffle is a type of lottery in which people buy tickets for a chance to win a prize.

words.ex: They crossed the river on a wooden raft.
words.ex_cn: 他们乘着木筏渡过了河。
words.en: A raft is a flat structure made of pieces of wood tied together, which is used as a boat or floating platform.

words.tr: adj. 家庭般的；舒适自在的
words.ex: The little cabin feels homey and warm.
words.ex_cn: 这间小木屋感觉温馨而温暖。
words.en: If you describe a place or someone's house as homey, you mean it is nice, comfortable, and inviting.

words.tr:
adj. 有返回原地本能的；自动寻向的
v. 送…回家；提供住处；“home”的现在分词
words.ex: The pigeon is homing to its nest.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子正飞回它的巢。
words.en: Homing refers to the ability to return home or to a specific location, especially used in the context of animals or devices.

words.ex: He amass wealth by working hard.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作积累财富。
words.en: If you amass something such as money or information, you gradually collect a large amount of it.

words.tr:
n. 贮藏物；隐藏物
v. 贮藏；囤积
words.ex: The treasure hunter found a hoard of gold coins.
words.ex_cn: 寻宝者发现了一堆金币。
words.en: If you hoard things such as food or money, you save or store them, often in secret, because they are valuable or important to you.

words.ex: The farmer used a harrow to break up the soil.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用耙来松土。
words.en: A harrow is a piece of farm equipment that is used to break up and smooth out the surface of the soil.

words.tr:
n. 耙子；耙地机
v. 用耙子耙；扫掠过；搜索
words.ex: He uses a rake to collect leaves.
words.ex_cn: 他用耙子收集树叶。
words.en: A rake is a garden tool consisting of a row of metal or wooden teeth attached to a long handle. You use a rake to make the earth level or to gather leaves together.

words.tr:
n. 犁沟；车辙；皱纹
v. 犁耕；使皱眉头
words.ex: The farmer plowed a deep furrow in the field.
words.ex_cn: 农夫在田里犁出了一条深深的犁沟。
words.en: A furrow is a long narrow trench made in the ground by a plow, especially for planting seeds or for irrigation. It can also refer to a deep wrinkle on a person's face.

words.ex: The dog follows its owner every day.
words.ex_cn: 狗每天跟随它的主人。
words.en: To go or come after (a person or thing proceeding ahead); move or travel behind.

words.tr:
v. 潜伏；隐藏
n. 潜伏；埋伏
words.ex: A cat lurks behind the bush.
words.ex_cn: 一只猫躲在灌木丛后。
words.en: To lurk means to wait or move in a secretive way so that you cannot be seen, especially because you are about to attack someone or do something wrong.

words.tr: adj. 阴险的；潜伏的；暗中作祟的
words.ex: The insidious virus spread quietly through the town.
words.ex_cn: 这种隐蔽的病毒悄然在小镇蔓延。
words.en: Proceeding in a gradual, subtle way, but with harmful effects.

words.tr: adj. 泛滥的；猖獗的；蔓生的
words.ex: Rumors are rampant in the small town.
words.ex_cn: 谣言在这个小镇上四处流传。
words.en: If you describe something bad, such as a crime or disease, as rampant, you mean that it is very common and is increasing in an uncontrolled way.

words.tr: v. 使残废；使残缺不全；毁伤
words.ex: The accident mutilated his hand.
words.ex_cn: 事故使他的手残废了。
words.en: To mutilate something or someone means to damage them severely, for example by cutting off or destroying part of them.

words.ex: The main reason for his success is hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他成功的主要原因是努力工作。
words.en: The most important part or aspect of something.

words.tr:
n. 绳肌腱；腿筋
v. 割断腿筋；使不能正常工作
words.ex: He injured his hamstring during the soccer match.
words.ex_cn: 他在足球比赛中拉伤了绳肌腱。
words.en: A hamstring is a tendon at the back of a person's knee. If someone is hamstrung by something, it means they are severely restricted in their ability to act or perform.

words.tr:
adj. 向上游的；
adv. 向上游；
words.ex: The fish swam upstream to lay eggs.
words.ex_cn: 鱼逆流而上产卵。
words.en: In the direction that is opposite to the flow of a stream or river.

words.tr:
adv. 朝下游方向；
adj. 下游的；
words.ex: The boat moved downstream with the current.
words.ex_cn: 船顺流而下。
words.en: In the direction in which a stream or river flows; situated or moving in the direction of the flow of a stream or river.

words.ex: The bike ride is easy because it is downhill.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车很容易，因为是下山的。
words.en: If something or someone is moving downhill or is downhill, they are moving down a slope or are towards the bottom of a hill.

words.ex: The ball rebounded off the wall.
words.ex_cn: 球从墙上弹了回来。
words.en: To bounce back after hitting something; to recover in value, amount, or strength after a decrease or decline.

words.tr:
v. 倒退；退步；退化
n. 倒退；退步；退化
words.ex: The patient regressed to a childlike state after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故后，病人退回到了孩童般的状态。
words.en: If you regress, you return to a previous and less advanced stage of development.

words.ex: The dogs outnumber the cats in this neighborhood.
words.ex_cn: 这个社区里的狗比猫多。
words.en: If one group of people or things outnumbers another, the first group has more people or things in it than the second group.

words.ex: The benefits outweigh the risks.
words.ex_cn: 好处超过了风险。
words.en: If one thing outweighs another, the first thing is of greater importance, benefit, or significance than the second thing.

words.ex: The church runs an outreach to help homeless people.
words.ex_cn: 这家教堂开展外展服务来帮助无家可归者。
words.en: Outreach refers to the activity of an organization that provides a service or advice to people in the community, especially those who cannot or are unlikely to come to an office, a hospital, etc. for help.

words.tr: adj. 易恶心的；易受惊的；神经质的；过于拘谨的
words.ex: She was too squeamish to watch the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 她太容易呕吐了，不敢看手术过程。
words.en: If you are squeamish, you are easily upset by unpleasant sights or situations.

words.tr: adj. 神志不清的；极度兴奋的；发狂的
words.ex: He was delirious after the fever.
words.ex_cn: 他发烧后神志不清。
words.en: If someone is delirious, they are not able to think or speak in a sensible and reasonable way, usually because they are very ill and have a fever.

words.tr: adj. 发狂的；精神错乱状态的
words.ex: The demented man laughed loudly in the street.
words.ex_cn: 那个精神失常的男人在街上大声笑。
words.en: Someone who is demented behaves in a wild and uncontrolled way because they are mentally ill.

words.ex: They vie for the top prize.
words.ex_cn: 他们争夺最高奖项。
words.en: To compete eagerly with someone in order to do or achieve something.

words.ex: The new policy undercut the company's profits.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策削弱了公司的利润。
words.en: To undercut means to sell something at a lower price than a competitor, or to weaken something or someone.

words.ex: There is a dissonance between his words and actions.
words.ex_cn: 他的言行不一致。
words.en: A lack of harmony or agreement between people or things.

words.ex: The team acted in unison to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 团队一致行动赢得了比赛。
words.en: If two or more people do something in unison, they do it together at the same time.

words.tr: adj. （言行）谨慎的；不显眼的；朴素的
words.ex: He was discreet about his personal life.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的私生活很低调。
words.en: If you are discreet, you are polite and careful in what you do or say, because you want to avoid embarrassing or offending someone.

words.ex: He is scrupulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他检查作业时一丝不苟。
words.en: If you are scrupulous, you are careful, thorough, and extremely attentive to details.

words.ex: The door handle was unobtrusive and blended with the wall.
words.ex_cn: 门把手不显眼，与墙壁融为一体。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as unobtrusive, you mean that they are not easily noticed or do not draw attention to themselves.

words.tr: adj. 粗鲁的；莽撞的；唐突的
words.ex: He gave a brusque answer and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁地回答了一句，然后走开了。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as brusque, you mean that they deal with or say things quickly and shortly, so that they seem to be rude.

words.tr: v. 消散；“dissipate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The fog dissipated after sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 日出后，雾气消散了。
words.en: If you describe someone as dissipated, you disapprove of them because they spend a lot of time drinking alcohol and enjoying other physical pleasures, and are probably unhealthy because of this.

words.tr: v. 分泌唾液；垂涎；过量分泌唾液；
words.ex: The smell of food makes dogs salivate.
words.ex_cn: 食物的气味让狗分泌唾液。
words.en: If you salivate, you produce a lot of saliva in your mouth, often because you see or smell food that you would like to eat.

words.tr:
v. 流口水；垂涎；胡说
n. 口水；胡话
words.ex: The dog drools when it sees food.
words.ex_cn: 狗看到食物时会流口水。
words.en: If someone drools, saliva drops slowly from their mouth, often because they are thinking about food or are asleep.

words.ex: The flowers exude a sweet smell.
words.ex_cn: 花朵散发出甜美的香味。
words.en: If someone exudes a quality or feeling, or if it exudes, they show that they have it to a great extent.

chapters.name: Part III 核心词汇 Lesson 28

words.ex: He can articulate his ideas clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的想法。
words.en: If you describe someone as articulate, you mean that they are able to express their thoughts and ideas easily and clearly.

words.tr: v. 公开承认；宣布；声称
words.ex: He professes to love music.
words.ex_cn: 他声称自己热爱音乐。
words.en: If you profess to do or have something, you claim that you do it or have it.

words.tr:
v. 急促而含混不清地说
n. 急促不清的话
words.ex: The children gabble when they are excited.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们兴奋时会叽叽喳喳地说个不停。
words.en: If you gabble, you say things so quickly that it is difficult for people to understand you.

words.tr: v. 叽哩咕噜地叫；急促不清地说
words.ex: He gibbers when he is nervous.
words.ex_cn: 当他紧张时，他会胡言乱语。
words.en: To speak rapidly and unintelligibly, often in a state of panic or excitement.

words.ex: He blurted out the secret by accident.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心说出了秘密。
words.en: If someone blurts something, they say it suddenly, after trying hard to keep quiet or to keep it secret.

words.tr: v. 射精；射出；突然说出
words.ex: He cannot ejaculate due to medicine.
words.ex_cn: 由于药物，他无法射精。
words.en: To ejaculate means to say something suddenly and briefly, or to emit semen from the penis during orgasm.

words.tr:
v. 喘气；喘息
n. 气喘；喘息
words.ex: He panted after running up the stairs.
words.ex_cn: 他跑上楼梯后喘着气。
words.en: To breathe quickly and loudly through your mouth, usually because you have been doing something energetic.

words.tr:
v. 慢吞吞地说；拉长语调说话
n. 慢吞吞拉长调子的说话方式
words.ex: He speaks with a slow drawl.
words.ex_cn: 他说话慢吞吞的。
words.en: To speak slowly with vowels greatly prolonged.

words.tr:
v. （声音）颤抖
n. 颤抖的声音
words.ex: His voice quavers when he is nervous.
words.ex_cn: 当他紧张时，他的声音会颤抖。
words.en: If someone's voice quavers, it is unsteady because the person is uncertain, nervous, or upset.

words.ex: The baby babbles when she is happy.
words.ex_cn: 当宝宝开心时，她会含糊不清地说话。
words.en: To babble means to talk rapidly and continuously in a foolish, excited, or incomprehensible way.

words.tr:
v. 咕哝；含糊地说
n. 含糊的话；咕哝
words.ex: He mumbles when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，他会嘟囔。
words.en: If you mumble, you speak very quietly and not at all clearly with the result that the words are difficult to understand.

words.ex: He gesticulates when he talks about his travels.
words.ex_cn: 当他谈论旅行时，他会用手势示意。
words.en: If you gesticulate, you make movements with your arms and hands, usually while you are describing something that is difficult to express in words.

words.tr:
v. 咆哮；吼叫；（使）缠结
n. 咆哮（声）；缠结
words.ex: The dog snarls at strangers.
words.ex_cn: 狗对陌生人咆哮。
words.en: If an animal snarls, it makes a fierce, rough noise in its throat, usually to show anger.

words.ex: The old engine spluttered and then stopped.
words.ex_cn: 那台旧引擎发出劈啪声，然后熄火了。
words.en: If someone splutters, they make short sounds and have difficulty speaking clearly, for example because they are embarrassed or angry.

words.tr:
v. 呱呱地叫；发出低沉沙哑声
n. 呱呱的叫声
words.ex: The frog croaks loudly at night.
words.ex_cn: 青蛙晚上呱呱叫得很响。
words.en: To croak means to make a deep, harsh sound like that of a frog. It can also mean to die or to speak in a rough, low voice.

words.tr:
n. 说唱乐
v. 说唱；敲击
words.ex: He loves to rap about his life in the city.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢说唱自己在城市里的生活。
words.en: A type of music characterized by rhythmic and/or rhyming speech that is chanted or rapped.

words.tr:
v. 领会；抓紧；
n. 领会；
words.ex: I couldn't grasp the meaning of the poem.
words.ex_cn: 我没能领会这首诗的含义。
words.en: To grasp something means to take it in your hand and hold it firmly.

words.tr: adj. 健谈的；滔滔不绝的
words.ex: He is a voluble speaker who talks all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个健谈的人，整天说个不停。
words.en: If you describe someone as voluble, you mean that they talk a lot with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.tr:
adj. 急动的；颠簸的；抽筋的
n. 肉干
words.ex: His jerky movements made the camera footage blurry.
words.ex_cn: 他急动的动作让视频画面变得模糊。
words.en: If you describe something as jerky, you mean that it moves in a way that is not smooth, but rather with sudden stops and starts.

words.ex: The system will validate your password.
words.ex_cn: 系统将验证你的密码。
words.en: To validate something such as a claim or statement means to prove or confirm that it is true or correct.

words.ex: He proved his innocence to vindicate his name.
words.ex_cn: 他证明了自己的清白以洗清自己的名声。
words.en: To clear someone of blame or suspicion.

words.ex: The witness corroborated his story with photos.
words.ex_cn: 证人用照片证实了他的说法。
words.en: To corroborate something that has been said or reported means to provide evidence or information that supports it.

words.ex: He needs to substantiate his claim with evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他需要用证据来证实他的说法。
words.en: To substantiate a statement or a story means to supply evidence which proves that it is true.

words.tr: v. 回溯；将日期追溯到过去某时
words.ex: They backdate the contract to last month.
words.ex_cn: 他们把合同的日期回溯到上个月。
words.en: To backdate a document or agreement means to make its effective date earlier than the current date.

words.ex: He showed his credentials to get the job.
words.ex_cn: 他展示了资历来获得这份工作。
words.en: Credentials are documents that prove your identity or qualifications.

words.ex: The doctor will certify that you are healthy.
words.ex_cn: 医生将证明你身体健康。
words.en: To officially declare something to be true, correct, or genuine, often in writing.

words.ex: The detective tried to ascertain the truth.
words.ex_cn: 侦探试图查明真相。
words.en: If you ascertain the truth about something, you find out what it is, especially by making a deliberate effort to do so.

words.tr:
n. 审查员；检查员
v. 检查；审查
words.ex: The censor removed the bad words from the movie.
words.ex_cn: 审查员从电影中删除了粗俗用语。
words.en: A censor is a person who supervises conduct and morals: in particular, one who examines books, films, or other material for objectionable matter.

words.ex: The old woman gleaned wheat from the field after the harvest.
words.ex_cn: 这位老妇人在收割后从田里拾落穗。
words.en: To gather information or material bit by bit.

words.ex: The puppy frisks around the garden.
words.ex_cn: 小狗在花园里活蹦乱跳。
words.en: To frisk someone means to search them for weapons or illegal items by feeling their body with your hands.

words.ex: He delves into the history of ancient civilizations.
words.ex_cn: 他探究古代文明的历史。
words.en: If you delve into something, you try to discover new information about it by searching or investigating carefully.

words.tr:
n. 白鼬；雪貂
v. 用雪貂打猎；搜寻
words.ex: The ferret ran under the fence.
words.ex_cn: 白鼬从篱笆下跑过去了。
words.en: A ferret is a small, fierce animal which is used for hunting rabbits and rats. To ferret means to search for something persistently.

words.tr:
v. 搜寻；（动物）觅食；
n. 饲料；草料；
words.ex: The bear forages for berries in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这只熊在森林里搜寻浆果。
words.en: If you forage, you search for food or other supplies. Forage can also refer to food for animals, especially when it is grown or collected.

words.tr:
v. 搜寻；翻找；乱翻
n. 翻箱倒柜的寻找
words.ex: He rummaged through his drawer to find the keys.
words.ex_cn: 他翻找抽屉找钥匙。
words.en: If you rummage through something, you search for something you want by moving things around in a careless or hurried way.

words.tr:
v. 乱摸；摸索；笨手笨脚地做
n. 摸索；笨手笨脚
words.ex: He fumbled for his keys in the dark.
words.ex_cn: 他在黑暗中乱摸着找钥匙。
words.en: If you fumble with something, you try to hold, move, or find it with your hands in a clumsy way.

words.tr:
v. 逝去；过去
n. （光阴）逝去
words.ex: Two hours elapsed while he waited for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他等公交车时，两个小时过去了。
words.en: If time elapses, it passes.

words.ex: The tricky question eluded even the best students.
words.ex_cn: 这道难题难倒了即使是最优秀的学生。
words.en: If something that you want eludes you, you fail to obtain it. If you elude someone or something, you avoid them or escape from them.

words.ex: He tried to evade the police by driving fast.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过高速驾驶来逃避警察。
words.en: If you evade something, you find a way of not doing something that you really ought to do.

words.ex: He shirks his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天逃避作业。
words.en: If someone shirks their duties or responsibilities, they deliberately avoid doing them.

words.ex: He tries to eschew sugar for health reasons.
words.ex_cn: 他为了健康尽量避免吃糖。
words.en: If you eschew something, you deliberately avoid doing it or becoming involved in it.

words.tr:
v. 挡开；避开；回避
n. 挡开；闪避
words.ex: He parries the punch with his arm.
words.ex_cn: 他用胳膊格挡了这一拳。
words.en: If you parry a question or argument, you cleverly avoid answering it or dealing with it. In fencing, if you parry a blow, you defend yourself against it by pushing it away with your weapon.

words.tr:
v. 向旁侧避让；回避
n. 向侧方跨步
words.ex: He sidestepped the question during the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他在采访中回避了这个问题。
words.en: If you sidestep a problem or question, you avoid answering it or dealing with it.

words.ex: He loves to dance to funk music on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在周末随着放克音乐跳舞。
words.en: Funk can refer to a state of fear or depression, or to a style of music that combines elements of rhythm and blues, soul, and jazz.

words.tr:
n. 乳脂软糖；胡言
v. 敷衍；回避；捏造
words.ex: She made a fudge cake for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为聚会做了一个乳脂软糖蛋糕。
words.en: If you fudge something, you avoid making a clear and definite decision, distinction, or statement about it.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必然发生的
words.ex: The outcome was ineluctable.
words.ex_cn: 结果是不可避免的。
words.en: Something that is ineluctable cannot be avoided or escaped from.

words.ex: He extols the beauty of nature every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天赞美大自然的美。
words.en: If you extol something or someone, you praise them enthusiastically.

words.ex: The actor received acclaim for his performance.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员因他的表演而受到赞扬。
words.en: If someone or something is acclaimed, they are praised enthusiastically and publicly.

words.tr:
n. 圣歌；赞美诗；喊叫
v. 吟唱；诵扬；反复叫喊
words.ex: The monks sang a traditional chant during the morning prayer.
words.ex_cn: 修道士们在晨祷时唱了一首传统圣歌。
words.en: A chant is a word or group of words that is repeated over and over again. It can also refer to a simple song, especially one that is sung in a religious service.

words.ex: They revere their grandfather for his wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 他们因祖父的智慧而尊敬他。
words.en: If you revere someone or something, you respect and admire them greatly.

words.ex: He showed reverence for his grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他对祖父表示尊敬。
words.en: A feeling of profound respect for someone or something.

words.ex: The film is an homage to old Hollywood movies.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是对老好莱坞电影的致敬。
words.en: Homage is respect shown towards someone or something you admire, or to a person in authority.

words.ex: He tries to ingratiate himself with his boss by bringing coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上送咖啡给老板，试图讨好他。
words.en: If someone tries to ingratiate themselves with you, they do things to try and make you like them.

words.tr:
n. 幼鹿；浅黄褐色
v. 奉承；讨好
words.ex: The forest was filled with the sounds of baby fawns.
words.ex_cn: 森林里充满了幼鹿的叫声。
words.en: If someone fawns over you, they flatter you and show you too much attention.

words.tr:
n. （当众）侮辱；冒犯
v. （当众）侮辱；冒犯
words.ex: He felt an affront when they laughed at his idea.
words.ex_cn: 当他们嘲笑他的想法时，他感到受到了冒犯。
words.en: If something is an affront to you, it is an action or remark that insults or offends you.

words.tr:
n. 背后中伤；背后诽谤
v. 背后诽谤；背后中伤；“backbite”的现在分词
words.ex: He hates backbiting in the office.
words.ex_cn: 他讨厌在办公室里搬弄是非。
words.en: Backbiting is the act of saying unpleasant or unkind things about someone who is not present, especially in order to damage their reputation.

words.tr:
v. 含混不清地说话；诋毁；诽谤
n. 诽谤；诋毁；污辱
words.ex: He slurrs his words when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，说话含糊不清。
words.en: If someone slurs their speech or if their speech slurs, they do not pronounce each word clearly, because they are drunk, ill, or sleepy. A slur is an insulting remark which could damage someone's reputation.

words.tr: v. 诽谤；中伤；损毁名誉
words.ex: He tried to defame his rival with false stories.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用虚假的故事诋毁他的竞争对手。
words.en: To defame someone means to damage their reputation by saying or writing bad things about them that are not true.

words.ex: The article contained slanderous remarks about the company.
words.ex_cn: 这篇文章包含了对公司的诽谤性评论。
words.en: If something is slanderous, it falsely harms someone's reputation by saying something bad about them that is not true.

words.ex: His derogatory remarks hurt her feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他毁谤的言辞伤害了她的感情。
words.en: If you make a derogatory remark or comment about someone or something, you say something that shows you have a low opinion of them.

words.ex: They deride him for wearing old clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他们嘲笑他穿旧衣服。
words.en: If you deride someone or something, you say that they are stupid or have no value.

words.tr:
v. 暗笑；窃笑；吃吃地笑
n. 暗笑；窃笑；吃吃地笑
words.ex: He sniggered when his friend tripped.
words.ex_cn: 当他朋友摔倒时，他偷偷笑了。
words.en: To laugh in a half-suppressed, typically scornful way.

words.tr:
v. 嘲笑；嘲弄
n. 嘲笑；讥笑的言语
words.ex: The crowd began to jeer at the losing team.
words.ex_cn: 观众开始对落败的队伍嘘声四起。
words.en: To jeer means to laugh at someone or shout rude remarks at them in order to show that you do not respect them.

words.ex: He taunted his brother for losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他奚落弟弟比赛输了。
words.en: If someone taunts you, they say unkind or insulting things to you, especially about your weaknesses or failures.

words.tr:
n. 嘲笑；嘲弄
v. 嘲笑；狼吞虎咽
words.ex: His joke received a scoff from the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话引来了人群的嘲笑。
words.en: If you scoff at something, you speak about it in a way that shows you think it is ridiculous or inadequate.

words.tr:
n. 说笑；玩笑
v. 开玩笑
words.ex: He likes to jest with his friends during lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在午餐时和朋友开玩笑。
words.en: A jest is a remark that is intended to be amusing or funny, especially one that is made in a light-hearted or teasing manner.

words.tr:
n. 轻松说笑
v. 轻松说笑
words.ex: They enjoy banter during lunch break.
words.ex_cn: 他们在午餐休息时喜欢开玩笑。
words.en: the playful and friendly exchange of teasing remarks

words.tr: v. （以可望而不可即之物）逗引；使干着急
words.ex: The smell of food cooking in the kitchen began to tantalise him.
words.ex_cn: 厨房里做饭的香味开始让他垂涎欲滴。
words.en: If you tantalise someone, you tease or torment them by offering them something they want but then withholding it or making it difficult to obtain.

words.tr: v. （以可望而不可及之物）逗引；使干着急
words.ex: The smell of cookies tantalize him.
words.ex_cn: 饼干的香味让他垂涎欲滴。
words.en: If someone or something tantalizes you, they make you feel hopeful and excited about getting what you want, usually before disappointing you by not letting you have it.

words.tr:
n. 漫画；讽刺画；滑稽模仿
v. 画成漫画讽刺
words.ex: He drew a caricature of the teacher with big eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一幅老师大眼睛的漫画。
words.en: A caricature is a drawing or description of someone that exaggerates their appearance or behavior in a humorous or critical way.

words.tr: adj. 扭歪的；啼笑皆非的；挖苦的；讽刺的
words.ex: He gave a wry smile when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个消息时露出了苦笑。
words.en: If someone has a wry expression, it shows that they find a bad situation or a change in a situation slightly amusing.

words.ex: His oversight caused the project to fail.
words.ex_cn: 他的疏忽导致项目失败。
words.en: An oversight is a mistake that is made by not noticing something or by forgetting to do something.

words.ex: He abased himself before the king.
words.ex_cn: 他在国王面前贬低自己。
words.en: To abase someone or something means to lower them in rank, status, or esteem.

words.ex: He tried to debase the coin with cheap metal.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用廉价金属贬低硬币的价值。
words.en: To debase something means to reduce its value or quality.

words.ex: The soil degrades over time without proper care.
words.ex_cn: 如果没有适当照料，土壤会逐渐退化。
words.en: If something degrades or is degraded, it becomes worse in quality, or weaker in power or status.

words.ex: The manager decided to demote him for poor performance.
words.ex_cn: 经理因他表现不佳决定降职他。
words.en: If someone is demoted, they are given a lower rank or a less important position than they had before.

words.ex: The car depreciates every year.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车每年都会贬值。
words.en: If something such as a currency depreciates or if something depreciates it, it loses some of its original value.

words.ex: His rude words detract from the beauty of the speech.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话贬损了演讲的优美。
words.en: If one thing detracts from another, it makes it seem less good or impressive.

words.tr:
v. 使降低；使降级
n. 下坡路
words.ex: The company decided to downgrade the software version.
words.ex_cn: 公司决定将软件版本降级。
words.en: To downgrade something means to reduce its quality, value, or status.

words.ex: The team was relegated to the second division after losing all their games.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍在输掉所有比赛后被降级到第二级别联赛。
words.en: If you relegate someone or something to a less important position, you give them this position.

words.tr: v.  使中毒；使醉；使 ...陶醉
words.ex: The dirty water can intoxicate animals.
words.ex_cn: 脏水会使动物中毒。
words.en: To intoxicate someone means to make them lose control of their actions or behavior because they have drunk alcohol or taken drugs. It can also mean to make someone feel very excited and happy.

words.ex: The woman was ravished by a stranger.
words.ex_cn: 这名女子被一名陌生人强奸了。
words.en: If you are ravished by something, you are filled with delight and wonder by it.

chapters.name: Part III 核心词汇 Lesson 29

words.tr:
n. 骗局；欺骗
v. 欺骗；诈骗
words.ex: He fell for a con and lost all his money.
words.ex_cn: 他上了一个骗局的当，失去了所有钱。
words.en: If someone cons you, they persuade you to do something or believe something by telling you things that are not true.

words.ex: He diddle the old man out of his money.
words.ex_cn: 他欺骗了那位老人，骗走了他的钱。
words.en: To diddle means to cheat or swindle someone, often out of money, or to waste time in a trivial or aimless manner.

words.ex: He deluded himself into thinking he would win.
words.ex_cn: 他欺骗自己，以为自己会赢。
words.en: If you delude yourself, you let yourself believe that something is true, even though it is not true.

words.tr:
n. 被愚弄的人；容易受骗的人
v. 欺骗；诈骗；愚弄
words.ex: He was duped into buying a fake watch.
words.ex_cn: 他被骗去买了一块假手表。
words.en: A dupe is someone who is easily deceived or cheated, often because they are too trusting. As a verb, to dupe means to deceive or trick someone into believing something that is not true.

words.ex: He tried to hoodwink her with a fake story.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用一个虚假的故事欺骗她。
words.en: To deceive or trick someone.

words.tr:
n. 欺诈；谎话；骗子
v. 欺骗；行骗
words.ex: He was accused of being a humbug and spreading false information.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控为骗子，散布虚假信息。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behaviour as humbug, you mean that it is dishonest or insincere.

words.tr:
n. 骗局；恶作剧；戏弄
v. 愚弄
words.ex: The news was a hoax to scare people.
words.ex_cn: 这则新闻是个骗局，为了吓唬人。
words.en: A hoax is a plan to deceive someone, such as telling the police there is a bomb somewhere when there is not, or a trick in which someone tells people a lie.

words.ex: The company made fraudulent claims about its product.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司对其产品做出了欺诈性的声明。
words.en: A fraudulent activity is deceitful or dishonest.

words.ex: The slimy worm crawled on the ground.
words.ex_cn: 那条滑腻的蠕虫在地上爬行。
words.en: Something that is slimy is covered in a thick, slippery substance, or has a thick, slippery texture.

words.tr: n. 奸诈；欺骗；口是心非
words.ex: He showed duplicity by lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他通过对朋友撒谎表现出虚伪。
words.en: If you accuse someone of duplicity, you mean that they are deceitful.

words.tr: adj. 不直接的；不正直的；迂回的；
words.ex: He gave a devious answer to avoid telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个不直接的回答，以避免说出真相。
words.en: If you describe someone as devious, you mean that they are dishonest and unfair in the way that they behave, often by using indirect methods to achieve their aims.

words.ex: He admitted his infidelity after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争吵后承认了自己的不忠行为。
words.en: Infidelity refers to the action or state of being unfaithful to a spouse or other sexual partner.

words.tr: adj. 人为的；非自然产生的
words.ex: The success of the movie was attributed to factitious marketing strategies.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的成功归因于人为的营销策略。
words.en: If you describe a situation or emotion as factitious, you mean that it has been created or developed deliberately, rather than happening naturally.

words.ex: He is a bona fide expert in history.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位真正的历史专家。
words.en: Made in good faith without fraud or deceit.

words.tr: adj. 坦率的；坦诚的；偷拍的
words.ex: He gave a candid answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了坦率的回答。
words.en: If you are candid, you are honest and say what you really think.

words.tr: adj. 单纯的；天真的；坦率的
words.ex: He gave an ingenuous smile when he told the truth.
words.ex_cn: 当他讲真话时，他露出了天真无邪的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as ingenuous, you mean that they are innocent, trusting, and honest, often in a way that seems naive.

words.tr: adj. 虔诚的；衷心的；诚挚的；
words.ex: He is a devout Christian who goes to church every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名虔诚的基督徒，每周日都去教堂。
words.en: If you describe someone as devout, you mean that they have a deep religious faith.

words.tr: adj. 直截了当的；直率的；坦白的
words.ex: He is forthright about his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他坦率地承认自己的错误。
words.en: If you describe someone as forthright, you admire them because they show clearly and strongly what they think and feel.

words.ex: He is downright lazy.
words.ex_cn: 他完全懒惰。
words.en: You use downright to emphasize that something is completely the case, especially when you are describing something bad or negative.

words.tr:
adv. 彻底地；立刻地；
adj. 完全的；彻底的；
words.ex: He refused the offer outright.
words.ex_cn: 他彻底拒绝了这个提议。
words.en: If something is done outright, it is done completely and without any hesitation or attempt to hide it.

words.tr:
adv. 光明正大地
adj. 光明正大的
words.ex: He always plays aboveboard in business.
words.ex_cn: 他在商业中总是光明正大。
words.en: If something is aboveboard, it is done in an honest and open way without any attempt to deceive.

words.tr: adj. 公正的；正当的；正义的
words.ex: He is a righteous man who helps the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个帮助穷人的正直的人。
words.en: If you think that someone behaves or lives in a way that is morally good, you can say that they are righteous.

words.ex: The intrepid explorer climbed the high mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这位无畏的探险家爬上了高山。
words.en: If you describe someone as intrepid, you mean that they are brave, fearless, and willing to do things that might be dangerous.

words.tr: adj. 大丈夫气概的；刚毅的；勇敢的
words.ex: He showed a manful determination to overcome his challenges.
words.ex_cn: 他表现出克服挑战的勇敢决心。
words.en: If you describe a man's behaviour as manful, you mean that he behaves in a way which is traditionally considered to be brave and strong.

words.ex: The gallant soldier saved his comrades in battle.
words.ex_cn: 这位英勇的士兵在战斗中救了他的战友们。
words.en: If someone is gallant, they behave bravely and honorably in a dangerous or difficult situation. It can also describe someone who is very polite and kind towards women.

words.ex: He is bashful when he speaks in front of people.
words.ex_cn: 当他当着大家说话时，他很害羞。
words.en: If someone is bashful, they are shy and easily embarrassed.

words.ex: He was called effeminate for wearing pink.
words.ex_cn: 他因为穿粉色被说娘娘腔。
words.en: If you describe a man or his behaviour as effeminate, you mean that he behaves, looks, or sounds like a woman or girl.

words.tr:
adj. 崇高的；壮丽的；极端的；过分的
v. 变高尚；升华
n. 庄严；崇高；顶点
words.ex: The view from the mountain is sublime.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色是壮丽的。
words.en: If you describe something as sublime, you mean that it has a wonderful quality that affects you deeply.

words.tr: v. 使成贵族；使高贵；使受尊敬
words.ex: The king will ennoble the brave soldier.
words.ex_cn: 国王将封赏这位勇敢的士兵。
words.en: To ennoble someone means to make them a member of the nobility, or to make them seem morally or socially superior.

words.tr: adj. 平民的；卑贱的；卑鄙的；不光彩的
words.ex: He came from an ignoble family, but worked hard to succeed.
words.ex_cn: 他出身于平民家庭，但努力工作以取得成功。
words.en: If you describe something as ignoble, you mean that it is bad and something to be ashamed of.

words.tr: adj. 无道德观念的；不辨是非的
words.ex: He made an amoral decision to lie for money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了钱做出了一个不道德的决定。
words.en: If you describe someone as amoral, you mean that they do not consider whether their behavior is morally right or wrong.

words.ex: The wanton destruction of the forest shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 对森林的恣意破坏让每个人都感到震惊。
words.en: If someone describes a person or their behaviour as wanton, they are critical of them for behaving in a very uncontrolled or unacceptable way, often without caring about the consequences.

words.ex: The obscene behavior shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这种可憎的行为让所有人都震惊了。
words.en: If you describe something as obscene, you mean it offends you because it relates to sex or violence in a way that you think is unpleasant and shocking.

words.ex: His ribald jokes were inappropriate for a family gathering.
words.ex_cn: 他的下流笑话不适合家庭聚会。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behavior as ribald, you mean that it refers to sex in a rude or humorous way.
