words.en: If you describe someone as greedy, you mean that they want to have more of something such as food or money than is necessary or fair.

words.ex: He grimaced when he tasted the bitter medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他喝下苦涩的药时皱起了脸。
words.en: A grimace is an ugly, twisted expression on a person's face, usually because they are experiencing pain or strong feelings.

words.ex: The grime on the window made it hard to see outside.
words.ex_cn: 窗户上的尘垢让外面看不清楚。
words.en: Grime is dirt which has collected on the surface of something.

words.ex: He wore a big grin after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得比赛后露出了灿烂的咧嘴笑容。
words.en: If you grin, you smile broadly, usually showing your teeth.

words.ex: He grinds the coffee beans into powder.
words.ex_cn: 他把咖啡豆碾成粉末。
words.en: To reduce something to small particles or powder by crushing it.

words.tr:
v. 发牢骚；抱怨；轰鸣
n. 怨言；牢骚；轰隆声
words.ex: He grumbles when he has to wake up early.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不早起时就会抱怨。
words.en: If someone grumbles, they complain about something in a bad-tempered way.

words.tr:
v. 保证；确保；
n. 保证；保证书；
words.ex: The store guarantees a refund if you are not happy.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不满意，商店保证退款。
words.en: A guarantee is a formal promise that certain conditions will be fulfilled, especially that a product will be repaired or replaced if it is not of a specified quality.

words.ex: He is gullible and believes every story he hears.
words.ex_cn: 他很容易受骗，相信每一个他听到的故事。
words.en: If you describe someone as gullible, you mean they are easily tricked because they are too trusting.

words.ex: He goes to the gym every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上去健身房。
words.en: A gym is a place equipped for physical exercise and training, especially for athletes or for people who want to keep fit.

words.ex: They play basketball in the gymnasium.
words.ex_cn: 他们在体育馆打篮球。
words.en: A gymnasium is a large room or building with equipment for exercising the body and increasing strength.

chapters.name: 附录1 最常考专四词回顾 H

words.ex: The teacher gave us a handout about photosynthesis.
words.ex_cn: 老师发给我们一份关于光合作用的讲义。
words.en: A handout is a document which contains news or information about something and which is given, for example, to journalists or to people attending a talk or lecture.

words.ex: The desert has a harsh climate.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠的气候非常严酷。
words.en: If you describe something as harsh, you mean that it is extremely difficult and unpleasant to live in, do, or experience, especially because it is very cold, hot, or violent.

words.tr:
v. 拖；拉；拖运；
n. 拖；拉；拖运；
words.ex: He hauled the heavy box across the room.
words.ex_cn: 他把沉重的箱子拖过了房间。
words.en: To haul something means to pull it or carry it with a lot of effort.

words.ex: The memory of the accident still haunts him.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故的记忆仍然长期困扰着他。
words.en: If something unpleasant haunts you, you keep thinking or worrying about it over a long period of time. A place that is haunted is believed to be visited regularly by a ghost.

words.ex: The broken glass is a hazard.
words.ex_cn: 碎玻璃是危险。
words.en: A hazard is something which could be dangerous to you, your health or safety, or your plans or reputation.

words.tr: n. 听力；听觉； v. 听；听见；“hear”的现在分词；
words.ex: His hearing is getting worse with age.
words.ex_cn: 他的听力随着年龄增长而变差。
words.en: The ability to perceive sounds; a session in which evidence and arguments are presented to a court or committee.

words.tr:
n. 树篱；防范措施
v. 用树篱围住；限制；避免
words.ex: He planted a hedge around his garden.
words.ex_cn: 他在花园周围种了一排树篱。
words.en: A hedge is a row of bushes or small trees which have been planted along the edge of a garden, field, or road to separate it from another area or to protect it. As a verb, to hedge means to avoid committing oneself or to limit or qualify something by conditions or exceptions.

words.ex: The helicopter flew over the city.
words.ex_cn: 直升机飞过了城市。
words.en: A helicopter is a type of aircraft that derives both lift and propulsion from one or more sets of horizontally revolving overhead rotors. It is capable of moving vertically and horizontally, the direction of motion being controlled by the pitch of the rotor blades.

words.tr:
n. 兽群；
v. 放牧；
words.ex: The herd of cows walked slowly to the pasture.
words.ex_cn: 一群牛缓缓走向牧场。
words.en: A herd is a large group of animals of one kind that live together.

words.tr:
v. 突出；强调；高光；
n. 最突出的部分；
words.ex: The teacher highlighted the key words in the text.
words.ex_cn: 老师把文中的关键词突出了。
words.en: To highlight something means to make it stand out or to emphasize it, often because it is important or interesting.

words.ex: Hitherto, no one has solved the problem.
words.ex_cn: 迄今为止，没有人解决过这个问题。
words.en: Until now or until the point in time under discussion.

words.tr:
n. 猪；贪婪的人
v. 攫取；独占
words.ex: The hog is eating corn in the farm.
words.ex_cn: 这头猪在农场里吃玉米。
words.en: A hog is a domesticated pig, especially one that is raised for its meat. It can also refer to a greedy or selfish person. As a verb, to hog means to take or use more than one's fair share of something.

words.tr: n. 地平线；思想等的范围；眼界；
words.ex: The sun set below the horizon.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在地平线以下落山。
words.en: The horizon is the line at which the earth's surface and the sky appear to meet.

words.ex: The cow has two long horns.
words.ex_cn: 这头牛有两只长角。
words.en: A horn is a pointed projection on the head of various animals, consisting of a core of bone surrounded by a sheath of keratin, or a device for making a loud warning noise.

words.ex: There was clear hostility between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居之间明显存在敌意。
words.en: Hostility is unfriendly or aggressive behaviour towards people or ideas.

words.tr: n. 人性；人类；人道；仁慈；
words.ex: Kindness shows the best of humanity.
words.ex_cn: 善良展现了人性中最美好的一面。
words.en: Humanity refers to all human beings collectively or the qualities that make us human, such as kindness, compassion, and the ability to reason.

words.tr: adj. 歇斯底里的；异常激动的
words.ex: She became hysterical when she lost her wallet.
words.ex_cn: 她丢了钱包时变得歇斯底里。
words.en: If someone is hysterical, they are in a state of uncontrolled excitement, anger, or panic, often because of a shock or a very upsetting experience.

chapters.name: 附录1 最常考专四词回顾 I

words.ex: He can identify the bird by its song.
words.ex_cn: 他能通过鸟的叫声识别它。
words.en: If you can identify someone or something, you are able to recognize them or distinguish them from others.

words.ex: He showed his identity card to enter the building.
words.ex_cn: 他出示了身份证以进入大楼。
words.en: Your identity is who you are, or the qualities of a person or group that make them different from others.

words.ex: He called his friend an idiot after the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他在犯错后称朋友是白痴。
words.en: An idiot is a person who is considered to be very stupid or foolish.

words.ex: It is illegal to drive without a license.
words.ex_cn: 无证驾驶是非法的。
words.en: If something is illegal, the law says that it is not allowed.

words.ex: The lamp illuminate the dark room.
words.ex_cn: 这盏灯照亮了黑暗的房间。
words.en: To illuminate something means to shine light on it and to make it brighter and more visible.

words.ex: The mirror creates an illusion of a bigger room.
words.ex_cn: 镜子制造出房间更大的错觉。
words.en: An illusion is a false idea or belief, especially about yourself or your situation.

words.ex: The child imitates her mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子模仿她妈妈的声音。
words.en: If you imitate someone, you copy what they do or produce.

words.ex: The necklace is an imitation made of plastic.
words.ex_cn: 这条项链是用塑料做的仿制品。
words.en: An imitation of something is a copy of it.

words.ex: The mountain is immense.
words.ex_cn: 这座山非常巨大。
words.en: Extremely large or great, especially in scale or degree.

words.ex: The immigrant found a job in the city.
words.ex_cn: 这位移民在城市里找到了一份工作。
words.en: An immigrant is a person who comes to live permanently in a foreign country.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生的；临近的；
words.ex: An imminent storm is coming soon.
words.ex_cn: 一场即将发生的风暴很快就要来了。
words.en: If you say that something is imminent, especially something unpleasant, you mean it is almost certain to happen very soon.

words.tr:
n. 影响力；冲击（力）；
v. 对…产生影响；
words.ex: The new law had a big impact on education.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律对教育产生了重大影响。
words.en: The effect or influence of one person, thing, or action, on another.

words.ex: The president may be impeached for lying.
words.ex_cn: 总统可能因撒谎而被弹劾。
words.en: If a government official is impeached, they are formally charged with a serious crime in a special government court.

words.ex: The imperial palace was built long ago.
words.ex_cn: 这座帝国宫殿是很久以前建造的。
words.en: relating to an empire or an emperor; majestic or superior in quality or size

words.ex: The government will implement new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将实施新规定。
words.en: To implement something means to ensure that what has been planned is done.

words.tr: n. 含意；可能的影响（或后果）；暗示；
words.ex: The implication of his words was that he was sorry.
words.ex_cn: 他话中的含意是他很抱歉。
words.en: An implication is a possible future effect or result of an action or decision, often one that is not immediately obvious.

words.ex: The government imposed a new tax on sugar.
words.ex_cn: 政府对糖征收了一项新税。
words.en: To impose means to officially force a rule, tax, punishment, etc. to be obeyed or received.

words.ex: The bonus is an incentive to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 奖金是努力工作的动机。
words.en: Something that encourages a person to do something or to work harder.

words.ex: The dark clouds indicate rain.
words.ex_cn: 乌云表明要下雨了。
words.en: If one thing indicates another, the first thing shows that the second is true or exists.

words.tr: adj. 不感兴趣的；不关心的；
words.ex: He was indifferent to the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影不感兴趣。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being indifferent to something, you mean that they have a complete lack of interest in it.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必定的；
words.ex: It is inevitable that the sun will rise tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳明天一定会升起。
words.en: If something is inevitable, it is certain to happen and cannot be prevented or avoided.

words.ex: This product is inferior to the other one.
words.ex_cn: 这个产品比另一个差。
words.en: If one person or thing is inferior to another, they are not as good, important, or valuable as the other person or thing.

words.ex: The price of bread went up because of inflation.
words.ex_cn: 由于通货膨胀，面包的价格上涨了。
words.en: Inflation is a general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money.

words.ex: He is an influential teacher in our school.
words.ex_cn: 他是我们学校一位有影响力的老师。
words.en: Having great influence on someone or something.

words.ex: The inhabitant lives in a small house.
words.ex_cn: 这位居民住在一所小房子里。
words.en: An inhabitant of a place is one of the people who live there.

words.ex: Honesty is an inherent quality of a good leader.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是好领导固有的品质。
words.en: Existing in something as a permanent, essential, or characteristic attribute.

words.ex: He inherited a house from his father.
words.ex_cn: 他从父亲那里继承了一所房子。
words.en: If you inherit something such as a trait, characteristic, or quality, you are born with it, because your parents or ancestors had it. If you inherit money or property, you receive it from someone who has died.

words.tr: n. 倡议；主动权；自发性；措施；
words.ex: The school launched an initiative to reduce plastic use.
words.ex_cn: 学校发起了一项减少塑料使用的倡议。
words.en: An initiative is an important act or statement that is intended to solve a problem.

words.ex: The company values innovation in its products.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司重视产品的创新。
words.en: Innovation is the introduction of new ideas, methods, or things.

words.ex: There are innumerable stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有数不清的星星。
words.en: Too many to be counted; very many.

words.ex: His insight helped the team solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他的洞察力帮助团队解决了问题。
words.en: If you gain insight or an insight into a complex situation or problem, you gain an accurate and deep understanding of it.

words.tr: n. 检查；视察；查看；审视；
words.ex: The teacher did an inspection of the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 老师对教室进行了检查。
words.en: An inspection is an official visit to a building or organization to check that everything is satisfactory and that rules are being obeyed.

words.ex: He will install the new software on his computer.
words.ex_cn: 他将在他的电脑上安装新软件。
words.en: To set up or fix in position for use or service.

words.ex: The hospital is a public institution.
words.ex_cn: 这家医院是一家公共机构。
words.en: An institution is a large important organization such as a university, church, or bank.

words.ex: The vase remained intact after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 花瓶从高处摔下后依然完整无缺。
words.en: Something that is intact is complete and has not been damaged or changed.

words.ex: Honesty is an integral part of a good relationship.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是良好关系中不可或缺的一部分。
words.en: Something that is integral is very important or necessary. If something is an integral part of a whole, it is an essential part of that whole.

words.ex: He tried to integrate into the new school community.
words.ex_cn: 他试图融入新的学校群体。
words.en: If someone integrates into a social group, or is integrated into it, they behave in such a way that they become part of the group or are accepted into it.

words.ex: He lost his job because of his integrity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为正直而失去了工作。
words.en: Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.

words.ex: There is little intercourse between the two villages.
words.ex_cn: 这两个村庄之间很少交往。
words.en: Intercourse refers to communication or dealings between individuals or groups, or sexual activity between people.

words.tr:
n. 内部；
adj. 内部的；
words.ex: The interior of the house is very cozy.
words.ex_cn: 房子的内部非常舒适。
words.en: The interior of something is the inside part of it.

words.ex: He interprets the poem as a love story.
words.ex_cn: 他把这首诗解释为一个爱情故事。
words.en: If you interpret something in a particular way, you decide that this is its meaning or significance.

words.ex: He interrupted me while I was speaking.
words.ex_cn: 我在说话时他打断了我。
words.en: To interrupt someone means to stop them from speaking by saying or doing something, or to cause something to stop happening for a period of time.

words.ex: There is a five-minute interval between the two classes.
words.ex_cn: 两节课之间有五分钟的间隔。
words.en: An interval is a period of time between two events or dates.

words.tr: adj. 永无变化的；始终如一的
words.ex: The speed of light is invariable.
words.ex_cn: 光速是不变的。
words.en: An invariable thing or quality never changes or is always the same.

words.ex: He invests money in stocks.
words.ex_cn: 他投资股票。
words.en: If you invest in something, or if you invest a sum of money, you use your money in a way that you hope will increase its value, for example by putting it in a bank, or buying shares or property.

words.ex: The police will investigate the accident.
words.ex_cn: 警方将调查这起事故。
words.en: If someone, especially an official, investigates an event, situation, or claim, they try to find out what happened or what is the truth.

words.ex: He made an investment in a small business.
words.ex_cn: 他投资了一家小企业。
words.en: An investment is an amount of money that you invest in something.

words.ex: The project involves simple math and writing.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目包括简单的数学和写作。
words.en: If a situation or activity involves something, that thing is a necessary part or consequence of it.

words.ex: The ship sailed inward toward the harbor.
words.ex_cn: 船向港口内航行。
words.en: Directed or moving towards the inside; relating to the inside or inner part of something.

words.ex: The hospital will isolate the patient to stop the spread.
words.ex_cn: 医院将隔离这名病人以防止传播。
words.en: To isolate someone or something means to separate them from other people or things, often in order to protect them or to prevent the spread of something harmful.

chapters.name: 附录1 最常考专四词回顾 K

words.tr: adj. 渴望的；热心的；敏锐的；
words.ex: He is keen to learn English.
words.ex_cn: 他渴望学习英语。
words.en: If you are keen on doing something, you very much want to do it. If you are keen that something should happen, you very much want it to happen.

chapters.name: 附录1 最常考专四词回顾 L

words.tr: n. 迷宫；难解的事件；错综复杂；
words.ex: The child got lost in the labyrinth.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在迷宫里迷路了。
words.en: A labyrinth is a complicated irregular network of passages or paths in which it is difficult to find one's way; a maze.

words.tr:
v. 发射；发起；启动；
n. 发射；投掷；启动；
words.ex: They will launch a rocket tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天将发射一枚火箭。
words.en: To launch something means to send it into the air, space, or water, especially with a lot of force or effort, or to start an activity, event, or project.

words.ex: He is a Nobel laureate for his poetry.
words.ex_cn: 他因诗歌而获得诺贝尔奖。
words.en: A laureate is someone who has been given a prize or honor for achievement in a particular field, especially in the arts or sciences.

words.ex: The children play on the lawn after school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们放学后在草坪上玩耍。
words.en: A lawn is an area of grass that is kept cut short and is usually part of someone's garden or yard, or part of a park.

words.tr:
n. 跳跃；
v. 跳跃；
words.ex: The cat made a big leap over the fence.
words.ex_cn: 猫跳过了篱笆。
words.en: To leap means to jump high or a long way, or to move quickly and with a lot of energy.

words.ex: The new legislation bans plastic bags.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法规禁止使用塑料袋。
words.en: Legislation refers to the process of making or enacting laws by a government or other authority.

words.ex: He reads books in his leisure.
words.ex_cn: 他在空闲时间读书。
words.en: Leisure is the time when you are not working and you can relax and do things that you enjoy.

words.tr:
adj. 开明的；自由主义的；
n. 自由党党员；
words.ex: He is a liberal teacher who listens to students.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位开明的老师，会倾听学生的声音。
words.en: A liberal person, system, or policy is one that is in favour of allowing people a lot of freedom in their behaviour or opinions.

words.ex: The limitation of the phone is its short battery life.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的限制是电池续航时间短。
words.en: A limitation is a rule or situation that restricts what you can do or what can happen.

words.ex: The farmer feeds his livestock every morning.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每天早上喂他的家畜。
words.en: Livestock are animals such as cattle and sheep which are kept on a farm.

words.tr: adj. 高的；崇高的；傲慢的
words.ex: The mountain has a lofty peak.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一个很高的山顶。
words.en: If you say that someone behaves in a lofty way, you are critical of them for behaving in a proud and rather unpleasant way, as if they think they are very important.

words.tr:
n. 织布机；
v. 迫近；
words.ex: The old loom made a loud clicking sound.
words.ex_cn: 那台旧织布机发出很大的咔嗒声。
words.en: If something looms over you, it appears as a large or unclear shape, often in a way that is frightening or causes worry.

words.ex: We waited in the lounge before our flight.
words.ex_cn: 我们在登机前等在休息室里。
words.en: A lounge is a room in a house or public building where people can sit and relax. As a verb, to lounge means to lie, sit, or stand in a relaxed or lazy way.

words.tr: adj. 较低的；下游的；“low”的比较级； v. 降低；
words.ex: He sat in the lower row of the theater.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在剧院的较低一排。
words.en: If you lower something, you move it slowly downwards. If you lower something, you make it less in amount, degree, value, or quality.

words.ex: His loyalty to his friends never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的忠诚从未改变。
words.en: The quality of being loyal to someone or something.

chapters.name: 附录1 最常考专四词回顾 M

words.tr: n. 机械（总称）；机械装置；
words.ex: The factory uses old machinery to produce goods.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂使用旧机械来生产产品。
words.en: Machinery refers to machines in general or the parts of a machine that make it work.

words.ex: He acted out of malice, not mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他是出于恶意，而不是错误。
words.en: Malice is behavior that is intended to harm people or their reputations, or cause them embarrassment and upset.

words.ex: He tried to manipulate the results to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他试图操纵结果来赢得比赛。
words.en: To manipulate something means to handle or control it skillfully, often in a way that is considered unfair or dishonest.

words.tr:
n. 制造；
v. （用机器大量）制造；虚构；捏造；
words.ex: The manufacture of cars needs many workers.
words.ex_cn: 汽车的制造需要很多工人。
words.en: To manufacture something means to make it in a factory, usually in large quantities.

words.ex: The statue is made of white marble.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像由白色大理石制成。
words.en: Marble is a type of very hard rock which is used for making statues and for building. It is usually white with dark lines in it.

words.tr: n. 差额；边缘；净利润；余地；
words.ex: The profit margin is five dollars.
words.ex_cn: 利润差额是五美元。
words.en: The margin is the edge or border of something, or the difference between two amounts, especially the difference between the cost of producing something and the price it is sold for.

words.ex: The birds live in a quiet marsh.
words.ex_cn: 这些鸟生活在一片宁静的沼泽中。
words.en: A marsh is an area of low-lying land which is flooded in wet seasons or at high tide, and typically remains waterlogged at all times.

words.tr:
n. 元帅；高级军官；典礼官；消防局长
v. 整理；集结
words.ex: The marshal led the army into battle.
words.ex_cn: 元帅率领军队上战场。
words.en: A marshal is a high-ranking officer in the armed forces, especially in the army or air force, or a person who arranges or directs a public event.

words.tr:
n. 殉道者；殉教者；烈士
v. 处死；折磨
words.ex: He became a martyr for freedom.
words.ex_cn: 他为自由而成为烈士。
words.en: A martyr is someone who is killed or made to suffer greatly because of their religious or political beliefs, and is admired and respected by people who share those beliefs.

words.tr:
v. 惊异于；惊异；
n. 令人惊异的人（或事）；
words.ex: I marvel at how fast she runs.
words.ex_cn: 我惊异于她跑得有多快。
words.en: If you marvel at something, you express your great surprise, wonder, or admiration.

words.tr: adj. 大规模的；大而重的；
words.ex: The company launched a massive advertising campaign.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司发起了一场大规模的广告活动。
words.en: Something that is massive is extremely large in size, amount, or extent.

words.tr:
n. 最大限度；最大量；
adj. 最大极限的；最多的；
words.ex: The maximum of the crowd is 100 people.
words.ex_cn: 人群的上限是100人。
words.en: The greatest or highest amount possible or attained.

words.ex: The cows are grazing in the meadow.
words.ex_cn: 牛群正在草地上吃草。
words.en: A meadow is a field with grass and often wild flowers in it.

words.ex: The castle is a medieval building.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡是一座中世纪的建筑。
words.en: Relating to the Middle Ages, the period in European history from about the 5th century to the 15th century.

words.ex: The merchant sells fresh fruit every morning.
words.ex_cn: 商人每天早上卖新鲜水果。
words.en: A merchant is a person who buys and sells goods, especially one who owns a shop.

words.ex: The two companies will merge next year.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司明年将合并。
words.en: To combine or unite to form a single entity.

words.ex: Calling time a thief is a metaphor.
words.ex_cn: 把时间称为小偷是一种隐喻。
words.en: A metaphor is a figure of speech in which a word or phrase is applied to an object or action to which it is not literally applicable.

words.ex: He lives in a big metropolis with many tall buildings.
words.ex_cn: 他住在一个有很多高楼的大都市里。
words.en: A metropolis is a very large city, often the most important city in a country or area.

words.ex: The millennium began in the year 2000.
words.ex_cn: 一千年始于2000年。
words.en: A millennium is a period of one thousand years.

words.ex: The child's recovery was a miracle.
words.ex_cn: 孩子的康复是个奇迹。
words.en: A miracle is an event that cannot be explained by the laws of nature and is therefore considered to be the work of a divine agency.

words.ex: He lost his job, which was a great misfortune.
words.ex_cn: 他丢了工作，这是一场巨大的不幸。
words.en: An unfortunate condition or event.

words.ex: He ate a moderate amount of food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了适量的食物。
words.en: If you moderate something or if it moderates, it becomes less extreme or violent, or if you moderate a discussion, you help the people in it to reach an agreement.

words.ex: The monarch ruled the country for 50 years.
words.ex_cn: 这位君主统治这个国家长达50年。
words.en: A monarch is a king, queen, emperor, or empress.

words.ex: The monks live in a quiet monastery.
words.ex_cn: 僧侣们住在一座安静的修道院里。
words.en: A monastery is a building or collection of buildings in which monks live and work.

words.ex: The old ship was a monster on the sea.
words.ex_cn: 那艘旧船在海上是个庞然大物。
words.en: A monster is an imaginary creature that is very large, ugly, and frightening.

words.ex: He goes to the mosque every Friday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周五去清真寺。
words.en: A mosque is a building where Muslims go to worship.

words.ex: The motion of the ball is very fast.
words.ex_cn: 球的运动非常快。
words.en: The action or process of moving or being moved.

words.ex: His motive was to help his family.
words.ex_cn: 他的动机是帮助家人。
words.en: Your motive for doing something is your reason for doing it.

words.ex: The baker used a metal mold to shape the cake.
words.ex_cn: 面包师用一个金属模具来塑造蛋糕。
words.en: A mold is a hollow container used to give shape to molten or hot liquid material when it cools and hardens. It can also refer to a fungus that grows on food or damp surfaces.

words.tr:
n. 模具；霉；
v. 铸造；
words.ex: The clay was poured into the mould to shape the pot.
words.ex_cn: 将黏土倒入模具中以塑造花盆。
words.en: A mould is a hollow container that you pour a liquid or soft substance into, which then becomes solid in the same shape as the container. Mould can also refer to a fungus that grows on old food or on damp surfaces.

words.ex: He has a small mustache.
words.ex_cn: 他有一小撮胡子。
words.en: A mustache is a strip of hair left to grow above the upper lip.

words.ex: He has a black moustache.
words.ex_cn: 他有一撮黑色的胡子。
words.en: A moustache is the hair that grows on a man's upper lip.

words.ex: The bacteria multiply quickly.
words.ex_cn: 细菌迅速增加。
words.en: If you multiply one number by another, you add the first number to itself as many times as is indicated by the second number. For example, 2 multiplied by 3 is equal to 6.

words.ex: They have mutual respect for each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们彼此相互尊重。
words.en: Mutual is used to describe a situation, feeling, or action that is experienced, felt, or done by each of two or more parties towards the other or others.

chapters.name: 附录1 最常考专四词回顾 N

words.ex: The child gave a naive smile when he believed the story.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子相信这个故事时，他露出了天真的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as naïve, you think they lack experience and so expect things to be easy or people to be honest or kind.

words.ex: The child was naked in the bathtub.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在浴缸里是裸体的。
words.en: If something is naked, it is not covered by anything such as clothes or paint.

words.tr: adj. 负面的；消极的；否定的；
words.ex: The news had a negative effect on the market.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻对市场产生了负面影响。
words.en: If someone is negative or has a negative attitude, they consider only the bad aspects of a situation, rather than the good ones.

words.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, we went for a walk.
words.ex_cn: 天下雨了；尽管如此，我们还是去散步了。
words.en: Despite what has just been said or done; nonetheless.

words.ex: They will nominate her for the award.
words.ex_cn: 他们将提名她获得这个奖项。
words.en: If someone is nominated for a job or position, their name is formally suggested as a candidate for it.

words.ex: Mother's milk nourishes the baby.
words.ex_cn: 母乳滋养婴儿。
words.en: To nourish someone or something means to provide them with the food and other substances they need in order to live, grow, and be healthy.

words.ex: There are numerous books on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 书架上有许多书。
words.en: If people or things are numerous, they exist or are present in large numbers.

chapters.name: 附录1 最常考专四词回顾 O

words.ex: The law obliges drivers to wear seat belts.
words.ex_cn: 法律迫使司机系安全带。
words.en: If you are obliged to do something, you have to do it because the situation, the law, a duty, etc., makes it necessary.

words.ex: The fallen tree obstructs the road.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树挡住了道路。
words.en: If something obstructs a road or path, it blocks it, stopping people or vehicles from getting past.

words.ex: The occupation of the city by foreign troops lasted for years.
words.ex_cn: 外国军队对这座城市的占领持续了多年。
words.en: An occupation is a job or profession, or a way of spending your time.

words.tr: adj. 奇怪的；奇数的；余的；
words.ex: He wore an odd hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶奇怪的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as odd, you mean that they are strange or unusual.

words.ex: He opposes the new law.
words.ex_cn: 他反对这项新法律。
words.en: If you oppose someone or something, you disagree with them and try to prevent them from doing something, or you try to change what they are doing.

words.ex: You have three options to choose from.
words.ex_cn: 你有三个选项可以选择。
words.en: An option is something that you can choose to do in preference to one or more alternatives.

words.ex: He used the sun to orient himself.
words.ex_cn: 他用太阳来确定方向。
words.en: To orient means to align or position something in relation to the points of a compass or other specified positions, or to familiarize someone with a new situation or environment.

words.ex: This tradition originates from ancient times.
words.ex_cn: 这个传统起源于古代。
words.en: To originate means to have a specific beginning or to start something.

words.ex: The ostrich runs very fast on the grassland.
words.ex_cn: 鸵鸟在草原上跑得很快。
words.en: An ostrich is a large African bird that cannot fly and has long legs and a long neck.

words.ex: His outlook on life is very positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对生活的观点非常积极。
words.en: Your outlook is your general attitude towards life.

words.tr:
adj. 总的；全面的；总体的；
adv. 总计；大致上；
words.ex: The overall cost is too high.
words.ex_cn: 总成本太高了。
words.en: You use overall to indicate that you are talking about a situation in general or about the whole of something.

words.tr: v. 使不知所措；使无法解决；击败；压垮；淹没
words.ex: The homework overwhelms her every night.
words.ex_cn: 每天晚上的作业让她感到不堪重负。
words.en: To overwhelm means to bury or drown beneath a huge mass of something, or to defeat someone completely.

words.tr: adj. 压倒的；无法抗拒的；势不可挡的； v. “overwhelm”的现在分词；
words.ex: The crowd's cheers were overwhelming.
words.ex_cn: 人群的欢呼声压倒了一切。
words.en: If something is overwhelming, it affects you very strongly, and you do not know how to deal with it.

words.ex: The ozone layer protects us from the sun's harmful rays.
words.ex_cn: 臭氧层保护我们免受太阳有害射线的伤害。
words.en: Ozone is a form of oxygen that has three atoms in each molecule, and it is a pale blue gas with a pungent smell. It is found in the Earth's atmosphere and absorbs ultraviolet radiation, which is harmful to living organisms.

chapters.name: 附录1 最常考专四词回顾 P

words.tr:
n. 恐慌；
v. 感到恐慌；
words.ex: A panic spread through the crowd when the fire alarm rang.
words.ex_cn: 当火警响起时，人群陷入了恐慌。
words.en: Panic is a very strong feeling of anxiety or fear, which makes you act without thinking carefully.

words.tr:
n. 游行；阅兵；
v. 游行；阅兵；
words.ex: The city held a big parade on Independence Day.
words.ex_cn: 城市在独立日举行了盛大的游行。
words.en: A parade is a procession of people or vehicles moving through a public place in order to celebrate an important day or event.

words.ex: It's a paradox that he is rich but unhappy.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个悖论，他很富有却不快乐。
words.en: A paradox is a statement that seems to contradict itself but may nonetheless be true, or a situation that defies intuition.

words.ex: The parliament passed a new law about education.
words.ex_cn: 国会通过了一项关于教育的新法律。
words.en: A parliament is a legislative body of government, typically composed of elected representatives, that is responsible for making laws and representing the interests of the people.

words.ex: He will participate in the school play.
words.ex_cn: 他将参与学校的戏剧演出。
words.en: To take part in an activity or event.

words.tr:
n. 划分；隔离物；分割
v. 分开；隔开
words.ex: The partition of the room made it more private.
words.ex_cn: 房间的隔断让它更私密了。
words.en: A partition is a wall, screen, or divider that separates one part of a room, vehicle, or other space from another.

words.ex: Reading books is his favorite pastime.
words.ex_cn: 读书是他最喜欢的消遣。
words.en: A pastime is something that you do because you enjoy it or are interested in it, rather than as a job.

words.tr: n. 特性；怪癖；奇异之物
words.ex: One peculiarity of the old house is its red door.
words.ex_cn: 这座老房子的一个特点是它的红门。
words.en: A peculiarity is a characteristic or quality that is distinctive or unique to a particular person, place, or thing.

words.tr: v. 兜售；沿街叫卖； 散播
words.ex: He tries to peddle fake watches on the street.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在街上兜售假手表。
words.en: To peddle goods or ideas means to try to sell them or make them accepted by going from place to place.

words.ex: I perceive a change in his mood.
words.ex_cn: 我察觉到他的情绪有变化。
words.en: If you perceive something, you see, notice, or realize it, especially when it is not obvious.

words.ex: They persecute people for their beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他们因人们的信仰而迫害他们。
words.en: If someone is persecuted, they are treated cruelly and unfairly, often because of their race, religion, or political beliefs.

words.tr: n. 视角；观点；（对事物的）合理判断；
words.ex: His perspective on life is very positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对生活的看法非常积极。
words.en: A particular attitude towards or way of regarding something; a point of view.

words.ex: He likes to study philosophy in his free time.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在空闲时间学习哲学。
words.en: Philosophy is the study or creation of theories about basic things such as the nature of existence, knowledge, and thought, or about how people should live.

words.ex: The pilgrim walked to the holy place.
words.ex_cn: 朝圣者步行前往圣地。
words.en: A pilgrim is a person who journeys to a sacred place for religious reasons.

words.tr: adj. 似乎合理的；看似真实的；似乎可信的；看似真实的；
words.ex: His excuse sounded plausible.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口听起来似乎合理。
words.en: An explanation or statement that is plausible seems likely to be true or valid.

words.tr:
v. 掠夺；抢劫
n. 掠夺物；掠夺；赃物
words.ex: The pirates plundered the ship.
words.ex_cn: 海盗劫掠了那艘船。
words.en: If someone plunders a place or plunders things from a place, they steal things from it.

words.ex: He sat by the window to ponder his future.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在窗边深思自己的未来。
words.en: If you ponder something, you think about it carefully.

words.ex: He sits on the porch and drinks coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在门廊上喝咖啡。
words.en: A porch is a covered shelter projecting in front of the entrance of a building.

words.ex: He has a positive attitude toward life.
words.ex_cn: 他对生活持积极的态度。
words.en: If you are positive about things, you are hopeful and confident, and think of the good aspects of a situation rather than the bad ones.

words.ex: Wear a helmet as a precaution when riding a bike.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔作为一种预防措施。
words.en: A precaution is an action that is intended to prevent something dangerous or unpleasant from happening.

words.ex: He has prejudice against people from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 他对来自其他国家的人有偏见。
words.en: Prejudice is an unreasonable dislike of a particular group of people or things, or a preference for one group of people or things over another.

words.ex: He did a preliminary test before the main experiment.
words.ex_cn: 他在主要实验之前做了一个初步测试。
words.en: Preliminary means something that is done or happens before the main part or event, especially as an introduction or preparation.

words.ex: The doctor prescribed medicine for my cold.
words.ex_cn: 医生给我开了治疗感冒的药。
words.en: If a doctor prescribes medicine or treatment for you, he or she tells you what medicine or treatment to have.

words.tr:
v. 保存；保护；保持；
n. （某群体）专有的活动；
words.ex: She preserves fresh fruit by making jam.
words.ex_cn: 她通过做果酱来保存新鲜水果。
words.en: To preserve something means to maintain it in its original or existing state.

words.ex: The university has great prestige for its research.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学因其研究而享有很高的声望。
words.en: The widespread respect and admiration felt for someone or something on the basis of a perception of their achievements or quality.

words.tr: n. 伪装；假象；虚伪的表现
words.ex: He was accused of using pretense to gain sympathy.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控利用伪装来博取同情。
words.en: A pretense is an action or way of behaving that is intended to make people believe something that is not true.

words.ex: She tried to prevail on him to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 她试图劝服他改变主意。
words.en: If a proposal, principle, or opinion prevails, it gains influence or is accepted, often after a struggle or argument.

words.ex: The tribe lives in a primitive hut.
words.ex_cn: 这个部落住在原始的小屋里。
words.en: Belonging to a very early period in the history of the world, or to a time before modern things existed.

words.ex: Going first is a privilege, not a right.
words.ex_cn: 优先权是一种特权，而不是权利。
words.en: A privilege is a special right or advantage that only one person or group has.

words.ex: The factory improved its productivity by using new machines.
words.ex_cn: 工厂通过使用新机器提高了生产率。
words.en: Productivity is the rate at which goods are produced or work is completed.

words.ex: This small business is profitable.
words.ex_cn: 这家小企业有利可图的。
words.en: If something is profitable, it makes a profit or is beneficial.

words.ex: His words had a profound effect on her life.
words.ex_cn: 他的话对她的生活产生了深远的影响。
words.en: If you describe something as profound, you mean that it is very great or intense.

words.ex: The school prohibits students from using phones in class.
words.ex_cn: 学校禁止学生在课堂上使用手机。
words.en: If a law or someone in authority prohibits something, they forbid it or make it illegal.

words.tr: adj. 突出的；杰出的；显著的；
words.ex: He is a prominent scientist in the field of medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他是医学领域的一位突出的科学家。
words.en: Someone or something that is prominent is important and well-known, or is positioned in a way that makes them easily seen or noticed.

words.tr: v. 促进；推动；宣传；推销；
words.ex: Exercise can promote good health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进健康。
words.en: To promote means to help something to happen, develop, or increase, or to raise someone to a higher position or rank.

words.tr:
n. 提示；
v. 促使；
adj. 迅速的；准时的；
words.ex: The teacher gave a prompt to help students start writing.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个提示，帮助学生开始写作。
words.en: If you prompt someone when they stop speaking, you encourage or help them to continue. If you are prompt to do something, you do it without delay or you are not late.

words.ex: The proportion of students who passed the test was high.
words.ex_cn: 通过考试的学生比例很高。
words.en: A proportion is a part of a whole, or the relationship of one part to another in terms of size, amount, or degree.

words.ex: The cost is proportional to the size.
words.ex_cn: 成本与大小成比例。
words.en: If one amount is proportional to another, the two amounts increase and decrease at the same rate so there is always the same relationship between them.

words.ex: He made a proposal to improve the school lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他提出了一个改善学校午餐的提案。
words.en: A proposal is a plan or suggestion, especially a formal one that is put forward for people to think about and decide upon.

words.tr: n. 所有者；经营者 ；业主
words.ex: The proprietor runs a small coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 店主经营一家小咖啡馆。
words.en: A proprietor is a person who owns a particular type of business, especially a hotel, a shop, or a company.

words.ex: The country enjoys prosperity after years of peace.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在多年的和平后迎来了繁荣。
words.en: Prosperity is a condition in which a person, community, or country is thriving and successful, especially in financial terms.

words.ex: The city became prosperous after the new factory opened.
words.ex_cn: 新工厂开业后，这座城市变得繁荣了。
words.en: A prosperous person, place, or economy is rich and successful.

words.tr:
v. 抗议；
n. 抗议活动；
words.ex: The students protest against the new school rules.
words.ex_cn: 学生们抗议新的校规。
words.en: A protest is the act of saying or showing publicly that you object to something.

words.ex: He puffed after running up the stairs.
words.ex_cn: 他跑上楼梯后喘着气。
words.en: If you puff, you breathe in and out quickly and with force, for example because you have been running or because you are out of breath. A puff of something such as air or smoke is a small amount of it that is blown out from somewhere.

words.tr:
n. 购买；采购；
v. 购买；采购；
words.ex: The purchase of a new car took all his savings.
words.ex_cn: 买一辆新车花光了他所有的积蓄。
words.en: To purchase something means to buy it. It can also refer to something that has been bought.

words.tr: n. 女用小包；钱包；资金；
words.ex: She put her keys in her purse.
words.ex_cn: 她把钥匙放进她的女用小包里。
words.en: A purse is a small bag used especially by women to carry everyday personal items.

words.ex: He solved the crossword puzzle quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快解开了这个填字谜。
words.en: If something puzzles you, you do not understand it and feel confused.

chapters.name: 附录1 最常考专四词回顾 Q

words.ex: The teacher gave us a questionnaire about our habits.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了我们一份关于我们习惯的问卷。
words.en: A questionnaire is a written list of questions which are answered by a lot of people in order to provide information for a report or a survey.

chapters.name: 附录1 最常考专四词回顾 R

words.ex: He faced racial discrimination at work.
words.ex_cn: 他在工作中遭遇了种族歧视。
words.en: Relating to the common characteristics of different races of people, especially in the context of social or cultural differences.

words.tr: adj. 根本的；彻底的；激进的；
words.ex: The government made radical changes to the education system.
words.ex_cn: 政府对教育系统进行了根本性的改革。
words.en: A radical change or difference is very big and important.

words.ex: He burst into rage when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他勃然大怒。
words.en: Rage is a feeling of intense anger that is difficult to control.

words.tr:
v. 集合起来；振作；复苏
n. 集会
words.ex: The crowd rallied to support their team.
words.ex_cn: 人群聚集起来支持他们的球队。
words.en: A rally is a large public meeting that is held in order to show support for something such as a political party or a sports team. It can also mean to come together again in order to continue fighting or arguing after a defeat or a period of confusion.

words.tr:
n. 一系列；（变化）范围；山脉；
v. （在某范围内）变化；包括（各种不同的人或物）；
words.ex: The store offers a range of colors.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店提供一系列颜色。
words.en: A range of things is a number of different things of the same general kind.

words.ex: It is rational to save money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 为未来存钱是合理的。
words.en: Based on or in accordance with reason or logic.

words.ex: He reacts quickly when he hears a loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到大声响时，他会迅速做出反应。
words.en: When you react to something that has happened to you, you behave in a particular way because of it.

words.ex: Many people lost jobs during the recession.
words.ex_cn: 在经济不景气期间，许多人失去了工作。
words.en: A recession is a period when the economy of a country is not doing well, industrial production and business activity are at a low level, and many people are unemployed.

words.tr: adj. 鲁莽的；不计后果的；
words.ex: He drove reckless and got into an accident.
words.ex_cn: 他开车鲁莽，结果出了事故。
words.en: If you say that someone is reckless, you mean that they act in a way which shows that they do not care about danger or the effect their behaviour will have on other people.

words.ex: I reckon it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我认为明天会下雨。
words.en: If you reckon that something is true, you think that it is true.

words.ex: I recommend this book to you.
words.ex_cn: 我向你推荐这本书。
words.en: If someone recommends a person or thing to you, they suggest that you would find them good or useful.

words.ex: The teacher gave me a recommendation for the scholarship.
words.ex_cn: 老师给我写了一封奖学金推荐信。
words.en: A suggestion or proposal as to the best course of action, especially one put forward by an authoritative body.

words.ex: The company plans to recruit new staff next month.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司计划下个月招聘新员工。
words.en: To recruit means to enlist someone in the armed forces or to persuade someone to join a company, organization, or group.

words.ex: He refines his writing every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天完善自己的写作。
words.en: To refine something means to make it purer or to improve it, especially by removing unwanted substances or by making small changes.

words.tr: v. 反映；反射；反省；思考；仔细考虑；
words.ex: The mirror reflects the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 镜子反射阳光。
words.en: If a surface reflects light, heat, sound, or an image, it sends the light, etc. back and does not absorb it. If something is reflected in a mirror or in water, you can see its image in the mirror or in the water.

words.ex: We had a snack and some drinks as refreshment after the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 会议结束后，我们吃了点心和喝了一些饮料作为茶点。
words.en: Refreshment refers to the act of refreshing or the state of being refreshed, especially by food or drink. It can also mean a light meal or drinks served in a social setting.

words.ex: The animals found refuge in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这些动物在森林中找到了避难所。
words.en: A place or state of safety or shelter from danger, trouble, or difficulty.

words.ex: The refugee walked to a new country.
words.ex_cn: 这名难民步行去了一个新国家。
words.en: A refugee is a person who has been forced to leave their country in order to escape war, persecution, or natural disaster.

words.ex: He went outside regardless of the rain.
words.ex_cn: 他不顾下雨就出去了。
words.en: If you say that someone does something regardless, you mean that they do it without taking account of the possible problems or difficulties.

words.ex: The new regime changed the tax laws.
words.ex_cn: 新的管理制度改变了税法。
words.en: A regime is the set of rules or the way that a country or organization is governed, especially when it is considered to be strict or unfair.

words.tr: v. 恢复；修复；改造（罪犯）
words.ex: The hospital will rehabilitate the injured athlete.
words.ex_cn: 医院将帮助受伤的运动员康复。
words.en: To rehabilitate someone who has been ill or in prison means to help them to live a normal life again. To rehabilitate a building or an area means to improve its condition.

words.ex: The queen's reign lasted 70 years.
words.ex_cn: 女王的统治持续了70年。
words.en: The period during which a sovereign rules; to hold royal office; to prevail

words.ex: Exercise can reinforce your muscles.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的肌肉。
words.en: To reinforce something means to make it stronger or more effective.

words.tr:
n. 释放；发布；
v. 释放；发布；
words.ex: The release of the prisoner made everyone happy.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯的释放让每个人都高兴。
words.en: To release something means to let it go or to allow it to be free, or to make something available to the public.

words.ex: This information is relevant to our project.
words.ex_cn: 这些信息与我们的项目相关。
words.en: Something that is relevant to a situation or person is important or significant in that situation or to that person.

words.ex: He was reluctant to leave his home.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意离开家。
words.en: If you are reluctant to do something, you are unwilling to do it and hesitate before doing it, or do it slowly and without enthusiasm.

words.ex: The renaissance brought new art and ideas to Europe.
words.ex_cn: 文艺复兴为欧洲带来了新的艺术和思想。
words.en: The Renaissance was a period in European history marking the transition from the Middle Ages to modernity and covering the 15th and 16th centuries, characterized by an effort to revive and surpass ideas and achievements of classical antiquity.

words.ex: They will renovate the old house next month.
words.ex_cn: 他们下个月将翻新那栋老房子。
words.en: To renovate means to restore something to a good state of repair or to make it as good as new.

words.tr:
n. 救援；营救；
v. 救援；营救；
words.ex: The rescue came just in time to save the hikers.
words.ex_cn: 救援及时赶到，救出了徒步者。
words.en: To rescue someone or something means to save them from a dangerous or unpleasant situation.

words.ex: There is a resemblance between the two brothers.
words.ex_cn: 这两兄弟之间有相似之处。
words.en: If there is a resemblance between two people or things, they are similar to each other.

words.ex: The boy resembles his father.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩长得像他父亲。
words.en: If one thing or person resembles another, they are similar to each other.

words.ex: He resents being ignored by his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他怨恨被老板忽视。
words.en: If you resent someone or something, you feel bitter and angry about them.

words.ex: The resolution of the conflict took many meetings.
words.ex_cn: 这个冲突的解决花了多次会议。
words.en: A resolution is a formal decision made at a meeting by the vote of the people who are there. It can also refer to a firm decision to do or not to do something.

words.tr: adj. 有责任的；负责任的；
words.ex: He is responsible for cleaning the room.
words.ex_cn: 他负责打扫房间。
words.en: If someone or something is responsible for a particular event or situation, they are the cause of it or they can be blamed for it.

words.tr:
n. 撤退；退却；静居处；
v. 撤退；退却；
words.ex: The army ordered a retreat after the battle.
words.ex_cn: 战斗后，军队下令撤退。
words.en: If you retreat, you move away from something or someone, often because you are frightened or because you want to be alone. A retreat is also a quiet, isolated place that you go to in order to rest or to do things in private.

words.ex: The letter revealed his secret.
words.ex_cn: 这封信揭露了他的秘密。
words.en: To reveal something means to make known something that was previously secret or unknown.

words.ex: The company's revenue increased last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的收入去年增加了。
words.en: Revenue is the income that a company, organization, or government receives regularly.

words.ex: The medicine helped revive the sick man.
words.ex_cn: 这剂药帮助这位病人恢复了生机。
words.en: To revive something means to bring it back to life, consciousness, or use, or to make it active or successful again.

words.tr:
n. 韵文；
v. 押韵；
words.ex: The poem has a simple rhyme.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗有一段简单的韵文。
words.en: A rhyme is a repetition of similar sounds in the final stressed syllables and any following syllables of two or more words, most often used in poetry.

words.ex: The bridge crosses the river.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥横跨河流。
words.en: A bridge is a structure that is built over a railway, river, or road so that people or vehicles can cross from one side to the other.

words.ex: He faced ridicule for wearing old clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他因为穿旧衣服而遭到嘲笑。
words.en: To ridicule someone or something means to make fun of them in an unkind way.

words.ex: It's ridiculous to think he can run a mile in one minute.
words.ex_cn: 认为他能在一分钟内跑完一英里是荒谬的。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is ridiculous, you mean that they are very foolish.

words.tr:
n. 步枪；来复枪（又称来福枪）
v. 快速搜寻
words.ex: He carries a rifle in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他带着一把步枪在森林里。
words.en: A rifle is a gun with a long barrel which you hold against your shoulder when firing.

words.tr: adj. 刻板的；坚硬的；严格的；
words.ex: He has a rigid attitude toward rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对规则的态度很刻板。
words.en: not able to be changed or adapted; not able to be bent or moved; stiff

words.tr: n. （宗教等的）仪式；例行习惯；
words.ex: The village holds a ritual every spring to pray for good weather.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄每年春天都举行一个仪式，祈求好天气。
words.en: A ritual is a religious service or other ceremony which involves a series of actions performed in a fixed order.

words.tr:
n. 常规；例行公事；
adj. 常规的；例行公事的；
words.ex: He follows a morning routine every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都遵循固定的惯例。
words.en: A routine is a sequence of actions regularly followed; a fixed program.

words.ex: He plays rugby every Saturday.
words.ex_cn: 他每个星期六打橄榄球。
words.en: Rugby is a sport played by two teams of 15 players each, using an oval ball that players kick, pass, or carry in order to score points by grounding the ball behind the opponent's goal line or kicking it between the goalposts.

words.ex: He lives in a rural village with no big shops.
words.ex_cn: 他住在没有大商店的农村村庄里。
words.en: Rural areas are areas which are not towns or cities. They are often farming or agricultural areas.

words.ex: The old bike has rust on its chain.
words.ex_cn: 这辆旧自行车的链条上有锈。
words.en: Rust is a reddish-brown substance that forms on the surface of iron or steel when they are exposed to air and moisture, causing them to corrode.

words.tr:
adj. 乡村的；纯朴的；土气的
n. 乡下人；乡巴佬
words.ex: They live in a rustic cabin near the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在森林附近的一间乡村小屋里。
words.en: Rustic is used to describe things that are typical of the countryside rather than the town, or things that are simple and old-fashioned in a way that is considered typical of the countryside.

chapters.name: 附录1 最常考专四词回顾 S

words.tr:
v. 牺牲；
n. 牺牲（品）；
words.ex: He sacrificed his time to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他牺牲了自己的时间来帮助朋友。
words.en: If you sacrifice something that is valuable or important, you give it up, usually to obtain something else for yourself or for other people.

words.tr:
n. 批准；允许；认可；制裁；处罚
v. 批准；认可；制裁；处罚
words.ex: The company got official sanction to open a new branch.
words.ex_cn: 该公司获得了开设新分公司的正式批准。
words.en: A sanction is a penalty for disobeying a law or rule, or an official permission or approval for an action.

words.ex: He carries a brown satchel to school.
words.ex_cn: 他背着一个棕色的书包去学校。
words.en: A satchel is a bag with a long strap, traditionally used for carrying books.

words.tr:
n. 规模；等级；比例（尺）；刻度；秤；
v. 改变…大小；
words.ex: The scale of the project surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的规模让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A scale is a set of levels or numbers which are used in a particular system of measuring things or are used when comparing things.

words.ex: He scan the QR code with his phone.
words.ex_cn: 他用手机扫描了二维码。
words.en: To look at something carefully or quickly in order to find out specific information or to examine something thoroughly.

words.ex: She wore a warm scarf in winter.
words.ex_cn: 她在冬天戴了一条暖和的围巾。
words.en: A scarf is a piece of cloth that you wear around your neck or head, usually to keep yourself warm.

words.ex: The wind scatter the leaves everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 风把树叶吹得四处分散。
words.en: To scatter means to throw or drop things over a wide area in an irregular way, or to cause a group of people or animals to move apart in different directions.

words.ex: I checked the class schedule for tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我查看了明天的课程时间表。
words.en: A schedule is a plan that gives a list of events or tasks and the times at which each one should happen or be done.

words.ex: The police discovered a scheme to steal money.
words.ex_cn: 警方发现了一个偷钱的阴谋。
words.en: A scheme is a plan or arrangement, especially one produced by a government or other organization, or a secret plan to do something, especially something illegal or dishonest.

words.ex: There was a scramble for the last ticket.
words.ex_cn: 大家争相抢购最后一张票。
words.en: If you scramble over rocks or up a hill, you move quickly over them or up it using your hands to help you. Scramble can also mean to compete or struggle with others for something that is in short supply.

words.tr:
v. 刮；擦；刮出刺耳声；勉强通过
n. 刮；擦；擦痕；刮擦声
words.ex: He scraped his knee on the rough ground.
words.ex_cn: 他在粗糙的地面上擦伤了膝盖。
words.en: To remove something from a surface using a sharp or rough edge, or to injure a part of the body by rubbing it against a rough surface.

words.tr:
n. 抓痕；刮伤；
v. 抓搔；刮；
words.ex: The cat left a scratch on the door.
words.ex_cn: 猫在门上抓出了一道抓痕。
words.en: If you scratch something, you rub your fingernails or claws against it, often because it is itchy or irritating.

words.ex: He wrote a script for a short movie.
words.ex_cn: 他为一部短片写了剧本。
words.en: A script is the written form of a play, film, or broadcast. It includes the dialogue and stage directions.

words.tr: n. 仔细研究；详细检查；
words.ex: The teacher examined the student's work under close scrutiny.
words.ex_cn: 老师对学生的作业进行了仔细研究。
words.en: If someone or something is under scrutiny, they are being studied or observed very carefully.

words.tr: n. 雕刻（术）；雕塑品；雕刻品；
words.ex: He made a beautiful sculpture from clay.
words.ex_cn: 他用黏土做了一件精美的雕刻。
words.en: Sculpture is the art of making two- or three-dimensional representative or abstract forms, especially by carving stone or wood or by casting metal or plaster.

words.tr: adj. 中等的；次要的；第二的；
words.ex: He attends a secondary school in the city.
words.ex_cn: 他在城里上一所中学。
words.en: If you describe something as secondary, you mean that it is less important than something else.

words.ex: The government kept the mission in secrecy.
words.ex_cn: 政府将这次任务保密。
words.en: Secrecy is the practice of keeping something secret, or the state of being secret.

words.tr:
v. （使）获得；
adj. 安全的；稳定的；
words.ex: He worked hard to secure a job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以获得一份工作。
words.en: If you secure something that you want or need, you obtain it, often after a lot of effort.

words.ex: He attended a seminar on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他参加了一个关于气候变化的研讨会。
words.en: A seminar is a meeting where a group of people discuss a problem or topic.

words.ex: The senate voted to pass the new law.
words.ex_cn: 参议院投票通过了这项新法律。
words.en: The Senate is the smaller and more important of the two parts of the parliament in some countries, for example in the United States and Australia.

words.tr: adj. 明智的；有判断力的；恰当的；合理的；
words.ex: It is sensible to wear a coat in cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 在寒冷的天气里穿外套是明智的。
words.en: A sensible person is able to make good judgments and decisions based on reason rather than emotion.

words.ex: The serpent slithered quietly through the grass.
words.ex_cn: 那条大蛇静静地从草丛中滑过。
words.en: A serpent is a large snake. In stories and some religions, serpents are often associated with evil or cunning.

words.ex: The city cleaned the sewage from the streets.
words.ex_cn: 城市清理了街道上的污水。
words.en: Sewage is waste matter such as faeces or dirty water from homes and factories, which flows away through sewers.

words.tr:
v. 使脱落；去除；
n. 棚屋；
words.ex: The tree sheds its leaves in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树在秋天落叶。
words.en: A shed is a small building, usually made of wood, used for storing things such as garden tools. When something sheds, it loses its covering, such as leaves or hair, or it gets rid of something it no longer needs.

words.ex: It was sheer luck that he won the game.
words.ex_cn: 他赢了比赛完全是运气。
words.en: Sheer is used to emphasize that a state or situation is complete and does not involve or is not mixed with anything else.

words.tr:
n. 避难所；庇护所；
v. 庇护；遮蔽；
words.ex: The refugees found shelter in a small building.
words.ex_cn: 难民们在一个小建筑里找到了避难所。
words.en: A shelter is a small building or covered place which is made to protect people from bad weather or danger.

words.tr:
n. 转移；移位；转变；轮班；
v. 变换位置；转移；换（挡）；轮班；
words.ex: The shift of power to the new government was sudden.
words.ex_cn: 权力向新政府的转移是突然的。
words.en: If you shift something or if it shifts, it moves or changes its position slightly. If someone's opinion, attitude, or behaviour shifts, it changes slightly, especially in response to a particular situation or event.

words.tr: adj. 精明的；敏锐的；机灵的；
words.ex: He made a shrewd decision to buy the house low.
words.ex_cn: 他精明地决定低价买下这栋房子。
words.en: A shrewd person is able to understand and judge a situation quickly and to use this understanding to their own advantage.

words.tr:
adj. 刺耳的；尖声的；尖厉的
v. 尖叫；发出刺耳的声音
words.ex: The baby's cry was shrill.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿的哭声很尖锐。
words.en: A shrill sound is high and unpleasant to listen to.

words.ex: He ate grilled shrimp for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚餐吃了烤虾。
words.en: A shrimp is a small shellfish with a long tail and many legs, which can be eaten as food.

words.tr: n. 神龛；神社；圣地；圣殿
words.ex: People visit the shrine to pray.
words.ex_cn: 人们去神社祈祷。
words.en: A shrine is a place of worship which is associated with a particular holy person or object.

words.tr:
n. 耸肩
v. 耸肩
words.ex: He shrugged when asked why he was late.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到为什么迟到时，他耸了耸肩。
words.en: If you shrug, you raise your shoulders to show that you are not interested in something or that you do not know or care about something.

words.ex: He pressed the shutter to take a photo.
words.ex_cn: 他按下快门拍了一张照片。
words.en: A shutter is a device used to cover or uncover a window or a camera lens.

words.ex: The castle endured a long siege during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡在战争中经历了长期的围攻。
words.en: A siege is a military operation in which enemy forces surround a town or building, cutting off essential supplies, with the aim of compelling those inside to surrender.

words.ex: The significance of this discovery changed science.
words.ex_cn: 这一发现的重要性改变了科学。
words.en: The quality of being worthy of attention; importance.

words.tr: adj. 重大的；重要的；影响明显的；
words.ex: This discovery is a significant step forward.
words.ex_cn: 这一发现是一个重大的进步。
words.en: Something that is significant is important or large enough to be noticed or to have an effect.

words.ex: The red light signifies stop.
words.ex_cn: 红灯表示停止。
words.en: If an event, a sign, or a symbol signifies something, it is a sign of that thing or represents that thing.

words.ex: The two events happened simultaneously.
words.ex_cn: 这两个事件同时发生了。
words.en: Happening, existing, or done at the same time.

words.tr: adj. 邪恶的；险恶的；不祥的
words.ex: The old house looked sinister in the moonlight.
words.ex_cn: 那座老房子在月光下显得阴森可怖。
words.en: Something that is sinister seems evil or harmful.

words.ex: He is skeptical about the new plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个新计划持怀疑态度。
words.en: If you are skeptical about something, you have doubts about it.

words.tr:
n. 纸片；
v. 滑倒；溜走；
words.ex: She found a slip of paper on the table.
words.ex_cn: 她在桌子上发现了一张纸片。
words.en: If you slip, you accidentally slide and lose your balance.

words.ex: The floor is slippery after it rains.
words.ex_cn: 下雨后地板很滑。
words.en: Something that is slippery is smooth, wet, or oily and is therefore difficult to walk on or to hold.

words.tr: adj. 诡诈的；诡秘的；心照不宣的
words.ex: The sly fox stole the chicken at night.
words.ex_cn: 那只狡猾的狐狸在夜里偷了鸡。
words.en: Someone who is sly is clever and good at deceiving people in a way that is not easily noticed.

words.ex: He tried to smuggle cigarettes across the border.
words.ex_cn: 他试图走私香烟过境。
words.en: To smuggle goods or people means to move them into or out of a country illegally.

words.tr:
n. 快照；
v. 突然断裂；猛然咬；
adj. 突然的；匆忙的；
words.ex: He took a snap of the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他拍了一张日落的快照。
words.en: If something snaps or if you snap it, it breaks suddenly, usually with a sharp cracking noise. | A snap is a photograph. | If someone snaps, or if something snaps inside them, they suddenly stop being calm and become very angry.

words.tr:
v. 夺取；一把抓住
n. 夺取；一把抓住；音乐片段
words.ex: He tried to snatch the bag from her hand.
words.ex_cn: 他试图从她手中抢走包。
words.en: If you snatch something, or if you snatch at it, you take it or pull it away quickly.

words.ex: The price of oil soared last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月石油价格骤升。
words.en: To rise or increase dramatically in amount or level.

words.tr: v. 恳求；征求；（妓女）拉客
words.ex: He solicits donations for the charity.
words.ex_cn: 他为慈善机构募捐。
words.en: If you solicit money, help, support, or an opinion from someone, you ask them for it.

words.ex: He wrote a sonnet about love.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一首关于爱情的十四行诗。
words.en: A sonnet is a poem that has 14 lines. Each line has 10 syllables, and the poem has a fixed pattern of rhymes.

words.tr: adj. 精密复杂的；老练的；
words.ex: The phone has a sophisticated camera.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一个精密复杂的摄像头。
words.en: A sophisticated person is intelligent and knows a lot, so that they are able to understand complicated situations. A sophisticated machine, device, or method is more advanced or complex than others.

words.ex: He is a sophomore at Harvard University.
words.ex_cn: 他是哈佛大学的二年级学生。
words.en: A sophomore is a student in the second year of college or high school.

words.ex: The village has a sparse population.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄人口稀少。
words.en: Something that is sparse is small in number or amount and spread out over an area.

words.ex: This restaurant is famous for its specialty, fried dumplings.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅以特色菜煎饺而闻名。
words.en: A specialty is a particular area of study or expertise that someone has, or a product that is particularly associated with a specific place.

words.ex: Her speciality is cooking Italian food.
words.ex_cn: 她的专长是做意大利菜。
words.en: A speciality is a particular field of work or study that someone specializes in, or a product that is particularly associated with a specific place or producer.

words.tr: adj. 特定的；明确的；具体的；
words.ex: He gave a specific reason for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个迟到的具体原因。
words.en: If someone is specific, they give a description that is precise and exact.

words.ex: Please specify the time for the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 请详细说明会议的时间。
words.en: If you specify something, you give information about what is required or should happen in a certain situation.

words.ex: The teacher showed a specimen of a butterfly.
words.ex_cn: 老师展示了一个蝴蝶标本。
words.en: A specimen is a single thing or example of something, especially one that is used to represent the whole group or type.

words.ex: He speculates that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他推测明天会下雨。
words.en: If you speculate about something, you make guesses about its nature or identity, or about what might happen.

words.tr:
v. 溢出；溅出
n. 溢出；溅出
words.ex: He spilled milk on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他把牛奶洒在了地上。
words.en: To cause or allow (a liquid, powder, etc.) to flow or fall out of a container, usually by accident.

words.tr: adj. 自发的；自然产生的；
words.ex: The children gave a spontaneous cheer.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们自发地欢呼起来。
words.en: Something that is spontaneous is not planned but happens or is done because of a sudden impulse or natural feeling.

words.tr:
n. 地点；场所；斑点；
v. 发现；识别；
words.ex: This is the spot where we met for the first time.
words.ex_cn: 这是我们第一次见面的地方。
words.en: A spot is a particular place or point. It can also refer to a small mark or stain, or a small amount of something. As a verb, it means to see, notice, or recognize someone or something.

words.tr:
n. 鞭策；
v. 刺激；
words.ex: The competition served as a spur to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 竞争成了推动他更努力工作的鞭策。
words.en: A spur is something that makes you want to do something or that encourages you to do it. It can also refer to a sharp device worn on the heel of a rider's boot to urge a horse forward.

words.ex: He squeezed into the small seat.
words.ex_cn: 他挤进了小座位里。
words.en: To squeeze something means to press it firmly, usually with your fingers or hands, often to get liquid out of it or to make it smaller.

words.ex: The water in the pond was stagnant.
words.ex_cn: 池塘里的水不流动。
words.en: If something such as a business or economy is stagnant, there is little activity or change.

words.tr: n. 停滞；滞止；萧条；迟钝
words.ex: The economy is in stagnation.
words.ex_cn: 经济处于停滞状态。
words.en: A situation in which there is no progress or development.

words.tr:
n. 茎；柄；梗
v. 跟踪；偷偷接近；昂首阔步地走
words.ex: The stalk of the sunflower is very tall.
words.ex_cn: 向日葵的茎很高。
words.en: The main stem of a plant, typically rising above ground but occasionally subterranean. Also, to pursue or approach stealthily.

words.tr:
n. 摊位；
v. 故意拖延；
words.ex: He sells fruits at a stall in the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场的一个摊位上卖水果。
words.en: A stall is a small open-fronted shop or a compartment for one animal in a stable or barn. As a verb, it means to stop or cause to stop making progress.

words.ex: The loud noise startle the bird.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音惊动了那只鸟。
words.en: If something or someone startles you, they surprise and frighten you slightly.

words.ex: His status in the company is very high.
words.ex_cn: 他在公司里的地位很高。
words.en: The status of someone or something is their position or situation according to the law or according to other people's opinions.

words.ex: The statute says drivers must stop at red lights.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律规定司机必须在红灯时停车。
words.en: A statute is a formal written law of a country or state, enacted by its legislative authority.

words.tr: adj. 陡峭的；急剧升降的；
words.ex: The mountain has a steep path.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一条陡峭的小路。
words.en: A steep slope or hill is one that is at a sharp angle, rather than being flat or gradual.

words.ex: The church's steeple was visible from miles away.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的尖塔在数英里外就能看到。
words.en: A steeple is a tall pointed structure on the top of a building, especially a church.

words.ex: His neck was stiff after sleeping wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他睡姿不对，脖子变得僵硬。
words.en: If something is stiff, it is firm and does not bend easily. It can also describe a person who is not relaxed or friendly.

words.ex: He fastened the strap around his wrist.
words.ex_cn: 他把带子系在手腕上。
words.en: A strap is a narrow piece of leather, cloth, or other material that is used to fasten, secure, or carry something, or to hold onto something.

words.ex: The cow eats straw from the barn.
words.ex_cn: 牛吃谷仓里的稻草。
words.en: A straw is a thin tube of paper or plastic that you use to suck a drink into your mouth.

words.tr:
v. 闲逛；散步；漫步；
n. 闲逛；散步；漫步；
words.ex: They stroll in the park after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他们晚饭后在公园里闲逛。
words.en: If you stroll somewhere, you walk there in a slow, relaxed way.

words.ex: He is stubborn and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很顽固，不肯改变主意。
words.en: Someone who is stubborn is determined to do what they want and is very unwilling to change their mind.

words.ex: The table is made of sturdy wood.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是用坚固的木头做的。
words.en: Someone or something that is sturdy looks strong and is unlikely to be easily injured or damaged.

words.ex: He will submit his homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会提交他的作业。
words.en: To yield or surrender (oneself) to the will or authority of another.

words.ex: He failed the test, but subsequent efforts helped him pass.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格，但随后的努力让他通过了。
words.en: Following in time or order; succeeding.

words.ex: The government gives a subsidy to farmers.
words.ex_cn: 政府向农民提供补贴。
words.en: A subsidy is money that is paid by a government or other authority in order to help an industry or business, or to pay for a public service.

words.ex: I take the subway to work every day.
words.ex_cn: 我每天坐地铁去上班。
words.en: An underground railway system in a city, usually operated by electricity, which provides a rapid means of transportation.

words.ex: We have sufficient food for the trip.
words.ex_cn: 我们有足够的食物用于这次旅行。
words.en: If something is sufficient for a particular purpose, there is enough of it for the purpose.

words.ex: The climbers reached the summit of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 登山者到达了山顶。
words.en: The highest point of a hill or mountain; a meeting between heads of government.

words.ex: This phone is superior to the old one.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机比旧的更好。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as superior, you mean that they are better than other people or things.

words.ex: The teacher supervises the students during the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 老师在实验期间指导学生。
words.en: If you supervise an activity or a person, you make sure that the activity is done correctly or that the person is doing a task or behaving correctly.

words.tr:
n. 激浪；拍岸浪花；
v. 冲浪；（互联网上）冲浪；
words.ex: He bought a new surf for the beach trip.
words.ex_cn: 他为海滩之旅买了一块新的激浪。
words.en: To surf means to ride on the crest of a wave towards the shore, typically on a surfboard. It can also mean to browse the internet.

words.ex: There was a surge in sales during the holiday season.
words.ex_cn: 假期期间销量激增。
words.en: If something surges, it increases suddenly and greatly, after having been steady or only small in size or amount.

words.ex: He surpassed his brother in math scores.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学成绩上超过了他弟弟。
words.en: If one person or thing surpasses another, the first is better than, or has more of a particular quality than, the second.

words.tr:
n. 调查；勘测；
v. 调查；勘测；
words.ex: The school did a survey about student lunch preferences.
words.ex_cn: 学校做了一项关于学生午餐偏好的调查。
words.en: A survey is a detailed study or inspection, especially as a means of collecting information about people's opinions or behavior.

words.ex: He looked at her with suspicion.
words.ex_cn: 他带着怀疑的眼神看着她。
words.en: A feeling or thought that something is possible, likely, or true, especially something bad or wrong, without having proof.

words.ex: The farmer works hard to sustain his crops.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民努力维持他的庄稼。
words.en: To sustain something means to continue it or maintain it for a period of time.

words.ex: He swallowed the pill with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水吞下了药片。
words.en: To swallow means to make food or drink go down your throat and towards your stomach. It can also mean to accept something without protest or to believe something too easily.

words.ex: The swamp is full of tall grass and frogs.
words.ex_cn: 这个沼泽里长满了高草和青蛙。
words.en: A swamp is an area of low-lying, uncultivated ground where water collects; a bog or marsh.

words.tr:
n. 群；蜂群
v. 云集；充满
words.ex: Bees swarm around the flower.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂围绕着花朵成群飞舞。
words.en: A swarm is a large group of insects, especially bees, moving together. As a verb, it means to move in or form a swarm.

words.ex: The wound began to swell after the insect bite.
words.ex_cn: 被昆虫叮咬后，伤口开始肿胀。
words.en: To increase in size or volume as a result of internal pressure; to expand.

words.tr:
v. 转换；
n. 开关；
words.ex: He switched off the light before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前把灯关掉了。
words.en: A switch is a small control for an electrical device which you use to turn the device on or off.

words.ex: She was sympathetic to his problems.
words.ex_cn: 她对他的问题很同情。
words.en: If you are sympathetic to someone who is in a bad situation, you are kind to them and show that you understand their feelings.

words.ex: He follows a systematic approach to solve math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他用一种系统的方法来解决数学问题。
words.en: A systematic approach or method is one that is done according to a fixed plan, in a thorough and efficient way.

chapters.name: 附录1 最常考专四词回顾 T

words.ex: He will tackle the problem tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会处理这个问题。
words.en: If you tackle a problem or task, you deal with it in a determined way. In sports such as football and rugby, a tackle is an act of trying to take the ball from a player on the other team.

words.tr:
n. 目标；对象；
v. 以…为目标；
words.ex: His target is to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他的目标是按时完成项目。
words.en: A target is something at which someone is aiming a weapon or other object.

words.tr: n. 关税；税率；（旅馆、饭店等的）价目表
words.ex: The government raised the tariff on imported cars.
words.ex_cn: 政府提高了进口汽车的关税。
words.en: A tariff is a tax that a government collects on goods coming into a country.

words.ex: His calm temperament helps him stay peaceful in stress.
words.ex_cn: 他平静的性情让他在压力下保持平和。
words.en: Your temperament is your basic nature, especially as it is shown in the way that you react to situations or to other people.

words.ex: The ancient temple stands on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的庙宇矗立在山上。
words.en: A temple is a building used for the worship of a god or gods in some religions.

words.ex: He took a temporary job during summer.
words.ex_cn: 他在暑假期间做了一份短暂的工作。
words.en: Something that is temporary lasts for only a limited time.

words.ex: He testified that he saw the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他证明自己看到了那起事故。
words.en: To testify means to make a statement based on personal knowledge or belief, especially in a court of law, or to serve as evidence or proof of something's existence or truth.

words.ex: His testimony proved the suspect was innocent.
words.ex_cn: 他的证词证明了嫌疑人是无辜的。
words.en: A formal written or spoken statement, especially one given in a court of law.

words.ex: The store sells many kinds of textile, like cotton and silk.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店出售多种纺织品，比如棉和丝绸。
words.en: Textiles are types of cloth or fabric, especially ones that have been woven.

words.ex: The theme of the essay is friendship.
words.ex_cn: 这篇作文的题目是友谊。
words.en: The subject or main idea in a talk, piece of writing, or work of art.

words.ex: The roller coaster gave her a thrill.
words.ex_cn: 过山车让她感到兴奋。
words.en: A thrill is a sudden feeling of great excitement, pleasure, or fear.

words.tr: v. 兴旺；繁荣；茁壮成长；
words.ex: Plants thrive in sunny places.
words.ex_cn: 植物在阳光充足的地方茁壮成长。
words.en: To thrive means to grow or develop well or vigorously.

words.tr:
n. 人群；一大群；众多
v. 群集；挤满；涌进
words.ex: A throng of people waited outside the store.
words.ex_cn: 一大群人站在商店外面等候。
words.en: A large, densely packed crowd of people or animals.

words.tr:
v. 费力地做；苦干；跋涉
n. 苦工；劳累的工作
words.ex: He toils in the field every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天在田里辛苦劳作。
words.en: If you toil, you work very hard doing something that is difficult or tiring.

words.ex: The rain caused a torrent down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 大雨在山间形成了一股急流。
words.en: A torrent is a fast-moving stream of water or other liquid.

words.tr: adj. 安静的；平静的；宁静的；
words.ex: The lake was tranquil in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早晨的湖面很安静。
words.en: If a place or situation is tranquil, it is calm, peaceful, and quiet, with no disturbance or agitation.

words.ex: The new teacher transformed the class into a lively group.
words.ex_cn: 这位新老师把班级变成了一个充满活力的团体。
words.en: To transform something or someone means to change them completely and usually improve their appearance, form, or structure.

words.ex: The transition from school to work was hard for him.
words.ex_cn: 从学校到工作的转变对他来说很难。
words.en: The process or a period of changing from one state or condition to another.

words.ex: The signal transmission is clear and strong.
words.ex_cn: 信号传输清晰而强劲。
words.en: The act or process of sending or passing something from one place, person, or thing to another.

words.ex: The radio transmits music to listeners.
words.ex_cn: 收音机将音乐传递给听众。
words.en: To send or pass something from one person, place, or thing to another.

words.ex: Two countries signed a treaty to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 两个国家签署了一项条约以停止战争。
words.en: A treaty is a formal agreement between two or more countries or groups, especially one that is written down and signed by their leaders.

words.ex: The earthquake caused tremendous damage.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了巨大的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as tremendous, you mean that they are very great in amount, extent, or intensity.

words.tr:
v. 触发；引起；发动；
n. 诱因；触发；
words.ex: The loud noise triggered the alarm.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音触发了警报。
words.en: A trigger is a device that activates a mechanism when it is pulled or pressed. It can also refer to something that causes a particular reaction or development.

words.ex: He always keeps his garden trim and neat.
words.ex_cn: 他总是把花园打理得整洁有序。
words.en: To trim something means to make it tidier or more level by cutting a small amount off it.

words.ex: The team celebrated their triumph after winning the match.
words.ex_cn: 球队在赢得比赛后庆祝了他们的胜利。
words.en: A triumph is a great success or achievement, often one that has been gained with a lot of skill or effort.

words.ex: The tuition for this course is $500.
words.ex_cn: 这门课程的学费是500美元。
words.en: Tuition is the fee charged for instruction, especially at a college, university, or private school.

words.tr:
v. 跌倒；摔倒；暴跌
n. 摔倒；混乱；暴跌
words.ex: The child tumble down the stairs.
words.ex_cn: 孩子从楼梯上跌倒了。
words.en: If someone or something tumbles, they fall quickly and suddenly, often turning over or spinning as they fall.

words.tr: adj. 狂暴的；骚动的；动荡的；汹涌的
words.ex: The turbulent sea made the boat shake.
words.ex_cn: 汹涌的海让船摇晃。
words.en: A turbulent situation, time, or relationship is one in which there is a lot of change, confusion, and often conflict.

words.ex: The gardener laid new turf in the backyard.
words.ex_cn: 园丁在后院铺了新的草皮。
words.en: Turf is a surface layer of earth containing a dense growth of grass and its matted roots; used especially for lawns and sports fields.

words.tr: n. 黄昏；薄暮；暮光；衰退期
words.ex: The birds fly home at twilight.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在黄昏时飞回家。
words.en: The time of day immediately following sunset, or the period of time at the end of the day when the sun is just below the horizon, especially the period between sunset and dark.

words.tr:
v. 闪耀；闪烁
n. 闪烁
words.ex: The stars twinkle in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星在夜空中闪烁。
words.en: If a star or a light twinkles, it shines with an unsteady light that rapidly and gently changes from bright to faint.

chapters.name: 附录1 最常考专四词回顾 U

words.tr: adj. 最终的；最后的；极端的；
words.ex: This is the ultimate solution to the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这是这个问题的最终解决方案。
words.en: You use ultimate to describe the final result or aim of a long series of events.

words.ex: He opened his umbrella when it started to rain.
words.ex_cn: 天下雨时，他打开了伞。
words.en: An umbrella is a device consisting of a circular canopy of fabric on a folding metal frame, used as protection against rain or sunlight.

words.tr: adj. 无意识的；无知觉的；
words.ex: He was unconscious after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他失去了意识。
words.en: If someone is unconscious, they are not awake, usually because they have had a severe injury or illness.

words.ex: He had to undergo surgery last week.
